“Me?!”

“Yes, you. Is there anyone else that I could be speaking to in this room?”

“Are you sure, Miss Aglaea?”

Aglaea only chuckled, leaning back in her golden chair and propping an elbow on the armrest. “I am entrusting this to you, Phainon. Do not fail me now.”

Phainon, who was standing across her desk, fidgeted in place. Although he has been summoned many times into this room, he would still never become accustomed to its grandeur. Aglaea was the ruler of Okhema, after all. How could he not be intimidated? “It just sounds like a tall order for a normal guardsman like me, Miss Aglaea. I would just think it would be better to entrust this task to someone more worthy.”

“There is no one more worthy in my eyes than you, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.” Aglaea leaned forward in her chair, narrowing her eyes. “The ruler of Kremnos will be arriving today, and I want you to accompany him around Okhema. If we want the military might of their kingdom on our side, you will do well to accommodate the Kremnoans’ requests.”

Phainon paused with wandering eyes, absorbing the information that was just presented to him. “I… do not mean to be so forward, Miss Aglaea, but are you sure this task must be done by me? I am just a lowly guardsman from a lowly town out in the countryside that only serves to grow crops for the kingdom. I don't believe this task should fall into my hands. If anything, I believe someone of noble blood should be accompanying the ruler of Kremnos. Maybe your adoptive daughter, Cifera?”

“I have a keen eye for things,” Aglaea began, “And from what I have learned of their ruler, you are the best fit to escort them around our kingdom. And anyway, as Cifera is not my daughter of blood, you and she

would be the same. Do well to win over their ruler. I am trusting you as I always have, Phainon.”

Phainon could only bow before leaving the room, shutting the heavy metal door behind him with a deep sigh. As much as he tried to convince Aglaea, it was to no avail. It wasn't as if he had absolutely zero confidence in himself; he just thought it would be rude to allow someone of no noble birth to accompany a figure of noble birth. What was Aglaea thinking? And, what would the Kremnoans think if he were the one to come out and greet them?

Aglaea had provided him with the exact time the Kremnoans were arriving and where their lodgings would be within Marmoreal Palace. It was Phainon's duty to lead them around, ensure they were comfortable with their stay, and accommodate any requests that they may have while staying in Okhema.

Every couple of years, Okhema holds a grand ball, inviting various kingdoms to attend. It was a way for Okhema to gather with other political leaders and forge or strengthen current alliances. And every year, Kremnos has always politely declined those invitations. This year, however, Kremnos suddenly confirmed its attendance, and Aglaea has been scrambling to do her very best to impress the Kremnoans.

One of the more curious things was why the Kremnoans had decided to attend this year; it may be due to the fact that Kremnos had welcomed a new king a few years ago and has now decided to make a public appearance outside of their own kingdom. No one outside of Kremnos knew what this king looked like or what they were like in general, other than that their military might and prowess rivaled even previous generations of kings.

The festivities in Okhema would only last a week, but Phainon was currently preparing to have his head severed from his neck during this week escorting the Kremnoans. If their new leader was truly as fearsome as described in rumors, Phainon wasn't going to make it out of this week alive. Surely, the man was going to be large, burly, covered in scars, and with an intimidating aura, right? He probably had a look in his eyes that would make Phainon immediately fall to his knees. There were even rumors that

the current king killed the previous king with his own hands. If he were able to accomplish such a feat, what would stop him from also slaying some lowly soldier in Okhema?

Wait. Phainon faltered in his steps in the middle of whatever hallway he was currently in, on his way to the guards’ quarters adjacent to the palace. What were the Kremnoans’ values of etiquette and manners? How should he even greet them? For as long as he has been a soldier for Okhema, he has never once conversed with a Kremnoan.

chapters.html:
Kremnoans were described as bloodthirsty, foolhardy, and one-track minded. They were barbaric, bold, and greatly determined. If the general Kremnoan was described as such, he couldn't even begin to imagine their king–a king who had slain even his own father. If he greeted them incorrectly and in a non-Kremnoan fashion, would his head immediately roll from his shoulders? Phainon had actually originally wanted to request leave a few years ago to go training in Kremnos, but when news of the King’s death due to his son's hands had flooded the continent, that request immediately ceased. Surely, Aglaea had a better fit than Phainon to escort them around? Unless Aglaea actually viewed Phainon to be just like a Kremnoan and thought they would get along best? What had Aglaea learned about the current Kremnoan ruler that she had deemed Phainon to be the best fit as their guard?

Heaving another sigh, Phainon willed his feet to continue on to his quarters outside the palace. He had to prepare himself before greeting a king, after all–a king who was rumored to be the strongest in the entire continent of Amphoreus. It was why Aglaea was so intent on forging an alliance with the Kremnoans. With the Kremnoans on their side, almost nothing could breach Okhema’s borders.

Phainon grimaced to himself. The more he thought about it, the less he thought he would make it out of this week unscathed. Not only was this one of the most important political alliances for Okhema, but Aglaea just had to send some country boy to escort their king. Aglaea had always been intelligent and cunning, and it was why Phainon had always looked up to her as the ruler of Okhema. But, surely her head was not working properly today when she decided to assign Phainon this task? Although Aglaea trusted in him a lot more than the average Okheman soldier, and Phainon had done his very earnest to see all of her assignments through, Phainon had no faith he would return with good results this time.

Sunlight streamed into his face, rousing him from his own deprecating thoughts. He hadn't even realized that he made it to the entrance of Marmoreal Palace, and the palace guards had already opened the grand doors for him to exit. Nodding in their direction in thanks, Phainon stepped outside to begin preparations for the Kremnoans’ arrival. He didn't have long until they arrived, but he would do as best as he could.

In summary, Phainon had quite the morning. He had returned to his quarters and tidied himself up; he couldn't greet the Kremnoans with a disheveled appearance, after all. After a quick breakfast in the downtown market, he had returned to the palace to ensure their room arrangements were in order and that nothing was missing from the rooms. He instructed the maids to draw baths for when they arrive so that they would still be warm by the time they settled into their rooms. He visited the kitchen to review what dishes they were preparing for their stay and even had them accommodate any special food requests that they had included on their acceptance letter– one of which was pomegranate juice mixed with goat's milk. What a strange concoction, but Phainon couldn't knock it without trying it. Maybe it was a special Kremnoan delicacy. Phainon filed the beverage into the back of his mind to bring up later if he needed to keep the conversation flowing with them.

After running around Marmoreal Palace for hours, Phainon eventually collapsed onto a nearby bench in an unused drawing room in the palace. The Kremnoans would eventually be brought to this drawing room as it was the closest one to their temporary quarters; Phainon was just reviewing the area and ensuring nothing was out of place before bringing them in here once they arrived. Everything had to be meticulous, spotless, and perfect, so that Aglaea had no excuse if Phainon died at the hands of the Kremnoan king this week. Glancing down at his clothes, which was the common garb of a normal soldier and now disheveled again after running around the palace the entire morning, Phainon did his best to straighten and tidy his attire one last time before they arrived.

Although Aglaea had prepared for him special guard attire for fancy occasions in case he would ever guard high-profile figures, Phainon thought to save it for the ball instead. Wait, did Aglaea prepare that outfit just for this moment? Phainon had never had to accompany high-profile noble figures until now, yet that was the only reason Aglaea had given him that garb many moons ago.

Well, she had also given him the garb as her own way of promoting him, as the Council of Elders in Okhema always vetoed Aglaea's proposals for a “round table,”–a gathering of Okhema's best soldiers that would closely adhere and follow Aglaea's orders. Aglaea and the Council of Elders were always clashing heads in Okheman government, unfortunately, as the Council of Elders, who oversaw different government and political policies within Okhema, despised the way Aglaea ruled the kingdom. They feared that Aglaea would truly gain even more power if she had her own round table–one that would rival the Council of Elders. The only reason why Aglaea had not been overrun by their rule was because the priests of Janusopolis were backing her, and there was no kingdom that didn't follow the words of the priests–except for maybe the Grove of Epiphany, who valued intelligence and logic above all else. Phainon knew Aglaea was scheming in her own way to combat the Council of Elders, and he knew he would be called upon whenever those plans were ready.

It was approaching the middle of Action Hour which was when they had signalled their arrival. Phainon had done the best he could to scrub off any debris or wrinkles he could catch in his clothes. With another deep sigh escaping his body, Phainon prepared himself for the worst as he shut the drawing room doors behind him to find the entrance of the palace.

Marmoreal Palace was in utter chaos–as it always was around the time of festivities. Grand, high-profile guests traveled from all across Amphoreus to attend the festivities, and it was the palace staff who had to deal with them and accommodate as many of their ridiculous requests as possible. Members of Janusopolis, the Grove of Epiphany, and Styxia always came for the festivities, but now the entire palace was erupting over the fact that Kremnos was actually joining this year. The palace staff already knew how to handle the other three kingdoms but was unsure how Kremnos would come into play. Phainon couldn't blame them at all–he was already counting down his days, after all. And it was Phainon who had to deal the most with the Kremnoans as their personal guard during their stay.

Phainon passed a multitude of rushing attendants as he made his way to the palace entrance–so many that he had begun to lose count of how many things he had to catch out of their arms as they dashed past him like mad in the corridors. The maids and butlers carried a wide assortment in their arms such as towels, books, ingredients, bedsheets, decorations, and many more things as they prepared for everyone's arrival.

Phainon was attending to Kremnos; he wondered who was attending to the other kingdoms that were arriving? He hadn't had time at all today to converse with anyone except for Aglaea this morning and the guard from even earlier who had interrupted his morning exercise to inform him that Aglaea was looking for him.

Reaching the grand garden that made up the entrance of Marmoreal Palace, there were only a few moments left until the Kremnoans would arrive. Heart pounding and hands sweating under the bright sunlight in anticipation for their arrival, Phainon decided to distract himself from his anxiousness by conversing with the other attendants waiting for the Kremnoans outside as well.

“Phainon!” One of the maids greeted him as he approached her. “I heard you were tasked with accompanying the Kremnoan ambassadors.”

Phainon nodded in confirmation. “Miss Aglaea informed me this morning. Truly a surprise to begin the day.”

“Miss Aglaea has never been wrong–if she tasked you with handling them, then you are surely our best bet.”

“Maybe it is because you are strong?” A nearby butler chimed in. “I've heard the Kremnoans value strength above all else. As our strongest warrior in Okhema, surely they would value your company over any other guard here.”

Phainon laughed lightly. It seemed no one knew anything about the Kremnoans outside of rumors. “I don't think I can compare to their king.”

“Nonsense, Phainon!” A range of voices burst at him. “Everyone knows how strong you are!”

The people began chatting about Phainon's heroic deeds ever since he joined the ranks of Okhema's soldiers many, many years ago. Frankly, Phainon didn't think he deserved all this praise. He was only completing what was tasked to him. There was nothing particularly special about that. There was nothing particularly special about him. He was just an average, Okheman citizen, who left his small hometown behind to become strong and help as many people as possible.

Among the chattering of all the servants came the sound of carriages being pulled into the garden. Everyone's conversations completely ceased as they scrambled back to their originally assigned positions to await the Kremnoan ambassadors. Phainon stepped up the stairs leading to the grandiose doors of Marmoreal Palace to watch as the first carriage pulled into place. The only sounds he could hear now were the faint rustling of the plants in the garden and his own pounding heartbeat. He would be one of the first people outside of Kremnos to ever witness their new king.

One of the Okheman attendants pulled open the door of the carriage, but Phainon was too far to see who had stepped out of the carriage. Traditionally speaking, royalty is often seated in the last carriage for protection purposes, so he didn't expect the King to be in the first carriage anyway. That was Phainon's initial thought, until the individual in the carriage was fully soaked in the sunlight.

With how elaborately dressed the first man to emerge was, Phainon could only assume that was the King himself. With glistening gold armor adorning his forearms and hands along with matching gold greaves, this man basically radiated the color of a gleaming, golden sun. With how soft and malleable the metal gold actually was, Phainon could easily tell this armor was only meant for royalty to be used as attire rather than actual protective gear. It was a way to portray both strength on the battlefield and noble blood, and only the King or others of the noble family would wear golden armor.

An equally gold necklace adorned with blue gemstones lay across his bare chest, and a large golden belt lay across his hips. The only other color this man seemed to wear was a bright crimson, with a heavy, velvet cloak draped over one shoulder and lined with gold accents. Golden clasps kept the cloak on his shoulder, with a grand golden brooch sitting on one side; Phainon could only assume it marked the noble family of Kremnos. A single, gold pauldron was strapped to one shoulder and a matching golden band adorned his bare bicep, with golden hair falling down his shoulders. Phainon was too far to assess the man's face, but what really shocked him were the bright red lines running across his body wherever he could see skin.

Phainon squinted, unsure if he was seeing correctly or if the sunlight really was just that bright. Why was he half-naked? The only thing on his torso was a single sash that indicated royalty draped diagonally across his body, but it didn't look like he wore an actual shirt. He wasn't sure if the sunlight was just playing tricks on his sight. But, what was most interesting was that this man did not wear a crown despite being king. Although Aglaea was the ruler of Okhema, she was not technically a queen, as much of the government was also run by the Council of Elders. Kremnos, on the other hand, truly held a monarchy, yet no crown adorned this man's head. But, with all the golden armor and jewelry, Phainon didn't think anyone else stepping out of subsequent carriages would be the King.

And, he was right. One by one, as all the carriages lined up and doors were opened by attendants, no one that stepped out was dressed nearly as extravagantly as the first man. Not only was he the first one to appear, but he was also half-naked and wore no crown. Phainon was adding these mental notes into his head about Kremnoans, hoping he wouldn't offend him in the future with any accidentally offensive remarks. He needed to know as much about them as possible to appease them during their stay and to keep his head.

While he watched the attendants greet the Kremnoan ambassadors down below, Phainon straightened his back, preparing to greet the Kremnoans himself. The butlers and maids scrambled around down below to take their luggages and coats as the new guests made their way up the stairs.

With a smile, Phainon greeted them as he finally came face to face with the man they called King. Contrary to his prior expectations, their king was absolutely, objectively beautiful. He was expecting a rugged, scarred man, but the King in front of him was completely unblemished with soft plump lips, a sharp jawline, and the most intimidatingingly gorgeous eyes. To one side of his hair, the front pieces were gathered together in a braid, ending in a golden cuff that held the braid together, yet the rest of his hair was untamed. He resembled a graceful, but wild, lion. That was the best way Phainon could describe his man's features. One could clearly tell this man was born of royal blood with the way he carried himself with such poise and elegance, yet confidence, intimidation, and strength.

“It is a pleasure to meet you.” Phainon smiled at this intimidatingly gorgeous man in front of him as his attendants stopped a little ways behind him. He still couldn't believe how objectively good-looking the King was. “My name is Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, and I will be your guard in Okhema during your stay.”

The King assessed him with eyes blatantly scanning his person. While being evaluated under keen, golden eyes, Phainon also noticed that the King did not wear a sword or any type of blade on his body. What did this king fight with without a single weapon on his person?

“Phainon,” the King repeated his name and, woah, the King's voice was deep. It was deep, but his voice was smooth, matching his elegantly intimidating aura. “I assume that you are Okhema's best warrior if they are sending you to accompany my side.”

That really was why Aglaea assigned Phainon to the Kremnoans?!

Phainon couldn't help perspiring under the King's intense gaze. But, with a slightly restrained smile, Phainon managed to respond, “I wouldn't possibly be your match, Your Majesty.”

The King hummed, assessing Phainon's build once more. “Do you take on sparring partners?”

“Pardon?”

“I asked if you train your swings against a person or a dummy, seeing as you have a sword strapped to your side.”

“Ah.” Phainon's hand instinctively reached for his greatsword. It was his most prized possession, Dawnmaker. He had gotten it forged by one of Okhema's greatest blacksmiths after a few years of working with Aglaea. “I would like to have a sparring partner; unfortunately, there is never a soul who would like to spar against me.”

Phainon's eyes couldn't help dropping to his lips when the King smirked at his response. Raising a chin at Phainon, the King said, “Show me to your training grounds. Let us fight.”

“Pardon?!” Phainon blinked blankly at the King, forgetting that he was supposed to be treating him like royalty.

“Is that all you ever say, Phainon?” the King chuckled, crossing his arms across his broad chest. “You said you wanted a sparring partner. Then, let us spar.”

Phainon was flabbergasted. After a long and arduous journey of travelling to a foreign country that they have never visited before, the first thing the King wanted to do was fight?

“I.. Well…” Phainon wasn't even sure how to respond. Firstly, the maids were already preparing their rooms to rest as they were speaking. Secondly, how would it be possible for someone as lowly as Phainon to exchange blows with a king? And thirdly, what if the King actually got injured?

Wait, maybe Phainon already failed their test, and he was being brought to the training grounds so they can spill his blood in a more private area?!

With a sheepish smile, Phainon could only say, “I am not sure if it is proper for me to exchange blows with you, Your Majesty.”

The King furrowed his eyebrows. “Not proper?”

“I am… I am just a common guard, Your Majesty. It wouldn't be proper to exchange blows with me. If you would like, I can call a knight of noble birth to–”

“What nonsense are you spouting?” the King scoffed. “Clearly, if there was a knight stronger than you, they would have sent them to accompany me instead. If they decided to send you, then there is no other warrior as strong as you within these borders.”

Phainon hesitated, unsure what the proper response was next. It wasn't as if he could just throw hands with the King of Kremnos, right? He couldn't even begin to imagine the Council of Elders walking in on him getting absolutely pummeled by the visiting king.

“I apologize, Your Majesty.” Phainon could only bow his head. “I am not sure if I am allowed.”

“Even if it is the request of the Kremnoan king?”

Phainon paused, his body growing rigid. Aglaea did task him with accommodating any and all requests that they had while they were here. Would fighting the King fall under that assignment? Phainon's head was a giant, jumbled mess, contemplating whether he should really throw it down against their king or not. It wasn't as if Phainon would actually win against the King, but it wasn't as if Phainon could just agree and say, “Sure, let's fight!”

He heard a sigh above him, as Phainon was still mid-bow. “We, Kremnoans, do not believe in anything such as noble birth or noble standing. Even if we are run by a king, the only importance that we hold is that strength is power. It does not matter to me whether you are a king or whether you are from a small, unknown town. What matters is how well you can wield your weapon and how well you can best your opponents.”

“I see.” Phainon stood himself back upright after his words, determination brimming off his eyes. There was no other excuse Phainon could use to deter this battle. If the Kremnoan king wanted to fight, then Phainon was going to give him one. “Then, you would like to spar with me?”

With his smirk returning to his lips, it almost seemed as if the King's eyes began to brightly glow. “Let us fight, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.”

The King had one of his attendants take his velvet cloak and sash, revealing more of his bare torso to Phainon's eyes. Phainon, with wandering eyes, forcefully tore his gaze away and informed a nearby maid that they still had time to prepare their rooms. The maid rushed off in a hurry to relay the news.

He led them to the training grounds and completely skipped the drawing room and their temporary quarters. This wasn't exactly what Phainon had in mind for their arrival, but he had to do what was best to accommodate them, right? Though, Phainon did his best to give them a tour of the areas around them that they passed on the way to the training grounds.

There were training grounds within Marmoreal Palace, which was where Phainon usually completed his training. Most soldiers used the training grounds near their quarters, but it was much smaller and more crowded. Aglaea had granted him and a few others special permission to use the royal palace's training grounds. Those few others were most likely escorting the other ambassadors from the different kingdoms that were visiting Okhema for the festivities.

Pushing open the doors to the vast training grounds, Phainon and the Kremnoans stepped back outside. It was a completely open training ground, with wooden weapons organised in one corner, and practice dummies and targets in another corner. The training grounds were completely customizable so that whoever was training could tailor to their own needs. Phainon was usually the only one who could be found here, as the others never trained as much as Phainon did, so the training grounds were almost always tailored to him.

He spared a glance at the King, who was nodding and taking in the sights. It seemed the training grounds were to his taste, much to Phainon's relief. He wasn't sure what kind of training grounds they had in Kremnos, where all they did was battle according to the rumors, but he was glad the King was at least satisfied with where he was brought to.

Phainon gently leaned Dawnmaker against the wall near the wooden sparring swords, grabbing one of the spare swords and approaching the center of the training grounds. the King followed soon after, with his attendants watching from the sidelines. Phainon had never had such a large audience before while training, and he was getting a little nervous over their peering eyes. The King, on the other hand, seemed more interested in the sparring partner in front of him.

“Are you ready, Your Majesty?” Phainon was rolling his shoulders and loosening up the tension in his body. He was so nervous over meeting the Kremnoans the entire first half of the day, but so far, the King was treating him with nothing but kindness. He was expecting the Kremnoan king to be brute and brash with all the rumors surrounding him, but he was pleasantly surprised that he was proven otherwise. It definitely helped relieve much of the tension in Phainon's body.

Narrowing his eyes at Phainon, the King flexed his wrist, and Phainon’s gaze immediately dropped to his hands at the action. Wait, did the Kremnoan king fight with his hands?! Was the King actually going to throw hands at him?! Was that why Phainon couldn't find a single weapon on his person?

“Mydeimos is my name.” The King's voice interrupted his thoughts. “No need for formalities.”

Okay, the tension immediately returned to Phainon's body. He wanted Phainon to address him by first name? Sure, he did that with Aglaea quite often, but he still added a “Miss” to the front of her name as a form of respect. And, he also knew and worked with Aglaea frequently. Calling an actual monarch that he had just met by his first name just didn't sit well with Phainon–someone who had a humble upbringing.

“I'm… afraid I cannot do that, Your Majesty.” Phainon breathed a laugh, readying his stance. Hopefully, the King didn't take too much offense.

Raising an eyebrow, the King also assumed a battle stance. He muttered under his breath, “Okhemans and their unnecessary formalities,” before declaring with a booming voice, “Then, if I win, call me Mydeimos.”

Phainon's eyes widened in response. But before he could respond back, the King rushed him, throwing a fist upward in an uppercut and aiming for his abdomen. Phainon could barely pull his feet backwards as he felt the wind brush against his tunic. If he had thrown his sword up to block the blow, it would have shattered into a million wood pieces.

Stumbling to catch his feet, Phainon barely had time to breathe when another fist came his way. Bracing his sword, he swung to his right, effectively blocking the blow, before jabbing straight into the King's shoulder. Although he did manage to mark the King, he wasn't sure how he was possibly going to win this. The King's defenses were quite strong, and he didn't see anywhere he could pierce through, even with his half-naked body.

The King smirked–possibly from the thrill of the battle or possibly from being scratched. Barely brushing a hand against his shoulder as if a speck of dust had landed on him, he lunged again, aiming for Phainon's shoulder as if seeking revenge. Phainon quickly brought the sword up to his shoulder, but the breath was knocked out of him when the King's other hand landed against his exposed shoulder.

Phainon gritted his teeth, slicing upwards when the King had approached him one more time in an attempt to follow up. His shoulder was throbbing, but it didn't matter if he could still stand. His sword had barely brushed the chin of the King, rushing through his golden and red hair. Tossing the hilt in his grasp, he turned his blade sideways to aim straight for his neck, but his wrist was caught by the King's own grasp.

The two were caught in a standstill, their eyes narrowed at each other and panting for breath. Adrenaline was pumping through Phainon's body–he had never felt such a rush in battle in a long time. It had been a while since he had ever sparred against an actual human rather than the monsters that occasionally showed up at Okhema’s borders, and it was exciting. No, even more than that; it was exhilarating. His heart was pounding, blood was pumping through his veins, and he couldn’t wipe the smile off his face as he stared at the man in front of him, completely forgetting how different their social statuses were. At that moment, they were bound by nothing but their own skills on the battlefield.

“Impressive.”

Phainon had barely registered those words before he threw his head back, dodging another fist. Seriously, why did it feel like this man had three hands? Ripping his hand from the tight grasp around his wrist, he tried to slice again, only to be effectively blocked by the King’s golden vambrace. Phainon decided to aim lower, aiming for his side that wasn’t blocked, but the King sidestepped as he attempted another slash.

He took advantage of this dodge, pushing forward and advancing toward him. This entire time, he had been playing on the defense, but now he was able to turn the tide. Phainon leaped forward, slashing a large arc downward and creating a wall of space between him in the King, before quickly stepping forward and swinging sideways, landing a hit on the man’s chest. He faintly heard a laugh, but he wasn’t sure if it was coming from him or the man he was sparring against. Continuing his advances with large swings, he aimed at the man’s shoulders, waist, and arms, and all were continually blocked by the man’s gauntlets.

With how wide his swings were, Phainon had managed to back the King into the wall and not let him escape, realizing that he may actually stand a chance to win this fight. Should he win this fight? Against a king? A slight hesitation from that thought left Phainon vulnerable, and before he could decide, he ended up tumbling to the floor.

His entire body ached as he pushed himself up, dust and debris flying through the air from when he had flown straight into the ground. Through the dust clouds, he could barely make out the King, who looked less than pleased that he had won.

“You,” the King growled, chest heaving from the fight, “You let me win that. Stand up. Again.”

Phainon quickly scurried to his feet as the King approached him. It didn’t help that his whole body throbbed from sliding into the floor, but it didn’t look like the King was going to back down anytime soon, especially since he despised the victory that Phainon had given him.

The Kremnoan attendants watched as Phainon and their king swung at each other for the remainder of the day, counting twenty battles and each individual winning exactly ten. It wasn’t until a maid had found Phainon after much effort and informed him that dinner was ready did they finally stop sparring, much to the attendants’ relief. Once their king got absorbed with a good opponent, it was nearly impossible to rip the man away.

However, they all agreed that it was quite a sight to behold, seeing how an ordinary soldier of Okhema was equally matched with their king. It was a battle like any other to the Kremnoans, as they all had watched the entire battle from beginning to end with sparkling eyes.

Phainon breathed a sigh as he dipped into his bath. The bath that he used was shared by all the soldiers, but no one was there as it had become so late in the night. He had no idea how time had passed so fast while sparring with the King, but the sensations of the battle and the rushing of adrenaline were still fresh in his mind. It was a feeling that he would never forget, and he spent the rest of his bath relaying the entire twenty sparring sessions in his mind. Not necessarily to lament over actions he should have done, but he was simply admiring their entire exchange.

Dressed back in the soldier’s uniform, it was time to pick up the Kremnoan guests from the dinner table. Phainon had a quick bite to eat before his bath, as it was rude to dine with royalty without a proper, explicit invitation. He had merely dropped them off in the dining room before quickly fleeing, explaining that he would return after their meal was complete. He didn’t hear what the Kremnoans had to say about that, but knowing the King, if he had opinions, he would hear them upon his return.

And, Phainon was completely correct. Upon entering the dining room again and laying eyes upon the Kremnoans, the King did not look pleased. In fact, much to Phainon’s panic, the King looked extremely angry.

“Yes, Your Majesty?” Phainon hesitantly approached the table, standing across from the King’s fury, who sent a sharp glare in his direction. The butlers and maids had quickly escaped the room the moment Phainon had entered, leaving the entire aftermath to him. “Did you not find the food palatable?”

“Why did you leave?”

Phainon blinked at him. “Pardon?”

The King leaned back into his chair, the fire only growing in his eyes. “HKS, how do I make you call me by name? You seemed to be treating me as an equal during our sparring sessions, so why can you not do that here?”

Phainon was speechless. He wasn’t exactly sure what to say. And, he had no idea what the King had just called him. Sure, Phainon agreed that he was sparring with the King just as if he were another soldier during the heat of battle, but they weren’t on the training grounds anymore. They were back inside the palace–a foreign king being accompanied by the country’s soldier. He was just one of many soldiers. Should he apologize? It didn’t look like the King would want an apology.

“In Okhema…it is quite rude for a commoner to be on equal standing as the nobility,” Phainon explained. “I apologize if that made you uncomfortable in any way.”

The King narrowed his eyes. “Even someone with skills as fine as yours?”

He laughed lightly. “One’s birthplace is never forgotten in Okhema’s borders. It is stuck to our name like glue.”

The King clicked his tongue. “Aedes Elysiae… How annoying. You would thrive so much better in Kremnos.” He pushed himself up, and the attendants next to him followed suit. “Phainon, as I am a Kremnoan, you will do well to follow Kremnoan traditions rather than your own.”

Phainon nodded. It felt almost like he was being reprimanded like a child.

“Next time,” the King’s voice cut through his thoughts, “call me Mydeimos. And, join us when we are eating. You are more than just skilled–you are the most worthy opponent that I have ever enjoyed the opportunity of facing in years. You more than deserve my company, and I would like to meet again with the man I had sparred with earlier today. Because the man in front of me right now is different from the man I faced in the training grounds.”

Phainon quickly scanned the attendants’ expressions to gauge what they were feeling about the King’s orders, but they didn’t seem the least surprised at all. Kremnoan traditions truly felt like whiplash to Phainon.

With a laugh, Phainon nodded once again, his shoulders relaxing. He hadn’t even realized how tensed he was before. “Of course, Mydeimos. As you wish.”

A smile graced the King’s lips at his words, and Phainon swore his heart pounded at the sight of it. Truly, he was the most objectively beautiful person that he had ever laid eyes on. The number of concubines this man had was probably in the hundreds. It was common for monarchs to have concubines, right? Phainon wasn’t exactly sure, considering that Kremnoan tradition was so much different compared to what he had known his whole life. Though, if he did have a concubine, or two, one of them would be accompanying him. And, none of the attendants were close enough to the King to appear as his concubine. But, there was absolutely no way a man as beautiful as Mydeimos was single; Phainon refused to believe it.

Phainon led the King and his attendants to their private quarters, where they were finally able to relax after their long journey to Okhema. Before Phainon had taken his own bath, he had instructed the maids to reheat their baths so that they would still be warm by the time they finished their dinner. They had spent basically their entire day in the training grounds; truly, the rumors of Kremnoans living for battle were true enough. Phainon would have never imagined being asked to spar with the King within their first exchange of words.

“Then, I will be returning tomorrow. Tomorrow, our ruler, Miss Aglaea, would like to speak with you. You will have the entire trip here in Okhema to think over her proposal, if that is suitable enough for you,” Phainon explained to the King. The King had his arms crossed across his chest, and he was leaning against the open door frame of his room while Phainon discussed tomorrow’s plans. The attendants had already retired for the day in separate rooms; they most likely did not have nearly as much stamina as the King, who not only endured the entire journey to Okhema from Kremnos but also immediately engaged in twenty duels upon entering Okhema’s borders.

Mydeimos fell silent, processing the information. “Yes, that is why I came here after all.” The King became deep in thought, seeming to mull over different political impacts and strategies in his mind. It must be quite complicated to rule a kingdom.

“Then.” Phainon nodded. “Good night, Mydeimos.”

The King, who was too busy lost in his thoughts over his own kingdom, glanced up at Phainon’s voice. “Tomorrow, I expect to be treated like your equal, rather than the King that you have seen me as all day.”

Phainon really, really could not help how loud the pounding of his heart had become. Seriously, did this man just naturally sound like he was flirting at every possible moment? It didn’t help that the King had such a seriously gorgeous complexion. With a laugh, Phainon could only respond with burning ears, “I will try my best, Mydeimos.”

With a smile, Mydeimos retired for the night, and Phainon was left falling asleep with the searing image of his smile in his mind.

chapters.title: Itinerary Day 2: Aglaea's Proposal
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I actually struggled so bad trying to find Okheman food to include in this fanfic thank god the Chrysos Maze Grand Restaurant event released when I was writing later chapters LOL

Or else they were literally going to be eating Golden Honeycakes forever... which I guess Mydei wouldn't complain about

Bright and early the following day, Phainon left the soldier's quarters and knocked on the attendants’ doors. He wasn't sure if it was rude of him to report directly to the King, so he reported to the attendants first.

One of them opened the door for him, and Phainon faintly remembered from their initial meeting that his name was Herklas. Phainon greeted him with a smile. “I have come to retrieve you all for breakfast. Has your king risen?”

Herklas stared at him with mild surprise. “I'm surprised you didn't go see him first.”

“Pardon?”

“The King will be quite sad that you came to talk to us about him rather than talking to him directly.”

With an expression of bewilderment, Phainon lightly laughed. “I don't think the King would be so sad about that.”

He cocked his head to the side, leaning on the door. “This is quite possibly the first time the King has ever taken such a liking to someone else. You should listen to him.”

“Surely… the King doesn't like me as much as you say.” Phainon sheepishly scratched the back of his head at the thought. He didn't

particularly think he received special treatment from the King during the previous day.

“It's true.” Another attendant–Phainon recalled her name was Empousa– showed up at the door. “King Mydeimos has never shown such favoritism to anyone before.”

Phainon frowned. “What favoritism, might I ask? He just genuinely seems like a polite man.”

The two attendants exchanged a look before glancing back at Phainon, with one of them responding, “King Mydeimos is surely a benevolent and strong ruler, and we all admire and look up to him. But he does not normally treat his subjects the way he treats you: the way he asks you to share meals with him, spar with him, and treats you as his equal. King Mydeimos knows his place as the King of Kremnos, but he seems to treat you with extra special attention, even forgoing his title of king to converse with you as equals.”

“That's… not normal for him?” Phainon was just as surprised as the attendants were yesterday, according to them. Their poker faces were truly magnificent; Phainon had been gauging their expressions all day yesterday to see if the King's actions were normal, and they acted as if they were. Now, Phainon was finally learning that they were in fact not normal.

Empousa shook her head. “Krateros is surely going to have a fit over this.”

Herklas, who was leaning against the door, widened his eyes at the statement. “Krateros is going to throw a table if he hears about this.”

“Krateros?”

The two attendants’ attention snapped back to Phainon. One of them replied, “Krateros is King Mydeimos’s teacher. You could also say he is his closest confidante. He is currently watching over Kremnos while we are away.”

Herklas continued, raising his head. “Krateros has been trying to find a suitable partner for the King for years now. Who knew that partner would

be residing in a different kingdom?”

Phainon's brain immediately did a backflip. “Wait, excuse me, partner? The King doesn't have a partner?”

Empousa laughed. “Surprising, isn't it? Kremnoans treasure the bond that is forged between lovers, as it is one of the strongest things a human can have. But, it has been years since King Mydeimos took the throne, and he has never once found a lover. Krateros has been in a fiery determination to find him a suitable partner and set him up but to no avail.”

“He seems to have taken a liking to you though.” Herklas leaned his head back against the door. “Who knows, maybe you will end up returning with us to Kremnos by the end of the week.”

With a burning face, Phainon wasn't sure how to respond to that statement. “There's… The King doesn't like me in that manner.”

Herklas scoffed. “Are you going to believe yourself, who has only known him for a day, or us, who have known him almost our entire lives?”

Jabbing him in the side with her elbow, Empousa sighed. “Although we do not know the King's true feelings, what we do know is that he has taken a very specific liking to you, Phainon. A very special liking.”

Her words only made Phainon burn even more. A very special liking…

“Done with your rambling?”

All three of the heads immediately turned in the direction of Mydeimos, who was already dressed and standing outside his bedroom door. The two attendants hurriedly jumped back into their room to prepare themselves for the day.

“Mydeimos.” Phainon smiled at him, mentally clapping himself on the back for remembering to call him by name. How long was he standing there? And, how much of the conversation did he hear? “Did you have a good rest?”

The King stared at him with a blank gaze. Phainon wasn't sure what exactly on his person the King was so intensely looking at, as he was wearing the exact same garb as when they had first met.

“The way you talk to my attendants.” Mydeimos glanced at the door adjacent to Phainon, which was now closed shut as the attendants inside rushed to get ready. “Speak to me how you speak to them.”

Phainon stared back at Mydeimos with wide eyes. “With… such casualty?”

“Is that so wrong?” Mydeimos returned his stare.

“Well… No, but,” Phainon couldn't help stammering at the sudden request. “It will… take me some time to become accustomed to.”

“That is of no matter. We have time. Didn't you say you would try your best?”

Last night's conversation flashed in Phainon's mind and the verbal promise that he had given the King. With a light chuckle, Phainon nodded. “Yes, of course I remember, Mydeimos.”

“And next time, report to me instead of my attendants.”

Phainon smiled. “I will do that, Mydeimos.”

The attendants opened the door again, and before they could shut the door behind them, Phainon could see how much of a whirlwind their room had become in the process of rushing to get ready. The maids will certainly have a trip attending to that mess later.

Once all the attendants in the other rooms were ready, he led them down to the dining room where they ate their dinner the previous night. As they were settling in their seats, the King gave Phainon a look, and Phainon knew what he was referring to.

“May I sit across from you, Mydeimos?”

“Hmph, you don't need to ask.”

With a laugh, Phainon settled in the seat across from the King. Sitting across from the King and being able to fully appreciate his radiance… Phainon could easily see why anyone would worship and follow this man as their king.

The chefs brought out their breakfast on shining silver dinnerware. Silver dinnerware was always used, especially for those of higher ranking, to detect any poisons that may be in the dish itself. It was a form of trust to indulge in someone else's cooking, and for the palace, it was a form of trust to pass their dishes onward on a silver platter for their guests.

The dish that was brought out for breakfast was a classic Okheman delicacy. Although it was originally a dish reserved for royalty, it has now become a popular favorite among the masses with how fluffy and sweet it was. The dish was named Golden Honeycakes. With a self-explanatory name, the honeycakes were served in stacks, with a sweet, viscous syrup oozing down the sides. Shining under the lights, the syrup only made the fluffy honeycakes look even more enticing. And with an addition of berries scattered among the plates, the sourness balanced out the sweetness of the syrup.

Butter was served separately, so the guests can indulge in as much of as little as they would like. The table was set with utensils, napkins, silver creamers containing even more of that delicious syrup, and sugar bowls in case the guests would like to add powdered sugar on top of their honeycakes. Bowls of fresh berries could also be found around the table in case the guests would like to add more, and pitchers of some sort of pink milk were set on the table. Was that the pomegranate juice mixed with milk that Phainon saw before as their special food request?

Phainon didn't think about this before when he was told to dine with the Kremnos guests, but he didn't know the first thing about dinner etiquette or what good table manners consisted of. He only had brief lessons from when he first became a soldier, but that was years ago. As someone whose main job was to guard or fight, and as someone who was born and raised in the countryside by farmers, he had no need to know how to properly eat at the table. Digging through his brain for those few lessons he received, Phainon decided to just eat as little as possible so as to not appear rude or unbecoming in front of the guests. Later, Phainon could return to the kitchen and find something else to eat to satiate his appetite.

The Kremnoans indulged delightfully in silence in front of him; while scarcely picking at his food, Phainon eyed them every now and then just to ensure that no one needed assistance with anything or a request they needed tending to. But overall, they seemed to be happily enjoying the food, much to Phainon's relief.

“Is this dish not to your liking?”

Phainon glanced upward at the voice directed at him and was met with golden eyes. Based on the state of his plate, it seemed that the King thoroughly enjoyed the dish set before him.

It seemed Phainon couldn't get away with anything in front of this man. He set down the silver utensils in his hands with a smile, his Golden Honeycakes barely touched. “No, I am just not particularly hungry today.”

Mydeimos hummed, glancing down at his plate at the few remains that were left. “This dish is truly worthy of my attention.”

Phainon laughed lightly. “I'm glad you enjoyed it. It's a popular local delicacy of Okhema.”

Humming, Mydeimos agreed. “I can see why.”

One of the Kremnos attendants poured the King a glass of the pink milk. Even though the attendant was in the middle of explaining to the King that he had already tasted the milk, Mydeimos had already taken a mighty swig from his glass. It was like absolutely nothing could kill this man, and this man was not afraid of anything either.

“I saw your special food request.” Phainon nodded in the direction of the glass in Mydeimos’s hand. “Is pomegranate juice and milk a common beverage in Kremnos?”

The attendants all looked puzzled at his statement, with one of them opening their mouth to answer his question: “The King just happens to enjoy it himself. It's weird.”

The attendants all nodded and muttered amongst themselves in agreement. Phainon was shocked that they so blatantly knocked their king's choice of drink, but the man in question didn't seem to pay them any mind as he continued drinking his glass full of pomegranate juice milk.

“It's common in Kremnos culture to drink pomegranate juice,” the female attendant that Phainon was speaking to earlier, Empousa, chimed in. “To us, it is named sanguine honey brew. As a way of forging alliances, we will share a chalice of blood among our new allies. That ‘blood’ would be pomegranate juice.”

Phainon has heard that tradition before, where Kremnos would sustain their bodies with blood, and it was also believed that, by drinking the blood of powerful enemies, they would be granted the valiance of the deceased. Although Phainon didn't know if those rumors were true or not, now he knew that they were drinking pomegranate juice the entire time.

“So, Mydeimos,” Phainon smiled in his direction, “do you just prefer the taste of goat's milk and mix it in with pomegranate juice?”

Mydeimos set down his glass. “I prefer the color.”

That answer made him pause. Tilting his head to one side, Phainon asked, “Pink?”

Swirling the glass, Mydeimos gently smiled. “It is quite a pleasant color.”

Phainon was surprised at how gentle his smile was. This intimidating man, known as probably the most powerful person on the entire continent of Amphoreus, was smiling so gently over the color of his beverage. With his softened golden eyes and his soft lips upturned into a smile, Phainon felt as if he were mesmerized by the sight of the man before him; he almost wanted to reach out to brush his hand across his cheek, even swiping a thumb along his lips that were shimmering from the syrup from the Golden Honeycakes that he had just enjoyed.

As much as Phainon wanted to continue staring at the King as he admired the color of his glass, he knew it was time for his meeting with Aglaea. Swallowing dryly and pushing all those indecent thoughts about the King away, he stood from his table and instructed the maids waiting nearby to clear the rest of the dining table. Phainon even added an extra instruction to save his own dish in some corner of the kitchen so that he could indulge in it later. Receiving his request, the maids quickly went to work while one of them had carefully taken Phainon's plate away separately.

Only two attendants continued on with the King while the rest were escorted away by other soldiers. As the King was meeting with Aglaea, he didn't need all of his attendants there, so the remainder of them would have the freedom to do whatever they would like around Marmoreal Palace or around Okhema with the protection of the other guards. Phainon led the King and two of his attendants to Aglaea’s personal office, where Phainon was previously given this task of being the Kremnoan's escort during their temporary stay in Okhema.

“Miss Aglaea will let me know when to come get you, so for now, I will inform her of your arrival.” Before Phainon could disappear into her office to speak with her, the King's voice cut him off.

“You do not need to worry about manners around me.” the King's gaze bore straight into Phainon. “As I said before, we are equals. No need to treat me as if I would break.”

Phainon stared at him with wide eyes. “I apologize, where is this coming from?”

“I saw you ask the maid to take your plate away separately. Were you afraid of eating improperly in front of me?”

Pausing for a brief moment, Phainon laughed at his words. “You caught me, Mydeimos. Truly, nothing can get past you.”

Mydeimos huffed, but he didn't seem the least bit angry. “Just eat your food next time. Did you think I invited you to the table just to ridicule your table manners?”

Phainon chuckled. “I just didn't want to offend.”

“You would never offend me, Phainon.”

Seriously, can this guy stop with all of these flirtatious statements? Phainon was afraid he was going to get the wrong idea at this point. It was barely the second day of meeting the King of Kremnos, but the amount of times his heart had beat so loudly in his ears over what the King had said to him was more than in his entire lifetime. The way Mydeimos so plainly stated his feelings as if they were a fact was something that always made Phainon's ears burn.

“Then,” Phainon tried to avert his gaze from the man as his ears were so obviously as red as Mydeimos's cloak. “I will let Aglaea know you have arrived.

Raising a fist, he knocked on the door. Once he heard Aglaea’s voice, he let in the King and his two attendants.

“Then, I will see you all later.” Phainon smiled before shutting the door behind him.

“Thank you, Phainon.” Aglaea returned the smile as Phainon disappeared behind the closed door. Glancing at the King who took the seat that was prepared in front of her desk, she placed down the scroll that she was previously reading.

“King Mydeimos, what an honor to finally meet you. I was quite surprised when I received news that you would be attending the grand ball this year.” Aglaea leisurely rested a chin in the palm of her hand as her elbow rested on top of her mahogany desk. “Would you like some tea? I have prepared Okhema's finest in preparation for your arrival.” Aglaea waved a hand toward the maid who was standing in a corner of the room. Nodding, she quickly wheeled her cart over, pouring the King some tea in a delicate, ceramic tea cup.

“It's an honor to still be welcomed after declining your invitations so many times previously,” Mydeimos said as one of his attendants took the tea from the maid's hands. “Now that things have settled in my kingdom, I thought it was time to make my public debut to the other kingdoms.”

Aglaea nodded in understanding. “How do you like the guard I sent you? I couldn't find much information about you, but I felt that Phainon would be the best fit to show you around our country.”

“His growth has stagnated by being here.” Mydeimos wasted no time in revealing his true thoughts. He took a sip of tea from the tea cup his attendant returned to him. “He has a great potential that this kingdom is not taking advantage of.”

The smile on Aglaea's face only grew as she stirred her own cup of tea on her desk. “I am so glad we are of the same, King Mydeimos. That is the reason why I have brought you here today. Phainon is someone who deserves more than what is given to him, but I need some help.”

“Speak, why are you delaying this?”

Aglaea, unbothered by his comment, brought out the scroll that she was holding, detailing the Okheman government. “I cannot do this alone, you see. As you may already know, I am not the sole ruler of Okhema. It is me and the Council of Elders, which you see here.” She gestured to the scroll portraying the duties of the Council of Elders. “I have been working to create a specific regiment, you could say. It would consist of the strongest warriors in Okhema; of course, Phainon would be a part of it.”

Mydeimos crossed his arms, glaring at the scroll being shown to him. “And I am assuming you are in conflict with the Council of Elders, as they are refusing this personal guard?”

“I haven't been quite as successful as I would like to be,” Aglaea agreed. “However, if a kingdom whose expertise was war happened to want to collaborate through this specific regiment, arrangements could certainly be pushed through. It would make sense that this valiant country would rather work with only a specialized few rather than the entire Okheman guard, as no crisis in Okhema is large enough as of right now to warrant needing to be in contact with our whole guard.”

Narrowing his eyes, Mydeimos commented, “And why should Kremnos become involved in your inner political conflict?”

She placed the scroll down on her desk, but her constant smile only served to unnerve the King. “I am assuming you already have a price in mind. Tell me, is it something I can grant you?”

“You already know what I want. Why not spell it out?”

Aglaea chuckled. “I am torn. I had originally thought you wanted Okhema to welcome your citizens as our own in times of conflict. I have heard your people have been fighting for decades against the Black Tide monsters on your borders, and I had assumed you came to discuss peace with Okhema in the case your kingdom falls.” She examined her fingernails, polished in a brilliant gold. “However, it seems as if you also have eyes on my guard. Am I wrong?”

Mydeimos scoffed, ignoring her last comment. “You want me to back your plans for a specialized regiment in return for housing my citizens in times of war? It seems like you are neglecting to mention something else.”

“Why?” Aglaea tilted her head with an innocent smile. “Does the deal seem too good? It is an alliance with Kremnos, after all–the strongest military might in the world. If that doesn't appease you, would you like me to throw in my guard as well? I've heard you have no concubines or lovers.”

“Why does that concern you?” Mydeimos growled.

Aglaea laughed, covering her mouth with a gentle hand. “My apologies, King Mydeimos. I only said that in jest. If you truly wanted my guard, you would have to speak with him first.”

Mydeimos only stayed silent, waiting for the golden woman to continue speaking.

However, Aglaea wasn't the least bit intimidated by the King in front of her. “I would like your help with a little something. You see–” Aglaea raised the scroll again into the air, staring at the sun peeking through the scroll from the window. “–the Council of Elders is rather… troublesome, might I say.”

Mydeimos narrowed his eyes once more at the trade she was insinuating. “Hmph, so you don't want my help in supporting your specialized regiment. You want to take them down entirely.”

Aglaea was beaming at the King. “Oh, I didn't say that, did I?” She chuckled to herself. “Well, King Mydeimos, is that a fair trade? Of course, I don't expect an answer right away. I will give you the rest of your time here to ponder it over.” She set the scroll back down upon her desk, practically grinning at the King seated across from her.

“The political implications of your actions…” Mydeimos muttered more to himself than to Aglaea. He sank deep into thought, weighing the pros and cons in his mind over her proposal.

“I hope you enjoy the rest of your stay here in Okhema,” Aglaea said. “I hope you continue to enjoy your time with my guard, King Mydeimos. He is a wonderful man.”

Mydeimos stared at Aglaea, unmoving and without another word.

Nonetheless, Aglaea only smiled at him. “Do not worry, Your Majesty. I think of Phainon as a son of mine. I witnessed him join the ranks of soldiers when he was quite young and have only watched him grow overtime. There is no need to fear any competition on my part.” She hummed in delight, taking a sip of her tea. “Hasn't he grown to be such a handsome man?”

Mydeimos only let out a hmph in response before Aglaea gestured to the maid once more. “Please summon Phainon for me.”

The maid nodded at her order and exited the room.

Phainon was currently in the training grounds, practicing his swings against a dummy. He usually trained at the beginning of every day if he did not have any special missions or assignments to complete. Because he had to attend to the Kremnoans every day of this week, Phainon didn't expect he would get much training done until they departed.

He stopped mid-swing, his wooden sword hovering in the air at the thought. He had completely forgotten that Mydeimos would eventually leave. Well, he knew they were all going to leave once the Okheman festivities were over, but actually thinking about it sent a ball into the pit of his stomach. He had to admit it: Phainon had been enjoying the King’s company as of late. He was a great sparring partner, for one, and he genuinely enjoyed speaking with the King. Occasionally, he would even forget that he was actually nobility, but that was exactly what Mydeimos wanted.

Mydeimos was going to leave eventually… Phainon didn't think he would become so attached to a king that he had just met only the previous night. Especially as a commoner, Phainon didn't think he would become so close to a king in his entire lifetime. It was something he wouldn't have even entertained the idea of.
