“Good morning, Your Majesty.”

“Why did we go backwards this time?”

Phainon flinched at the question. He couldn't say his name without having flashbacks of the night before when he was in the public bath by himself, especially since he had specifically called his name too. Everytime Phainon echoed his name in his mind, all he could think of were the accompanying pants and moans from when he was alone, and he couldn't help his ears from burning from the memories.

He flashed a wry smile in response. He had previously prepared an answer on the way here, as he knew the King was going to question him about it. “We are going to the downtown market today. I just thought it would be appropriate to display proper manners in front of others.”

Mydeimos eyed him suspiciously, but he did not comment any further as he shut his bedroom door behind him. Phainon noticed that he was sporting new outerwear today–most likely lighter clothes that prioritized mobility and breathability. As they were spending most of the day in Marmoreal Market, the market in the downtown city, where crowds often gathered, Mydeimos most likely opted to wear clothes that weren't so focused on the golden armor that he had previously sported before.

Although he still wore those golden gauntlets, he no longer wore the golden greaves that he had arrived in. Instead, he was wearing umber leather boots with a small heel that reached to his thighs, with leather gaiters dyed in maroon that were locked in place by golden buckles. His dark trousers were tucked into the boots, clinging tightly to the shape of his legs due to the maroon garters encircling each of his upper thighs, and the golden belt he originally wore around his waist was now gone as only the same sash across his torso could be found. The most intriguing part of all was that half of Mydeimos’s hair was gathered in a loose bun at the back of his hair, and by all the Titans did Mydeimos need to continue wearing his hair like that.

However, a part of his hair was separated to form his signature braid that could always be found on the left side of his face.

The same crimson velvet cloak was still hanging off one shoulder along with his gold pauldron, but the thing that drew in Phainon the most was that he was actually wearing a shirt this time. Even though the shirt was open halfway down his torso, it was a collared maroon button-up that was tucked into his gauntlets while the end of his shirt was tucked loosely into the waist of his pants. His clothes were so tight against his frame that it truly almost looked like the button-up would burst at the seams even though it wasn't even closed all the way, and Phainon couldn't help his gaze from being glued to his bare chest. Somehow, it tempted him even more from when he didn't wear a shirt at all.

“HKS.”

Phainon's eyes immediately shot up at his voice. At this point, Phainon was no longer being discreet at how he basically ogled Mydeimos's body, and he was sure Mydeimos knew it too.

“I… I apologize. That was improper of me.” Phainon sheepishly scratched the back of his head. He was too ashamed to even gaze at the man before him, instead gluing his eyes on the man's leather boots and the maroon gaiters that wrapped across the tops of his feet. Embarrassment washed over him in waves as he thought about how Mydeimos was aware of how often Phainon had just been staring at him. He probably thought Phainon was crazy.

“Stop apologizing.” Mydeimos clicked his tongue in annoyance. “I truly thought we were making progress the previous day. What changed with you?”

The fact that I touched myself with thoughts of your naked body, but Phainon just kept his mouth shut and his eyes glued to the floor. He still couldn't believe what indecent thoughts he held for someone of such noble status; if Mydeimos even so much as found out, he would probably be beheaded. He was sure even Mydeimos, who had been emphasizing to treat him as an equal this entire trip, would be disgusted at the thought of a mere soldier thinking of him in such ways.

Mydeimos sighed heavily at Phainon's silence. “Speak to me as you spoke with me yesterday.”

“I will do my best.” Phainon offered the King a small smile, turning his head upwards. But, he still could not reach his eyes.

“HKS,” Mydeimos repeated that Kremnoan word with a firm tone. “Look at me.”

Although Phainon did manage to meet his unyielding golden gaze, he still couldn't help the unbelievable amount of shame that washed over his entire being at meeting his eyes. He wasn't sure what kind of pitiful expression he held, but he saw Mydeimos sigh once more when they made eye contact.

“Did something happen after departing my room?” Mydeimos narrowed his eyes, searching on Phainon's face as if his expression would give away any answers.

Flashes of last night and the public bath vividly flew through Phainon’s mind, and his eyes widened as he quickly exclaimed, “No! Nothing… Nothing happened, Your… Mydeimos.”

Clearly, something obviously happened. Phainon wasn't exactly the best liar, after all, and he knew Mydeimos did not believe a single word that came out of his mouth. But, before Mydeimos could confront him any further, the rest of the Kremnoan attendants filed out of their rooms, cutting their conversation to a close. As Marmoreal Market was often bustling with activity, only a few of the attendants were accompanying Mydeimos while the rest stayed in the palace.

Phainon led them down to the dining area as usual, where they ate a quick breakfast consisting of salted golden egg rolls topped with herbs and the same concoction of pomegranate juice mixed with goat's milk. The plan for today was to spend the majority of their time in Marmoreal Market in preparation for the ball that was to take place tomorrow, and Mydeimos was getting the last preparations to his attire completed in time for the occasion. As such, they only indulged in a small morning meal to get themselves ready for the remainder of the day.

With the palace entrance opened and sunlight flooding his vision, he led the party toward Marmoreal Market. Action Hour was beginning, and the sun was approaching high into the sky as he directed them to the market’s entrance and introduced them to any sights that they passed on the way. It was a clear day, and most of the Okheman citizens were out in the city, soaking in the warm sunlight as they wandered about. The Kremnoan attendants chatted amongst themselves as they admired all the sights to behold, and Phainon was amused with each one of their amazed reactions. However, Phainon never turned in the King’s direction.

When they finally reached the entrance to the downtown market, it was already a bustling sight as vendors were flooded with customers, and Okhemans citizens lined every corner of the streets. The chatter of the crowds filled his ears as he faced the attendants with a polite smile.

“So, to where do we need to go?” Phainon glanced at the closest attendant.

It happened to be Empousa again, who he had previously conversed with earlier. “We need fabrics to finalize the King’s attire. If you know the best place for fabrics or clothing, that would be great.”

Phainon nodded with a hum, running the different stores in his mind as he glanced to the side. “That should be no problem. Follow me.” He whirled around on his feet, directing the Kremnoans to the tailor shop that dealt with most of the clothing items for high nobility. He frequented this vendor fairly occasionally with Aglaea, and this was the tailor shop where Aglaea had gifted him his own outfit that he saved just for special occasions. Although Aglaea was a tailor of her own, she shopped many of her own pieces from this owner as well.

Passing through the bustling streets, they eventually arrived at the tailor shop. Owned by Aphrea, it was famously known by the upper class, and Phainon was extremely grateful he actually owned a piece tailored by Aphrea’s hands, courtesy of Aglaea, as he would never be able to afford such attire on his own soldier salary. Since the outfit was for the King of Kremnos, Phainon thought there was no other suitable place to bring them to other than this shop.

He opened the glass doors of the shop, and the Kremnoans passed through into the cool air that was circulating inside. Aphrea was currently in the main area of the store, sorting and organizing fabrics to be stored away in their respective spots.

“Phainon!” Aphrea beamed when she spotted the man. He was surprised she remembered him so well, as he never really had a reason to visit this store other than if he was accompanying Aglaea.

“Hey, Aphrea.” Phainon nodded in her direction. “I am sure you are busy during these times of the festivities, but do you perhaps have time for the King of Kremnos today?”

Her eyes widened like saucers at his request. The fabric that was in her hands dropped to the floor as she was shocked into a stupor, but she quickly scrambled for the fabric again, smoothing it out in her hands. She glanced between the Kremnoans and Phainon as if she couldn’t believe what he had said. “Of course I do!”

She quickly ushered the Kremnoans to approach deeper into the store, and Phainon nodded at them as they passed. He was sure a client such as a king would be a high-priority customer for Aphrea.

“I’ll be waiting near the entrance.” Phainon informed to the last attendant to pass by him, which was Empousa. “If you need me, just beckon me over.”

Empousa nodded in acknowledgement as Phainon departed to wait near the entrance of the store. There was no need for Phainon to be with them as they were preparing the King’s attire, after all.

With the silver-haired man out of earshot, Empousa immediately took the opportunity and whipped her head to Herklas, the other Kremnoan vanguard in attendance. “Did something happen between the King and the guard?”

“I was thinking the same.” Herklas stared in Phainon’s direction, who they could barely see now from where they were standing. “Did it seem like the guard wouldn’t even glance at the King?”

“That’s what I was thinking!” Empousa hissed. “Actually, I’m surprised you even noticed such a thing.”

Herklas gawked at her, but he couldn’t retort because a voice interrupted them.

“Done with your rambling?”

The two attendants immediately straightened their back, standing to attention at their king who was currently getting his measurements taken by Aphrea. His cloak and pauldron were currently set aside on a nearby wooden table as the measuring tape in Aphrea’s hands ran across his body. He was narrowing his eyes in their direction, clearly unamused at the conversation that directly centered around him.

“We were just worried about you, King Mydeimos.” Empousa anxiously laughed. “Is it our imagination?”

Herklas gawked at her again, not believing that she even had the audacity to ask him so bluntly to his face.

But, even more unbelievable to Herklas, the King ended up sighing in response. “I am not sure what happened either.”

It was almost as if Empousa was jumping in place at the thought of engaging in this sort of conversation with the King. Although King Mydeimos was always very benevolent with his subjects and happily conversed with them, because he was often busy as their king, that chance almost never occurred. Thus, Empousa was not going to let this opportunity slip away.

“What happened last night?! Wait, wait wait, just to make sure, you are interested in that Okheman guard, correct?!” Empousa slammed her hands down on the table in anticipation for the story, and she almost knocked the King’s golden pauldron onto the floor. The other attendant with them, Georgious, had barely caught it before it hit the floor. Because the attendants parted from the King halfway through the day, they didn’t know what had occurred between the two of them while they were alone. Empousa muttered a rushed apology to Georgious before turning back to the King, eager to not miss a single detail.

The King furrowed his eyebrows, raising his arms so Aphrea could measure them. “I invited him yesterday. To my private quarters.”

Empousa almost fainted, and Herklas had never gawked so much in a span of a single quint. Georgious almost dropped the golden pauldron that he was trying to place back onto the wooden table.

Empousa was trying very, very hard not to scream. Who knew their king was so forward! Though, she should have expected it–it was the Kremnoan’s way of always making the first move, after all; it was the best way to ensure true victory. Of course their king would embody that value. “So, what happened?”

Their king seemed to be recalling last night’s events as he gazed downward, deep in thought. “Nothing happened.”

“Did you want something to happen?” Georgious hesitantly asked. It seemed that everyone was now interested in their king’s love life.

King Mydeimos gazed in Georgious’s direction silently, seeming to mull over his words. He seemed to be entertaining the thought of what if something had actually happened and if he would have permissed it. “I took a bath.”

The three attendants were slightly puzzled on how their king indulging in a bath had to do with Georgious’s question, but it seemed that the answer hit all of them at the exact same time as they recalled his previous answers: He indulged in a bath while the Okheman guard was inside his private quarters?!

“And…” Empousa’s eyes were wildly searching the King’s face. “And nothing happened?”

A deep breath seemed to escape from the King’s lungs. “No.”

Empousa almost marched over to the Okheman guard still waiting by the entrance to slap the man across the face. Clearly, the Okheman guard was interested in the King as well; it was written all over his face since their initial meeting. How could he have the audacity to stand inside the private quarters of the King and do nothing?!

“Wow.” Herklas was breathless at this turn of events. He stared into the air, playing an imaginary replay of the events in his mind.

“Did…Did anything else happen?” Empousa stared intently at the King, who was now finished with his measurements. Georgious was now turning to Aphrea to discuss the types of fabrics that they were looking for.

“I invited him to bed.”

It seemed that all three of the attendants’ minds immediately turned blank. It wasn’t until a couple of beats later that Empousa could force her mind to work again, wracking her brain at the King’s statement that insinuated so many things. She was trying extremely hard to recall if she had heard any suspicious noises or activity from the previous night, as her room was directly adjacent to the King’s. But, she really did hear absolutely nothing. Truly, the King was right; nothing happened.

“Did he join you in bed?”

Empousa glanced at Herklas who had uttered the question, who he was leaning forward against the wooden table, clearly deeply involved in this conversation.

“He did.” the King’s gaze seemed to wander, staring at nothing in particular. Empousa was gauging each one of his expressions, ensuring she really did not miss anything that came from their king, and as she was about to ask whether anything had transpired once the guard had joined the King in his bed, he mumbled a question to his attendants with furrowed eyebrows. “Am I… not attractive?”

The three attendants’ minds went blank once more, both in shock that he had even asked such a question, and also for the fact that the answer was so obvious. Had he not seen a mirror recently? King Mydeimos was worldly famous for inheriting his beautiful looks from his mother, the late queen, Queen Gorgo. Empousa could still clearly recall Queen Gorgo from when she had first joined the Kremnoan vanguard, and she was absolutely awestruck at her radiance. The previous queen was a ferocious and formidable warrior, but she possessed one of the kindest souls that Empousa had ever witnessed, treating even the children of Kremnos as her own. When she had become acquainted with the then prince, she was shocked at how many similarities they shared, both physically and personality-wise. It still held true even now with King Mydeimos as their ruler.

“King Mydeimos,” Empousa could barely breathe those words from her chest, “I do not mean to make this sound offensive by any means, but it is quite obvious that you are the beauty of Kremnos.”

The other two attendants stayed silent in agreement, and they stared at their king as he seemed to take those words to heart. He nodded at her words with a serious gaze as Aphrea emerged from the back of the store with a handful of fabrics in tow. Empousa hadn’t even realized when the tailor shop owner had disappeared. Clearly, she was getting too invested in the King’s words.

“He really did nothing?” Herklas stole a glance at the Okheman guard who was still, thankfully, out of earshot. “Even after joining you in bed?”

The King glanced up at Herklas. “I had closed my eyes during our conversation, and it seemed that he thought I had fallen asleep.”

While Georgious was busy picking the right fabrics with Aphrea, Empousa and Herklas leaned even more forward against the table, waiting in great anticipation for what their king had to say next.

“He covered me with the sheets and departed from my room, turning out all the lights.”

Empousa almost dropped her head against the table, and she heard a slapping noise to her right from Herklas, who had a palm against his burning forehead. Was there something wrong with this Okheman guard? Or perhaps, was it just Okhema entirely? Were their cultures really so different that this Okheman guard could not understand a single clue that their king was practically throwing in his direction like a bone to a dog?

She almost cried aloud, “He just left?!” but she had to hold in her voice, else the Okheman guard actually picked up her voice from the entrance from where he currently awaited. Truly, Okhema was another beast entirely, and it was one even their unbeatable king was having difficulty facing. Though, she could at least applaud the Okheman for not jumping a sleeping man–well, the guard had thought the King was sleeping.

“There must be something wrong with that man.” Empousa had barely heard Herklas mutter these words under his breath, and she agreed wholeheartedly. If there was ever a chance she had time alone with that guard, she had to beat some sense into him. Or maybe, she had to sit the guard down and explain Kremnoan’s culture of courting from the very beginning so that he could understand what he had done wrong.

Contrary to the Okheman guard’s words, the noble status meant very little to the Kremnoans. Although it did matter somewhat, what mattered more was their display of strength, valiance, and honor. Rank and status were granted based on accomplishments, exploits, and victories achieved in battle. The late Queen Gorgo also was not of noble status, yet she was invited to be queen by the late King Eurypon after they had tied in a duel for the throne.

It was interesting that Okhema valued so much of what ran through a person’s blood rather than their achievements and valor throughout their lifetime. Why would a culture center around a part of an individual’s life that was uncontrollable rather than what that individual has achieved? Empousa couldn’t possibly wrap her head around such a culture, but it seemed this was the line that the Okheman guard refused to cross.

However, it was clear to all the Kremnoans in attendance in Okhema that this silver-haired guard was strong–so strong that he even rivaled their own king, similar to the late king and queen. There was no better match for their king than someone who rivaled him in strength. And, from what Empousa has seen and experienced so far, he genuinely seemed like a caring man as well–it was quite the plus that the Okheman guard was also quite handsome to boot. It seemed their king was set on this guard when they had drawn to a tie after multiple rounds of sparring during their initial day in Okhema.

“I have an idea,” Empousa announced to the party. If that Okheman guard wasn’t ever going to make a move due to their extreme differences in culture, then they would have to hit that man so hard that he would have no choice but to. She glanced at Georgious with a fiery determination burning in her eyes, and he looked surprised at how intense she was. “Georgious, we are changing the King’s attire for the ball.”

“Pardon?!” Georgious looked almost ready to fight her in the middle of the tailor shop. “Empousa, we are just now finalizing the fabrics–”

“Then tell the tailor shop owner that we require something else,” Empousa impatiently huffed. She glanced at the King to gauge his reaction to her abominable request, but he only narrowed her eyes at her. If he wasn’t saying anything to stop her, then he was going to allow it to happen.

“And? What fabrics should I ask for?” Georgious was running out of patience with this woman.

She smiled deviously at the Kremnoan soldier, resisting the urge to rub her hands together at the thought of her own little scheme. “If that Okheman guard refuses to approach the King, we will make it–no, make sure of it– that he absolutely cannot resist.”

“That didn't answer my question.”

In Kremnoan culture, one's body equaled one's strength. A person could gauge an individual's physical strength merely by the appearance of their body. Kremnoans valued this strength, and in turn, they valued the build that an individual could have. Displaying that body was almost as if they were displaying their own strength. It meant power to the Kremnoans, and it explained why their king was always showing off his body–because obviously, he was the strongest being in all of their kingdom. Naturally, there was a royal garb that displayed even more of his body than his normal attire. Although they hadn't brought it with them when they traveled to Okhema, it would be a simple task for this tailor to craft it for them, right?

She explained her idea to the party in attendance, and the King's attendants all muttered in agreement, completely immersed in this new plan and not even bothering to consult with the King in question who was actually going to be sporting the attire. Georgious was running the calculations in his head for exactly everything that they needed, and they needed a lot of gold to adorn their king in. A lot of gold.

“It is certainly doable.” Georgious nodded. “Let us prepare both outfits.” He quickly beckoned for Aphrea, who was in the back gathering the fabrics for the original outfit. As they discussed quietly about Empousa's new plan, she turned to the King, who continued to stand there with narrowed eyes.

She shot him a smile. “What do you think, my King?”

King Mydeimos only shut his eyes for a brief moment before slowly reopening them to stare at her with a plain gaze. “Do what you wish.”

Empousa almost cheered in the middle of the tailor shop. She was shaking with so much anticipation and excitement that she almost sprinted over to that oblivious Okheman guard standing at the entrance of the shop to tell him to prepare himself. She still couldn't believe that the King had invited the guard into his private quarters, took an entire bath with the guard in tow, and even invited him to his bed, yet nothing had occurred between the two. There must be something wrong with the Okhemans, right?

After a few quints spent in the tailor shop, they began finalizing the payments for all the materials and outfits for King Mydeimos that Aphrea had finished, and they were soon on their way from the shop. Their next stop to finish the King's outfit would ideally be a jeweler, so they could purchase the amount of gold jewelry that they would need to complete his attire.

Phainon saw from the entrance that the Kremnoans began to approach him with fabrics in their hands. They had spent quite a few quints in the tailor shop getting his outfit prepared, and he could only see from a distance that they were excitedly chatting about something. Perhaps, they were buzzing with excitement for the ball that was to occur tomorrow.

The female attendant, Empousa, stared at him with an almost too-pleasant smile; they must have really been excited for the ball. “Do you perhaps know of a jeweler we could visit?”

Phainon raised an eyebrow, running through the list of vendors available in Marmoreal Market in his mind. “Of course I do. Let me show you the way. But, I must ask, would you all like to eat a meal first?”

They had spent so much time in the tailor shop that they had completely skipped their midday meal. Although Phainon was quite used to going many days without eating, he wasn't sure about the noble class in Kremnos.

Empousa waved his question away, eager to complete their shopping trip. “No need. Let us go to the jeweler now.”

Phainon glanced at Mydeimos who nodded in confirmation at his attendant's words, and he thanked Aphrea before leading them out of the tailor shop and back to the blazing sun that beat down on the downtown market outside. The crowd was still bustling as ever as they navigated through the busy streets, visiting numerous caravans selling the goods that they needed. Dromas caravans, pulled by dromas that were great, strong, yet gentle beasts, often sauntered throughout the markets selling foreign or specialty wares that could not usually be found in Okhema. Especially during these times of festivities, the number of dromas caravans were much more generous than normal. Phainon didn't know much about jewelry, as he could never afford such a thing, but from the amount of gold and gemstones that they bought from each caravan, he could tell that the Kremnoans were at least satisfied with the places that he had taken them to.

As they were on their way to visit another dromas caravan to see what goods they sold, he ran into another individual that Phainon would say he was closer to than the average soldier.

“Castorice!” Phainon couldn't help exclaiming in delight when his eyes fell upon her usual purple and white ensemble.

Even though Castorice was of noble blood as well, they were actually quite close. Although she was not of royal blood in Okhema, she was actually related to the ruler of Styxia; in fact, the ruler of Styxia was her twin sister. But, Castorice came to Okhema very early in her age to learn more about the different kingdoms and to hone her magical power, and it was because of how long she had stayed in Okhema and how many years they have worked together under Aglaea that Phainon and Castorice grew close together despite Phainon usually keeping a respectable distance away from the upper class.

Castorice was a mage; to be specific, she was a necromancer. In Amphoreus, almost all members of the upper class possessed some form of magical affinity; for example, Aglaea was a weaver, and she could create objects out of thin air. Castorice was a necromancer and could summon death itself to fight for her. She had come to Okhema to hone that magical energy inside of her; she had previously explained to Phainon that she had a peculiar institution when she was born where she could not control her magical energy, and she would bring to death anything and anyone that physically came into contact with her. Although it proved just how strong the magical energy inside of her was, she came to Okhema to learn how to control her powers so she wouldn't have to dodge and avoid anyone anymore.

She and Phainon were classmates at the Grove of Epiphany where Castorice had also further honed her power–another reason lending to why Phainon and Castorice had grown so close. Phainon was only sent to the Grove because of Aglaea's orders; otherwise, he would have never been able to afford the steep tuition. The Grove of Epiphany and Okhema had quite a close alliance together, as many scholars visited Okhema, setting up lectures and schools around the kingdom, and many of the nobility class that could afford the travel and stay would go to the Grove of Epiphany for even more specialized teachings.

Phainon hadn't had the time to see Castorice due to the hustle and bustle of the festivities, but it seemed she was also a guard for the envoys of Styxia that came to visit for the ball. Styxia was a kingdom located near the ocean, and they believed that the departed would drift among the River of Souls on their way to the afterlife. It was why the kingdom centered heavily around water to ensure peaceful passage of their citizens. They were quite a tranquil kingdom that mostly kept to themselves. She was currently wheeling her sister, Queen Polyxia, who was seated in her usual wheelchair.

“Phainon.” Castorice cast a soft smile in his direction, and Phainon greeted both Castorice and Polyxia with a polite nod. “It has been a while. How are you doing?”

Phainon beamed at her. It truly felt like he hadn't seen her in quite a long time. “I’m doing great, Castorice. I see you are accompanying Styxia during their time here in Okhema, as usual.” Phainon directed his smile towards her twin sister. They truly shared quite the resemblance. “I hope you enjoy your time here in Okhema, Queen Polyxia.”

The queen smiled at Phainon. They had already been briefly acquainted before during previous balls due to Phainon's acquaintance with Castorice. “I always enjoy my time here in Okhema, and it is always even lovelier to spend time with my sister again.”

“I see Aglaea has tasked you with accompanying Kremnos.” Castorice nodded in their way. “I had wondered who she would choose to accompany them when I heard of their arrival.”

The Kremnoans attendants extended polite greetings to the Styxia attendants once they were brought up in the conversation, and Mydeimos stepped forward to give his greetings to Castorice and the queen, introducing himself as the King of Kremnos.

The three chatted away, most likely consisting of more pleasantries and discussions of their own kingdoms. Phainon had already stepped off to the side to give them some space, and he decided to use this spare time to run through the rest of their day. Action Hour was approaching its end with the beginning of Parting Hour, so most of the shops in Marmoreal Market were going to close soon. He hoped that the Kremnoan attendants were able to purchase all of the materials that they needed to finish Mydeimos's attire.

He turned to the King’s attendants, grabbing their attention. “Do you require anything else from the market? I think the shops are about to close up very soon for the day. I could point out any other caravans nearby while Mydeimos is here in case you need anything else.”

Empousa shook her head. She seemed quite satisfied with the haul that she and the other two attendants were carrying on their persons. “I think we have quite enough! In fact, I think we have just enough.” She glanced at both attendants next to her who nodded in confirmation.

“I see,” Phainon said. “Then, we should return to the palace once Mydeimos is ready before the sun begins to set.”

The attendants hummed in agreement, watching their king from a distance converse with the envoys from Styxia. Phainon was sure Mydeimos had a lot of work cut out for him at the ball tomorrow, as this was Kremnos's first public appearance in another kingdom in years. Especially as Kremnos's new king, he was sure Mydeimos had a lot of people that he would need to speak to from the other kingdoms. Phainon inwardly sighed at the thought. That meant he had to escort Mydeimos to every single kingdom's envoy in attendance at the ball tomorrow as his personal guard in Okhema. Although Mydeimos had a lot of work to complete tomorrow, as his Okheman guard, that meant Phainon also had a lot to do tomorrow.

“You should prepare yourself tomorrow.”

A voice cut his thoughts short as he turned around with furrowed eyebrows towards the origin of the voice. “What are you talking about, Empousa?”

Empousa smirked in Phainon's direction, shaking the bags of jewelry she held in her hands. “Prepare yourself tomorrow. You will soon behold a sight that will absolutely blow you away.”

Phainon smiled sheepishly, tilting his head to the side. “Do you mean Mydeimos’s attire for the ball tomorrow? Is it some sort of special Kremnoan attire?”

The female attendant nodded quite proudly. “Even you wouldn't be able to resist.”

“I'm sorry, resist?” Phainon was getting more lost by the second. What was she referring to? What was he resisting? Was there a foreign enemy that Empousa knew the arrival of?

“That's what I said.” She continued beaming with pride, but Phainon couldn't question her any further as Mydeimos had finished his conversation and rejoined their group.

Phainon cast one last smile to Castorice who was a few paces away as a way of bidding his farewells, and she returned quite the timid smile. She kept glancing between Phainon and something else with flushed cheeks– what was she looking at? He tried to scan in that direction she kept glancing toward, but only Mydeimos, who was standing right beside him, was in that direction. Did Mydeimos mention something to her during their conversation? But, what could they possibly speak amongst each other that would make her face redden like so?

Pushing his confusion away, he quickly explained to Mydeimos that the sun was about to set and the vendors were going to close shop, so they were going to return back to Marmoreal Palace before the sun disappeared under the horizon. With Empousa confirming that they had enough materials for his attire, they soon strolled down the streets of Marmoreal Market once again. They no longer had to navigate through bustling crowds as the people perusing the market dwindled in number with the setting sun.

With the sun no longer beating down on them, and the cool air of the night began to settle around them, it was quite a relaxing stroll back to the palace. Since the streets were no longer as packed, Phainon was able to point out more Okheman sights for the Kremnoans to admire and learn about as they made their way back from where they came. It was a beautiful sight to behold, with a burst of colors flying through the air above them as the sun dipped low beneath the horizon, casting its orange, glowing light upon them. Phainon couldn't help but steal glances at the King who walked beside him, who paid him no mind, because his glowing golden hair and red attire looked breathtaking under the sunset.

Arriving back at Marmoreal Palace, they decided to wash up and drop off the hefty amount of purchases to the bedrooms before indulging in supper, so Phainon bid them a quick goodbye after walking them back to their bedrooms.

He entertained the idea of just not showing up to dinner and picking them up afterwards, but he wasn't sure if Mydeimos would chastise him again for not eating dinner with them. But, it was hard; Phainon was still having trouble making eye contact with the man even after the entire day of leading him around the market. Although Phainon was able to avoid almost all conversation with the King due to how busy they were in the market, he knew he wouldn't be able to avoid the man during supper, especially if he was going to be sitting directly across from him at the table.

Tossing the idea in his mind, he made his way over to the palace training grounds, hoping to get a few good swings in before taking a bath. He also debated the idea of inviting Mydeimos to the training grounds with him, but he wasn't sure if it was too forward of him to ask a king to spar with him. In their past two sparring sessions, the King had initiated it. Phainon didn't want to overstep by any means if the King happened to be too exhausted after the market, after all. Though, it would be nice to have a partner to spar with, and maybe he would be able to forget about last night's solo activities if he were engaged in an intense battle with the man who was at the forefront of his mind all day.

He hummed, still debating the idea with himself as he stared at the wooden swords in front of him. He had already reached the training grounds, and he was sure Mydeimos was already washing himself off of all the sweat and grime from perusing the outdoor market all day. He was sure the King would refuse his request for a spar if he asked now, anyway. Maybe he will just ask Mydeimos next time, if there even was a next time.

After all, what was left of the agenda for the week was to attend the ball tomorrow, a rest day for everyone following the ball, and then only one more full day before the Kremnoans returned home on their last day. Phainon was sure Mydeimos wouldn't want to spar with him tomorrow, during his rest day, or during his last full day in Okhema as the King had to speak with Aglaea again on that day.

Sighing after running through the rest of the week's schedule in his mind, he plucked one of the wooden swords and headed over to the main area of the training grounds. He hadn't realized that the previous day would be the last time he would get to spar with the King, and the thought echoed in his mind as he swung his sword against the training dummy in front of him. Aiming for the dummy's shoulder, neck, and abdomen, the thought continued repeating over and over again in his mind, and no matter how many swings he struck upon the dummy, the more he could not ignore his aching heart.

Was he really that attached to Mydeimos? After only three days? Was it just because he had never spent so much time with another individual in a single day? No, that wasn't true at all; Phainon had guarded many other guests for the majority of the day, and it wasn't as if he got attached to them like he was now. So, what was so different with Mydeimos? Was it the fact that he was handsome, strong, valiant, skilled, supportive, kind, fair, intelligent, well-spoken, well-mannered…

Okay, clearly Phainon was heavily attracted to the man; his previous night's activities were also evidence of that. But, did that explain why he was so attached to the King? Because he liked him?

His mind cut short as he immediately stopped in his tracks at his own thoughts. Wait, Phainon liked him? The King? As in, he held feelings for the King?

He struck his sword against the crook of the dummy's neck, and his weapon flew out of his grasp before he could react. His brain felt static, and only that previous thought whirled around in his head as he faintly caught the sound of his wooden sword tumbling into the dirt.

With widened eyes, Phainon began mumbling incessantly to himself like a madman, glancing all around the training grounds with a dry throat and a pounding heart. Being attracted to someone was completely different from having feelings for someone, and the more the thought resounded through his mind, the more he could not deny the notion. It explained why he was so attached to the King, why he was always looking at the King, and why he was always thinking about the King.

No, not the King. Well, he was attracted to the King of Kremnos for sure; he was overwhelmed with how beautiful he was when they had first met, after all. But, Phainon held feelings specifically for Mydeimos: the man who had said Phainon was worth so much more, the man who had treated him as an equal, the man who tied with him multiple times in battle, and the man who asked to visit his hometown with him. He had feelings for the man who loved the color pink, who wasn't afraid of showing his body, and who wasn't afraid of mingling with anyone regardless of birth or blood. He was honest, forward, confident, and strong; the complete opposite of Phainon. He wasn't afraid of speaking anything that came to his mind, and Phainon yearned to have those qualities to himself, of having Mydeimos to himself.

His heart was pounding so loudly in his chest that it reverberated through his head, and he couldn't hear a single other sound other than his own heart. Phainon cursed himself for realizing his feelings so early when he still had to accompany the King for another three days in Okhema. Another four days, and then he would be gone. Gone forever from Phainon's life just as quickly as he had come in.

He warily turned himself around to pick up his sword, dusting it off and placing it back on the rack. He wouldn't be able to fit in any more swings in this unstable state he was in, as his heart continued twisting in his chest along with the feeling of his stomach dropping. He had to endure another three days with a man Phainon realized he had feelings for, and a man that Phainon knew he would never have a chance with. Mydeimos was a king, after all. He may have realized that he had feelings for a man, which didn't bother him at all, but that man just happened to rule a kingdom. If he was a normal man, maybe he would have had at least a slight chance, but definitely not with a king.

Phainon had never held such strong feelings for someone else before, so he hadn't actually known what it felt like to truly like someone in such a romantic manner. The soldiers in the barracks often discussed feelings of love, and they often conversed about the maids in the palace that they were attracted to. But, Phainon never really understood all those discussions. Sure, he would entertain the other soldiers, join in on the conversation, and even tease those blushing soldiers that described the ones that they loved, but he had never felt that same way before until now. Now, he could understand how those soldiers could drone on and on about one person and how their faces could become so red just thinking about that person. Because, now that was Phainon's reality.

The doors to the training grounds shut behind him with a loud bang, but before he could proceed any further, he was met with an exhausted maid who was practically running toward him with her skirt bunched up in her hands so she wouldn't trip.

“Phainon!” She stopped in front of him, bending over and gasping for breath, and Phainon knelt down to get a good look at the maid to ensure she was okay.

“Is everything okay?” His eyes wandered her face, gauging her reactions. But, other than being out of breath and her face flushed from running around, she was okay.

“Yes, I… I'm so sorry.” Bringing a hand to her chest, she shut her eyes and took deep breaths as Phainon raised himself from the floor.

“Take your time.” He smiled, but it seemed like the maid was in a bit of a rush.

The maid opened her eyes once more, staring up at Phainon. “I was looking for you everywhere. I went to the barracks and to the soldier's bath because that's where they all said you went.”

“They?” Phainon raised an eyebrow.

Clearing her throat, the maid straightened her  back, finally regaining her composure. “The Kremnoan attendants and their king all came down for supper. But, halfway through supper, it seemed that their king was in a foul mood, and his attendants ordered me to find you.”

Phainon's eyes widened at her explanation. Oh shit.

His shoulders dropped. “What time is it?”

Phainon truly did not want to know what time it was, but the maid hummed in thought. “I would say it is five quints into the Parting Hour. The Kremnoans came down to eat four quints into the Parting Hour. ”

Oh shit.

Phainon rushed past the maid, thanking her quickly before darting down the corridor in the direction of the dining hall. It was basically almost Curtain-Fall Hour, and he had completely missed the time to eat dinner with the Kremnoans. Sure, he did debate on the idea of skipping out of it so he didn't have to face the King, but he didn't mean to actually skip out. He had meant to get a quick workout in before heading to the baths and then meeting them at the dining hall for supper. But, how long did he spend in the training grounds that the time had completely escaped him? How long was he just thinking of Mydeimos after they parted? He was never this disorganized and unattentive, and he had no one to blame except for himself and these new feelings that he kept experiencing. These feelings just kept disorienting and confusing him, and they were about to cost even his life depending on how furious the King was.

It was now Phainon's turn to gasp for breath as he turned the corner and abruptly halted in his steps, coming face to face with the door that led to the dining hall. Mydeimos was definitely still waiting in there, right? They pretty much waited for him to arrive for an entire quint, and Phainon never so much as made an entrance even after Mydeimos had explicitly expressed wanting to eat with him. He couldn't even begin to imagine Mydeimos’s fiery gaze, and he certainly did not want to have to face it when he opened this door.

Phainon really fucked up this time. If Kremnos decided not to engage in an alliance with Okhema by the end of this week, he might as well kiss his life goodbye. Or, maybe he could just drop to his knees in Aglaea's office and plead for her mercy. Maybe he should just turn around from the dining hall door, avoid Mydeimos’s wrath, and cling onto Aglaea's knees right at this moment.

He tried his absolute best to tidy his appearance after the training session he just had and after practically sprinting over to the dining hall. Running a hand through his unkempt hair, he realized just how much he was sweating, but he didn't have enough time to wash himself off from the day's activities. He couldn't possibly keep the King of Kremnos waiting any longer.

Inhaling a deep breath, he firmly grasped the handle to the door and pushed them open. Acting as normal as possible, he was met with the attention of all the Kremnoan attendants and their king at the table.

Doing his utmost to appear as mannered and polite as possible, Phainon tried to mask how truly anxious he actually felt. “I truly apologize for my rudeness today. The time seemed to have escaped me, but I know that is no excuse for my behavior. I would accept any and all punishment you would have for me.”

He was too frightened to even look at the King, but he knew that he would have to if he wanted his apology to be perfect for the King. Locking eyes with golden ones, he expected irritation, anger, and exasperation. Phainon was expecting to have a plate thrown at him or a fist to knock the breath out of his chest. He was also assuming he would have to get on his knees and bow to the King before him.

But, his heart shattered when all he saw in Mydeimos's golden eyes was complete and absolute betrayal.

It was hard to keep his mask from dropping when he saw how deflated he looked, and it was even harder to stop himself from rushing over to comfort the man. He wasn't expecting such a headstrong and confident man such as Mydeimos to even know what “sadness” felt like, yet here he was, locking eyes with his heartbroken ones.

He waited a few beats for anyone to say anything at all, but they all continued to wordlessly stare at Phainon. He couldn't even begin to imagine what this dinner was like with him absent the entire time.

“I…” Was it appropriate to call him “Mydeimos” right now? Phainon wanted to call out to him, ask him to yell at him, ask him to make him kneel to the floor and apologize, but all of those words died in his throat as he didn't know how he should refer to him. Should he say “Mydeimos”?

Should he continue his formal apology and say “Your Majesty”? What if he said the wrong one and further disappointed him? If it was any other noble figure, this formal apology would be easy to recite, but because it was Mydeimos, Phainon hadn't a clue what to do. He had never met a nobleman such as Mydeimos before, and it was making his brain and his heart spiral.

“My king.” The attendant next to Mydeimos, Empousa, gently nudged him. “Would you prefer some time alone?”

Phainon almost blurted out, Please don't leave us alone, but he did his best to hold his tongue as he watched the King's gaze drop to the table with a silent nod at her words. The attendants all stood up at once, sparing a glance at Phainon before retreating from the room. Empousa's eyes seemed to linger on Phainon's, but he couldn't decipher what she was trying to soundlessly communicate to him before she passed him by.

The door shut behind him, and the sound was so much louder than what Phainon was used to. Besides the Okheman servants cowering in the corner, only Phainon and the King were left in the room.

“I truly, deeply apologize for what I have–”

“Drop it.”

Phainon inwardly flinched at the sharp, seething tone, but he did his best not to waver under the King’s stern gaze. There it was–the King's fury was now starting to come to the surface. The betrayal Phainon had seen in his eyes before was now gone, replaced with that fiery glare that Phainon was first expecting when he had stepped into the room. Most likely, he was holding it in front of his attendants until they had a moment to themselves.

Phainon fell silent at the King's orders, bringing his hands together in a tight grasp in front of him as he awaited his fate from the King. He was taking deep breaths to calm himself, but his anxious and pounding heartbeat was drowning out the rest of his senses. He could have his eyes picked from their sockets if the King ordered him to do so right at this moment, and Phainon could do nothing about it as he had so blatantly disobeyed the King's orders. Because Phainon was not a person of status in Okhema, it really did not matter what happened to him even if someone from a foreign kingdom harmed him. At least the last person Phainon would ever be able to lay his eyes upon was the King, so he guessed it wasn't that bad.

He kept waiting and waiting, standing upon his own two feet in front of the King's glare, but the King didn't say anything to him at all as he continued to bore his eyes straight through Phainon's soul. The only sound reasoning Phainon could think of for his prolonged silence was that the King was mulling over which body part of Phainon's he wanted to sever first.

“First, I tell you to drop the formalities. Then, I ask you to indulge in meals with me. But, it seems like you can do neither.”

Phainon grimaced at his harsh tone, gritting his teeth together at the pain he was expecting to feel after some body part of his was separated from his body. He was anticipating it now with the way the King continued to glare in his direction.

“I truly am–”

“I said to drop it.”

Phainon quickly shut his mouth, gritting his teeth once more to prepare himself for the pain and the blood. Maybe he shouldn't speak unless he was told to.

He heard an exasperated sigh come from the King's direction–when had Phainon's gaze dropped to the floor? Slowly raising his eyes, Phainon watched as the King rose from his seat and pushed the chair back into the table. His footsteps echoed in his brain as the King approached him, and Phainon could do nothing but tighten the grasp he held against his own hand.

The King cocked his head to the side, continuing to bore his eyes into Phainon's, and he felt as if he were trembling under his firm gaze no matter how much he tried to appear composed. He couldn't help the feeling of his heart continuing to drop into his stomach the longer the King glared at him.

“I…” Phainon hesitantly started, waiting to see if the King would permit him to speak. Because he didn't interrupt him, Phainon continued. “If you would like to arrange a new guard for the remainder of your stay, I could certainly have that arranged for you.” Phainon's heart was breaking with each word he spoke, but he thought it was for the best if it was so difficult for Phainon to follow the King's orders. Would that mean this would be the last conversation he would ever have with Mydeimos? He hated that thought. “If you would like me to, I can speak with Aglaea who could–”

“Drop it.”

The rest of Phainon's sentence died in his throat as he shut his mouth once more.

The King sighed once again, and the glare dissipated from his eyes as he glanced off to the side. “How could I continue my anger when you look like a kicked puppy?”

“I… I apologi–”

“Drop it.”

Phainon shut his mouth once more.

Another deep sigh escaped the King. “Did you not hear a single word I said?”

Phainon's eyes slightly widened in confusion as he replayed the entire conversation in his head. What was he referring to? Which part was he talking about? All he basically told Phainon to do was shut up, so what was he missing?

“It seems like you didn't.”

This was it–this was where Phainon would lose his arm. Or his leg, or his eyes. Saying a quick, silent goodbye to his body and thanking them for all that they have done for him, he also quickly bid his career a goodbye, as he wouldn't be able to serve the kingdom if he were handicapped. Now, Phainon would be known all across Okhema as the man who blatantly disobeyed the King of Kremnos and had to retire from being a soldier. But, Phainon was more disappointed in himself for letting Aglaea down like so; she had such grand expectations for him, and he had severely let her down in just a matter of a few days. And, thinking about it even further, if he retired and returned to his hometown, how would he possibly be of help in the fields if he was handicapped? Not only could he not help Aglaea, but he could no longer help even his own family.

A fourth sigh from the King could be heard. “Did I not tell you to drop the formalities? Then, why are you still speaking to me in that way?”

Phainon's body grew rigid. When the King said to drop it, he was referring instead to Phainon's manner of speech rather than Phainon merely speaking?

Chancing a glance at the king–when had his sight dropped to the floor again?–the glare was no longer evident on the man's face. He only plainly stared at Phainon as he awaited his answer.

“I… I'm really sorry, Mydeimos, for missing dinner.”

With a scoff, Mydeimos crossed his arms across his chest, and Phainon was shocked when a soft smile graced his lips. “That's a good boy.”

Phainon's eyes widened in response. It was as if, at those words, Phainon was never frightened or afraid for his life. It was as if all the tension immediately disappeared from his body, and the blood that was pounding in his heart in nervousness and apprehension immediately rushed to his dick. Phainon could not even believe how quickly his body had gone from fight-or-flight to turned on in a matter of two beats of his heart.

“Truly, how could you even insinuate such a thing?” Mydeimos was muttering under his breath, and Phainon tried to ignore the strain in his pants to listen to his words.

“Sorry?”

Mydeimos glared sharply at Phainon, and his erection immediately died. “Do not ever suggest replacing my guard again, do you hear me?”

To be honest, the only thing Phainon really heard was Mydeimos referring to him as “my guard.” It really was like music to his ears, and Phainon just really wanted to hear him say that again. Instead, Phainon nodded his head once his brain had finally processed the rest of his sentence.

“I won't.” He smiled at Mydeimos, thankful that he was so merciful with him. Truly, how did Phainon get so fortunate? If he had disobeyed any other noble in Okhema, he would have lost a limb by now.

“Then,” Mydeimos began, approaching the entrance to the dining hall, “if you are so sorry, then accompany me to my quarters.”

Phainon couldn't help the grin that spread across his face as he eagerly bounded to the door, opening it for Mydeimos to walk through. He waved a quick farewell to the servants who were still in the dining hall, and they all shared an expression of relief between each other that they did not have to clean up any blood that night.

They reached the door to Mydeimos's private quarters, and they both stepped inside to the room that Phainon was now so familiar with. It was in the exact same state that Phainon had seen before he departed the previous night, but Phainon was mostly thankful that he did not have to endure the hardship of watching such a beautiful man bathe again. He wasn't sure if he could handle another erection today.

“So, what made you so late to dinner?”

If it wasn't for Mydeimos's casual tone, he would have assumed he was being brought here in the privacy of his quarters to be interrogated.

“I was training in the training grounds, and time seemed to have passed me by.”

Mydeimos hummed, beginning to shed his velvet cloak and pauldron as he readied himself for the night. “And you didn't bother to invite me?”

Phainon laughed softly at the irony of his question. Really, why did he question himself so much over extending the invite to him? “I thought you would be too tired from shopping all day in the market, so I just planned on getting a quick workout in before taking a bath and joining you all for dinner. It really was not my intention to miss it.” Phainon purposefully left out the part where he had actually debated on skipping out.

Shedding the royal sash across his body and unbuttoning the rest of his shirt, Mydeimos scoffed. “If you are not tired, then neither am I. Do you really underestimate me so?”

He couldn't help the laugh that escaped him. “You’re right. I should've thought about that, Mydeimos.”

Mydeimos stripped the rest of his clothes, and Phainon averted his gaze to give him that bit of privacy as he slipped into more comfortable clothes to retire for the night. Somehow, Phainon was getting more used to being in the King’s naked presence which was quite an odd thing to get used to. Maybe after the nervousness he had felt earlier in the dining hall, nothing else would be able to scare him for the remainder of the day.

When he heard Mydeimos approach his bed, Phainon brought his gaze back to the man, who was adorned again in that all-too-tempting silk robe. “If you are retiring for the night, I should go now. Good night, Mydeimos.”

There was something with this man always preventing him from leaving, because before Phainon could take a step toward the exit, Mydeimos's voice interrupted him. “Stay. Join me in bed tonight.”

Phainon's eyes couldn't help but fall into the ample, empty space next to Mydeimos before returning to the man who was now covering his lap with the sheets. “Would you like me to accompany you until you fall asleep again?”

With his back leaning against the headboard, Mydeimos raised an eyebrow. “I meant for you to stay for the night.”

Phainon had meant to be teasing the King with his question, but with the way Mydeimos had so plainly asked him to sleep in the same bed as him for the entirety of the night, Phainon's heart began beating wildly in his chest.

“To stay?” Those were the only words that Phainon could manage. His brain was too busy processing the idea of falling asleep under the same covers and in the same bed as Mydeimos.

Mydeimos furrowed his eyebrows with a frown as if he couldn't believe he had to repeat himself. “Yes. Stay. And sleep. In this bed with me, HKS. What more do you need me to say to get it through your head?”

Attempting to suppress the blush that crept over his cheeks, which did not succeed, Phainon rigidly willed his legs to carry him over to the other side of the bed. Standing there, staring down at the clean, silk sheets that the maids had so meticulously spread across the bed, he felt sorry that he was about to sully them.

“Could I… take a bath first before climbing into your bed?” Phainon sheepishly smiled as he ran a hand through his hair, feeling the day's weight through his fingertips.

Mydeimos seemed to eye him carefully, gauging whether this was another tactic for Phainon to escape or not. But, with a sigh, Mydeimos agreed, and Phainon had never rushed out of the room to take a bath so quickly in his entire life. He felt as if he practically flew out of the palace as he headed to his belongings in the barracks before rushing once more to strip himself and step into the baths.

Again, as it was so late into Curtain-Fall Hour now, no one else could be found in the baths at this time. He felt as if this would be a repeating pattern for the remainder of the week. Phainon felt he had been so busy and caught up in so many things while escorting the Kremnoan envoys that he felt he could not return until it was late into the night. And, although being alone in the baths did remind him once again of his solo activities from the previous night, he had no time to dwell on those embarrassing memories as he quickly dressed himself and hurried back to Mydeimos's quarters. After being on the receiving end of his wrath and almost losing a limb today, he didn't want to keep the King waiting anymore than he needed to.

He brought a hand up to knock on the ornate door that led to Mydeimos's temporary bedroom, and he faintly heard his voice beckon him inside. Softly shutting the door behind him, he made his way back to the edge of the bed, propping his beloved Dawnmaker near his bedside, and climbed under the covers in one swift movement before he could overthink and hesitate again.

Mydeimos was still in the same place on the bed; he had been reviewing scrolls and documents with a keen gaze before Phainon had returned. However, once Phainon had made his reappearance, he had set the documents aside on the matching mahogany bedside table.

“Don't let me disturb you.” Phainon eyed the documents that were stacked away. “I'm sure you have a lot of work that needs to be done.”

Mydeimos, who had his back against the headboard, shuffled in bed until he had joined Phainon in laying down under the sheets. “No need. It doesn't need to be done today.”

Phainon softly laughed, heart pounding when he saw how close they were laying side by side in the same bed and even under the same sheets. He could only hope that Mydeimos could not hear his racing heart. “How much work are you behind on now that you have come to Okhema? I'm sure there is a lot of work waiting for you when you return.”

“I have my teacher watching things over for me while I am here. He should be doing more than fine in my absence.”

“Right, his name was Krateros?”

“Did my attendants speak of him?”

Phainon recalled the first conversation he ever had with his attendants. “Yes they did. They–” He immediately shut his mouth when he remembered exactly why they brought up Krateros in the first place. It was because they were gossiping about how Mydeimos didn't have a lover, and his teacher was trying to arrange matches for him.

“They?”

“Nothing. It was just meaningless chatter.” Phainon, the worst liar in all of Amphoreus, could only avert his gaze from scrutinizing golden eyes.

Mydeimos hummed, clearly not convinced, but he let it slide. “Yes, my teacher is named Krateros. He was made a close confidante and general after proving his strength in front of my parents, and he has been serving the royal family ever since.”

“You must really rely on him then,” Phainon remarked, eager to continue the conversation and learn more about Mydeimos's story.

“Yes, he is quite reliable and strong.” Mydeimos nodded. “He… scolds me quite often. We argue about how to run the kingdom, but I know he has good intentions.”

“It's nice to have someone next to you that you could trust to hear their thoughts.”

“I agree. Krateros is exactly that. He raised me, after all.”

“Raised you? Did your parents not raise you?” Phainon recalled that the news spread of Mydei ascending to the throne after his parents’ death was only a few years ago. But, Mydeimos made it sound like Krateros had been watching over him for a long time.

Mydeimos raised an eyebrow at his question. “I'm sure the passing of my parents is no secret to you.”

“I… don't mean to be so forward, but didn't that happen only a few years ago?”

Mydeimos fell silent, and Phainon wasn't sure if he was incorrect. But, did Kremnos really go on for more than those years without a king? He truly believed the news of Mydeimos ascending the throne was only a few years ago, but did his parents pass many years before that?

“You don't have to tell me.” Phainon softly chuckled, offering the man a small, reassuring smile. He could see how seriously Mydeimos was thinking to himself. “I know, as king, there are probably many things that you cannot tell me. I won't question it any further. We can talk about something else. Say–”

“No.” Mydeimos stared firmly back into Phainon's eyes. “I was just recalling everything. It seems the death of my parents truly did not reach your ears, or the outside world, I am assuming.”

“Sorry?” Phainon blankly blinked at him.

“My parents passed when I was quite young. My mother passed away when I was a child, and I killed my father with my own hands a few years later.”

“Wait, a few years later? Not just a few years ago?”

Mydeimos shook his head. “Once my father killed my mother, I–”

“Your own father killed your mother?!” Phainon was sitting up in bed now, clearly invested in the drama unfolding in Mydeimos's family.

The man still lying in bed chuckled at Phainon's dramatic reaction. “A prophecy was foretold when I was a child that I would soon ascend the throne. As a new ruler of Kremnos would only ascend to the throne only after killing the current ruler, the prophecy meant that my father was going to be killed by my hands sooner than everyone originally expected. After all, I was only a child. How could that prophecy foretell that a child would ascend to the Kremnoan throne so soon?”

“So he… wanted to kill you for that?” Phainon could only guess where this story was going.

“Yes, and my mother was against it.” Mydeimos closed his eyes as if reliving those memories. “I don't really remember my mother as I was quite young; I can only hear of her valor from Krateros and the other vanguards. But, she had challenged my father to a duel and lost her life. Subsequently, my father banished me from Kremnos and left me to die.”

“He just banished a child?!”

“Lower your voice; you are too loud.

“But that's–”

“I am alive and well now, am I not?”

Phainon couldn't argue with that logic and fell silent at his words.

“A group of Kremnoans followed me during my banishment, including Krateros, and it was outside Kremnos's borders that we staged a rebellion against the King. Many years later, I killed my father with a blade, and it was the last time I ever wielded one.” Mydeimos's eyes were open now, but they were downcast at recalling all his dark memories. “Many lives were lost; I lost all of my trusted confidantes in that detachment of ours, but we came out victorious. I didn't take the throne until I was of age a few years later.”

Phainon laid back down in bed, thoughts swirling in his brain as he digested this information. That explained why he couldn't find a weapon on Mydeimos when they had first met, and it also explained why he did not wield a weapon when they were sparring. “That's… Are you… okay?”

He stared at Mydeimos who looked quite shocked that he was being asked that question. But with a small smile, Mydeimos answered, “It was a long time ago. I am content with my place as King of Kremnos now.”

“The attendants all love you.” Phainon returned the smile. “They all seem to get along quite well with their king.”

“You seem to get along quite well with my attendants too.”

Chuckling, Phainon agreed, “Yes, they are easy to get along with, and they seem like enjoyable company.”

The man beside him nodded. “They are very reliable, quick-witted, and strong in battle. It was why I asked them to join me here in Okhema.”

“I'd love to see them in battle.”

“As confident as I am in my people, none of them would be able to best you if you are equally matched with me.”

“That is of no matter!” Phainon exclaimed with a grin. “It would be fun to spar with other Kremnoans. I'm sure I would have a lot to learn from you all.”

Mydeimos chuckled. “They would be eager to spar with you. We should, one of these days.”

One of these days? Was Mydeimos planning on trying to fit in sparring sessions during his last four days in Okhema? It was technically only just three days left, as they were leaving early on their last day here.

Admiring the glittering, golden chandelier above them and reviewing the schedule in his head, Phainon didn't think there would be any time suitable to visit the training grounds with the Kremnoans envoys again, but he didn't say anything, choosing to lament their short time left together in silence.

“Mydeimos?”

“What do you want now?”

He glanced over at the man beside him, and the sight never failed to take his breath away. The way his silk robe covered absolutely nothing, the way his golden hair draped along the pillows and sheets, the way his golden eyes stared right into Phainon. If Phainon outstretched his arm, he would be able to caress his cheek, brush his soft lips, and maybe even run his fingertips through his hair…

He heard a scoff, and Phainon's inappropriate thoughts were immediately cut short.

“You are staring, HKS.”

With burning cheeks, Phainon buried himself in the blanket, mumbling an apology. “Sorry. You are just… very eye-catching, Mydeimos.”

He couldn't see anything with his face buried away, but he heard an amused hum above him. “So, you do find me handsome.”

“Of course I do!” Phainon shot up from the blanket but quickly reeled back at how close Mydeimos was to him. When was the man practically above him? His golden hair was almost brushing Phainon's face.

“If that were the case, why did you avoid me all day today?”

Phainon's body froze up. So, he really did notice that Phainon was trying to avoid him the entire day? He thought maybe, or at least hoped, with all the hustle and bustle in Marmoreal Market, that Mydeimos would be too preoccupied to notice.

“I…” Phainon averted his gaze once more as his body burned at his memories from the previous night in the bath. With the silence from Mydeimos, he knew he wasn't going to back down from an answer, but he couldn't just plainly tell the man he had masturbated to him last night.

With wandering eyes, Phainon couldn't think of a single excuse to explain his actions. “I'm sorry. I really don't think it is appropriate for me to explain. But–” Phainon whipped his eyes back onto Mydeimos’s. “–it is not of your concern, nor is it your fault. That, I can promise you. “

“So, the fault lies with you?”

“Yes.” Phainon frowned when his face began to redden once more. “Please, don't ask any more questions.”

With a sigh from Mydeimos, at least Phainon was being let off the hook. “Fine. Then, at least stay the entire night this time.”

Phainon furrowed his eyebrows. This time? Wasn't this the only time Mydeimos had ever invited him to stay the night? But, Phainon couldn't dwell on it any longer, as Mydeimos shrouded the room into darkness as he retired for the night. And Phainon, who was still left with his pounding heart, had to fall asleep to the dark silhouette of Mydeimos falling asleep right beside him, who was so close he could practically feel his body heat upon his own person.

“I had never seen the King look like he did today.”

Empousa was wringing her fingers together in anxiousness as she sat at the edge of her bed. They had just departed from the dining hall, leaving that Okheman guard alone with the King. She tried to reassure the guard that he wouldn't be harmed–their King was never the type of ruler who harmed his own subjects–but the man was so frightened out of his wits that she was sure he did not understand what she was trying to convey. She felt bad with how the man had practically shook under the intense gaze of their King–a stark contrast to the man she saw spar against their King in the training grounds.

“He looked almost abandoned.” Herklas was removing his armor for the night, setting it at his bedside for easy access.

Empousa nodded with a saddened gaze. “He looked so lost. So betrayed, even. He didn't even look like that when his own mother passed. When his mother passed, he was with an air of vengeance and resolution. But here, I have never seen the King look so defeated in all my life.”

Herklas stayed silent at her words, and Empousa's eyes wandered the room, soon finding the haul that they had purchased thrown together in a corner of their room as she continued to fill the silence. “I'm sure, with the Okheman guard avoiding him the entire day, that him skipping out of supper as well didn't bode very well with King Mydeimos either.”

She suddenly slapped her hands against her thighs, jumping to her feet and making Herklas jump at the sudden noise. “It’s time! We are going to make the most stunning outfit for the King tomorrow. Come, help me put the jewelry together for his attire.”

Empousa rushed out of their shared bedroom before dragging Georgious from his room into theirs, and the three of them spent the remainder of the night preparing the King's new ball attire, determined to send the Okheman guard into cardiac arrest at the sight of their King.

“But–” Empousa whirled her attention over to Georgious. “–why did you suggest getting his original ball attire made still? If we're changing what he's wearing, we might as well not get the original outfit arranged.”

Georgious huffed, never breaking attention from the chains he was connecting together. “In case that guard ruins it.”

“Huh? Ruins?” Empousa furrowed her eyebrows. “What do you mean by ‘ruins’?”

Georgious did not comment any more on the subject, and Empousa was left wondering why the Okheman guard would ruin such an expensive outfit.

Phainon was surprised he even managed to sleep that night with how loudly his heart was racing at watching Mydeimos sleep next to him. Upon opening his eyes in the morning, he was momentarily shocked to be met with such an elaborate ceiling and the grand chandelier that hung in the middle of the room, as he had completely forgotten he actually went to sleep in the King of Kremnos's room.

He turned to the side and found himself face-to-face with the king in question. The robe was falling off his shoulders and being covered instead with Mydeimos’s golden hair as he slept with lips slightly parted and long eyelashes brushing against his cheeks. Phainon watched, mesmerized, as his shoulders rose and fell with each breath, and he had to resist with all his might not to wrap his arms around his waist, pull the man close to him, and breathe in his scent.

With the morning sunlight streaming through the closed curtains, dimly lighting the room, Mydeimos looked absolutely breathtaking. His hands were curled loosely near his face, and it was probably the first time Phainon had ever seen his bare hands as the King usually wore gold gauntlets. His hands were big, yet his fingers were lithe, and Phainon just wanted to interlock their fingers together and feel his skin against him. He could see calluses on his hands from all his efforts in training, yet his hands still looked so alluring, graceful, and elegant. He wanted to rub little circles in his hand, trace his calluses, and plant little pecks and kisses all along the tops of his hands.

Phainon inwardly sighed. Why did he have to realize his feelings so soon? He wished he could have stayed ignorant, then maybe he could have treated Mydeimos as close to a friend as possible before they parted ways by the end of the week. He would have had fond memories to look back upon as he thought about the one week he got to spend time with a king that treated him so generously. Now, Phainon will feel nothing but regret the moment the King of Kremnos disappeared from Okhema, never to return again for the next couple of years. Would Mydeimos even remember their time together? Or would he just be the one of many people that a king would meet in his life, never to be thought of again.

Pushing those negative thoughts away and pulling himself from the bed, Phainon decided to start his day and distract himself with something else. Today was the day of the royal ball, and most of the royal guests spent the majority of the day preparing their appearance for the ball that started in the evening during Parting Hour. That most likely meant that Mydeimos would spend the majority of his time in his room, preparing his attire and hairdress for the ball tonight.

That also meant that Phainon would not be needed until it was time to attend the royal ball as Mydeimos’s personal guard. There was no need for Phainon to prepare himself in the same way the other guests did; after all, he was only there to guard a high-profile guest. He was not actually an invited guest. Although it was more proper to wear a uniform that matched the occasion, he didn't have to worry about other things such as styling his hair, for instance, or decorative armor and jewelry. As such, while Mydeimos was spending the day getting ready, Phainon had a lot more free time today until the ball started.

He swung his legs off the edge of the bed to stand up, strapping Dawnmaker back to his hip where his greatsword often sat on his person. It was when he was fiddling with the straps around his waist to secure the greatsword in place when he heard a soft groan coming from the bed.

Phainon glanced up with a small smile, admiring how Mydeimos was adorably blinking the sleep out of his eyes and pushing his tangled bangs from his face with his bare hand. Truly, the individual that would lay their eyes upon this sight in the future every single morning would have to be the luckiest person to ever live.

“Leaving?” Mydeimos grumbled, eyes wandering to the sword now strapped against Phainon's person.

Phainon tried hard not to admire how beautiful his soft but husky voice in the morning sounded. “Good morning, Mydeimos. I was just on my way out. Did I wake you?”

“You were going to leave without telling me?”

Titans, was this man sprawled out in the bed in front of him pouting up at him? Mydeimos was stretching in the middle of the bed, hands balled into fists as he arched his back, his stomach pressed against the bed as he pouted up at Phainon with a sleepy, half-lidded gaze. Holy Titans, Phainon had to get out of here before he exploded–before his lower half exploded, to be exact. Was this what drowsy Mydeimos was like every morning? Phainon burned in envy again thinking of his future partner who would be able to witness him like this every day.

“I didn't want to disturb your sleep,” Phainon muttered, bending down toward him with a smile. “I'll be picking you up for the ball later today. The chefs are still serving morning meals today, so you may go to the dining hall to enjoy before getting ready. Just know that the chefs are preparing food for the ball, so the morning meal may not be as exquisite as previous days.”

Mydeimos nodded languidly, and Phainon couldn't help his smile from growing as he cherished the soft view before him. In a gentle tone, Phainon continued, “Then, Mydeimos, I will see you tonight.”

Phainon had only briefly turned around and taken a few steps toward the exit when he heard Mydeimos's voice faintly call from the bed.

“Stay.”

Raising an eyebrow, Phainon faltered in his steps and turned around. “Stay?”

Mydeimos nodded with another languid nod. “Come back.”

Phainon was unsure if Mydeimos still needed something from him, so he approached his bedside and knelt down until they were nearly eye level.

“Did you need something from me before I go?”

“You.”

“Sorry?”
