The entire Marmoreal Palace was in absolute chaos. As the royal ball was a time where royal guests from all over Amphoreus gathered in one place, despite the heavy workload that went into preparing the ball, it was worth the effort, as they were able to hear all the exclusive news that only people working within the palace would be able to hear. Every royal ball, a new stream of gossip flowed among the servants, and the workers all looked forward to what would happen at this next ball.

Though, no one could have ever expected what the hot new topic was this time.

“There's no way, right?!”

“She must be joking!”

“She said she witnessed it herself, just this Entry Hour.”

“Is she truly assigned to their rooms?”

“Someone needs to go check!”

Whispers upon whispers erupted among all the workers of the palace. Maids, butlers, chefs, and guards were all in an uproar over this new, hot scoop that was occurring right before their very eyes.

Most of the royal guests continued sleeping until later in the day because the royal ball usually ended very late. Thus, every Entry Hour following the ball, it was common courtesy to bring breakfast to all the guests’ rooms rather than have them come down to the dining hall. A tray of various teas, desserts, and savory bites would be delivered to the doors of every guest. And, even if the guests were not awake, after three knocks and still no answer, the maid would quietly bring the food in, place it upon a table near the bed, and quickly step out.

However, one maid had rushed down to the kitchen in an absolute frenzy, her cheeks flushed a bright red as she had basically hurled her tray back onto a counter. The chefs were all yelling at her that the food takes a long time to prepare and to bring it back up, but the maid could not bring herself to return to the corridor, which she was assigned to.

“Phainon and the King of Kremnos are sleeping together!”

The news spread like absolute wildfire. The King of Kremnos, who was making his official debut outside of his kingdom, was very well-known for his strength and valor. He was an intimidating presence, with his cold gaze and his obvious show of power, and the servants always kept to themselves whenever he was around. Although he had never treated anyone in the palace with disrespect, no one was willing to be the first person to get on his bad side.

And Phainon, the man who was known all throughout Okhema. He was a hero who worked closely with the ruler of Okhema, Miss Aglaea. But, he was more than just her guard; he never hesitated to help anyone, regardless of status and regardless of the reward. He completed all of his quests faithfully and truthfully, and his success rate was near one hundred percent. It was why everyone called him the Deliverer. Phainon could do almost any impossible feat and could fulfill the hopes and dreams of anyone. He had even slain a dragon, as he had traveled to Styxia long ago to aid in the quest to slay Pollux.

Everyone in Okhema Kingdom knew of Phainon. He was kind, loyal, intelligent, strong, and most of all, he was the most dashing, eligible bachelor among the maids. Almost every maid fell for the sight of him and his radiant smile, and every new maid that was hired in the palace is immediately given some palace ground rules, with one of them being:

“Do not ever approach Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.”

He was held on a pedestal, hailed to be beloved by all. If anyone could be crowned a knight without noble blood, the first person in line would be Phainon. The only thing stopping him from achieving so much greatness was his blood, and all of the common citizens in Okhema despised the Council of Elders for that reason, as the Council of Elders only focused on representing the nobility. Phainon represented the common people, and it was he who gave all the commoners hope that, no matter one's blood or background, one could still become a hero known throughout the land. The commoners all hailed him as their true hero, and it was for this reason that he was absolutely off-limits to everyone. For someone who has achieved so much greatness in life, he is a man who should be appreciated and loved by all and never by just one.

They all knew Phainon was tasked with accompanying the Kremnoan envoys as their guard, but never in a millennium would they have expected this kind of development.

You could press your ear against the door and hear everything! No one answered my three knocks, so I tried to bring the food inside only to run into them… them… As they were…” The maid's face bloomed a bright red once more as she shut her eyes. She couldn't wipe the memory from her mind even if she tried.

As he felt Mydei's breathing even out as he fell into a deep slumber against his chest, Phainon continued tangling his fingertips within golden strands, whispering into the air.

“I love you, Mydei.”

chapters.title: Itinerary Day 6: Aglaea's Proposal, Again
chapters.html:
Phainon was getting used to the sight of the elaborately decorated ceiling above him now. He didn't think it would be a sight he would ever become accustomed to, but here he was, opening his eyes in the midst of Entry Hour to that grand chandelier above him once again.

Mydei had an arm thrown over Phainon's abdomen with his head resting on Phainon's chest. From the angle that Phainon was seeing, he couldn't tell if Mydei was awake or not because his face was turned away from him; he could only watch his head of golden hair rise and fall with each one of Phainon's breaths. Phainon watched, mesmerized, as the morning sunlight peeking through the windows only served to illuminate his golden hair. As if he were wearing this golden crown or even a halo around his head, it was as if nature itself recognised Mydei in all his glory and royalty.

He brought a hand up to run his fingertips through his soft, glowing strands but jumped when Mydei shifted in his place. Lifting his head up toward his face, Phainon could now see Mydei’s somewhat drowsy expression.

“You're awake.”

“That, I am,” Mydei mumbled. “For a while.”

“Did I keep you waiting?” Phainon teased with a smile, lowering his hand onto Mydei's head.

Much to Phainon’s surprise, Mydei was completely serious when he huffed, “You did.”

“I… I did?” Slightly taken aback, Phainon pointed a hesitant finger at himself.

Mydei scoffed while narrowing his eyes. “Every day upon awakening, you were never to be found in my bed.”

“I…” Phainon frowned, furrowing his eyebrows to recall where he had gone while he was staying in Mydei's bedroom. The first day he stayed in this room, he had gotten up to prepare for the royal ball, only for Mydei to drag him back into bed. The second day, he had gotten up to tidy the room. He did return to the room to see him sitting upright in bed after passing the sheets to Empousa–was he looking for Phainon the entire time he was gone?

Phainon's shoulders went slack. “Oh.”

“Is that all you have to say to me?”

“You…” Phainon couldn't even believe the thought that had popped into his head. There was no way, right? “Were you waiting to wake up in bed with me these last few days?”

“The better question is, why do you have so much to do in the morning?” Mydei had pushed himself off of Phainon's chest, and before Phainon could respond, Mydei had draped his upper body to hover over Phainon with his lips ghosting over his.

He couldn't help his line of sight from dropping to Mydei's lips as he felt them faintly brush against his, and a breath caught in Phainon's throat when a chuckle sounded from the man above him.

“Choosing not to answer me?” Mydei smirked.

“I…” Phainon's voice died in his throat as his eyes struggled to focus on either his brightly glowing eyes or the teasing lips that continued to brush against his with every syllable they exchanged. “Well, I–mmm!”

His thoughts were silenced when those enticing lips pressed into his, and Phainon's eyes immediately fluttered shut as a moan escaped his throat. Mydei’s fingers had intertwined with Phainon's, pinning him down into the bed underneath them as he deepened the kiss. Phainon's brain melted with every movement of his lips, and his stomach twisted in pleasure at every sound their connected lips emitted.

Phainon slipped his fingers from Mydei's and grasped his waist, and a soft moan slipped from the lips pressing down on him as Phainon felt the delicious curves upon Mydei's body. He couldn't get enough of Mydei's enticing body as he swirled his fingertips upon his hips, the arch of his back, and even ran his fingers upwards to reach as far as the middle of his back.

The man jolted at the touch and pulled back from the kiss. Phainon was in a daze when they finally parted, warm breath tickling his lips as Mydei panted for breath. He stared up at Mydei who just looked absolutely dazzling over him, with his slightly disheveled bedhead, bruised lips, and dilated golden eyes.

“That spot.” Mydei reached behind him to grasp Phainon's fingers, which were still pressing down the middle of his back. “Not too hard.”

“Does it hurt here?” Phainon gently circled his fingers over that spot, earning a shiver from the man above him.

“It's…” Mydei was panting merely from Phainon teasing this small patch in the middle of his back. “I already explained to you that no harm can befall my body.”

Phainon only nodded silently, stilling his fingers that were teasing his back.

“And, you questioned whether this body truly could never be harmed. The truth is that this spot–” Mydei pressed their fingers down against his spine, and he deeply exhaled at the sensation. “–is the only spot that can be harmed. Drive your blade through this spot, and my life will end.”

Phainon almost ripped his fingers away from his back as if it were a burning fire, but Mydei's tight grasp kept him in place. “So, that means you are sensitive here?”

Mydei nodded, wincing when Phainon hesitantly resumed his ministrations upon his back. “So, not too hard.”

“Do the others know?”

“My people only know that my body is immortal, not of this spot on my tenth thoracic vertebrae. No one outside of Kremnos, besides you, knows of my body's disposition.”

Phainon could only imagine the advantages Kremnos Kingdom held merely by having a basically indestructible monarch. Of course, it was something that they could not easily let slip to other lands. The number of people who would even attempt to exploit his disposition and even his weakness would be immeasurable.

“And, you are trusting me with this knowledge?”

Mydei smirked, bending down and brushing his lips upon his once more. “If you are to return to Kremnos with me, you ought to know this information as my guard.”

They locked their lips together once more in a much more heated exchange than before. Relentlessly, Phainon continued teasing that spot on his back, earning him long moans vibrating against him as Mydei arched his back at every press against his spine. He grasped his hands upon Phainon's shoulders, shaking above him as Phainon slipped his tongue between his lips, swirling inside his warm mouth, and sliding his tongue against Mydei's.

Mydei panted into the kiss, refusing to acquiesce to Phainon's actions. He darted his tongue back, tangling their tongues together as they exchanged saliva between them. Phainon couldn't get enough of Mydei's taste as the sounds of their heated kiss reverberated through his brain. With one hand teasing Mydei's back and another grasping his waist, he was almost tempted to pull Mydei onto his lap and resume their prior competition that currently held no winner.

“Don't we have things to do today, Deliverer?” Mydei parted their lips and cocked his head to the side with an amused smile.

Phainon was too busy trailing the string of saliva that connected their lips together as it led back into that warm cavern that he was still craving the taste of. Mydei's warm breath continued to ghost over his lips as Phainon was locked in a trance, wondering why they had even stopped kissing in the first place.

At that thought, it was as if Phainon finally snapped out of his stupor as he scrambled in his mind for any semblance of sanity. “We–uh–Aglaea! Yes, we are to meet with Aglaea later today.”

Phainon swiped the back of his hand over his mouth and scrambled out of bed, faintly hearing Mydei laughing at him in the background. He was whipping his head around, still slightly in a daze, and he realized he was still adorned in his previous ball attire from two days ago.

“I should return to the barracks to get my uniform.”

Before he could make a mad dash toward his belongings in the barracks, Mydei's voice stopped him.

“Why? We already had this uniform cleaned for you.” He gestured to the remaining belts and armor that were meticulously placed on the desk. “You might as well just use this outfit.”

“Well…” Phainon solemnly glanced at the armor neatly organized together. “This armor is more befitting a Knight's on a day-to-day basis. Now that the ball is over, there's no need for me to wear such extravagant pieces."

“You're the Deliverer, are you not?” Mydei had already left the bed and begun untangling all the belts and buckles. “Come. I will help you put these on.”

“Mydei, there's really no need–”

“Come.”

As if someone had taken over his body, Phainon rigidly met Mydei's side, sitting himself down in the desk chair while Mydei figured out where all the extra attachments belonged. With the two of them, it took a much faster time to become completely adorned in the full outfit compared to when it had taken multiple quints for Phainon to wear it all by himself. Even so, it was Lucid Hour by the time the two of them were both fully dressed and ready to depart from the bedroom.

Mydei stepped back while Phainon was once again adorned in the fanciest white and blue armor he had ever seen. He still felt a bit uncomfortable, as it was so drastically different from his usual uniform, but he knew Mydei wouldn't allow him even a brief moment of escape back to the barracks to retrieve his normal attire.

“You look good,” Mydei stated. “So, stop overthinking.”

Phainon couldn't tear his eyes away from the leather gauntlets adorning his hands, or the white sleeves embellished in gold that ran down his arms. “I'm not overthinking it. It's just…” What was the right word? Not normal? Unusual? Unfitting? It felt more like Phainon was dressing up in a costume rather than wearing clothes.

“Stop looking at yourself and get up.” Mydei had shoved a knee in between Phainon's legs, and the change in scenery broke Phainon's thoughts. “Let's go.”

Trailing the knee that had slotted itself between his legs, Phainon's eyes ran up his thighs, torso, and neck to finally reach golden eyes peering down on him. He shook his head, clearing his thoughts and pushing himself up from his seat. “You're right. Let's go.”

They met with the Kremnan attendants outside in the corridor, and Phainon led them once more to the dining hall on the lower floor. It was quite the peaceful day, as the attendants had one last full day before returning home, and they were free to do whatever they pleased while Mydei spent a part of his day speaking with Aglaea. Phainon was running the itinerary through his head as he shoveled his breakfast down, not really paying attention to what was set in front of him.

Phainon was to bring Mydei to Aglaea’s office after breakfast, so Phainon would be free until Aglaea called him back. He will probably help accompany the Kremnoan attendants if they decide to venture elsewhere around the city. Regarding whether he would stay in Okhema or join Mydei in Kremnos would have to be a conversation he would have to have with Aglaea later on in the day, when they were both freer. He wasn't sure what to expect from that conversation, and he didn't want to think about it. Just thinking about it made his stomach churn.

“Eat properly, HKS.”

Phainon's head shot up to the view in front of him upon hearing the Kremnoan word, and he was met with a scowl.

His eyes widened in confusion. “Sorry?”

“I don't want to eat with someone who cannot appreciate the food that is being served to them.”

Phainon blinked blankly at the man in front of him before glancing down at the food he had already eaten half of without actually knowing what he was shoving into his mouth.

It was a bowl of steaming vegetable potage. Filled with cabbage and potatoes that were slow-cooked to become this filling stew, the taste was light enough to be perfectly suitable for breakfast yet satiating enough to power oneself for the rest of the day. Served off to the side in a separate dishwear were an assortment of salads and bread to eat with the potage, and a pitcher made of sterling silver which Phainon could only assume housed Mydei's beloved pomegranate milk concoction.

He let out a breath he didn't know he was holding as he stared down at his food, his tensed shoulders slowly relaxing. Mydei was right; he can eat and enjoy the food now and worry about all of his problems afterwards.

Taking a deep breath, Phainon took a much more appropriately-sized bite this time. Though, he wasn't sure why he was staring at Mydei while doing so. Maybe it was his way of letting him know Phainon had heard and understood his words?

The man in front of him smiled, tilting his head to the side without breaking eye contact. “Good boy.”

Phainon struggled to hold down a cough at his words, his face blooming a bright red as his eyes immediately shot back down to his bowl. He was still struggling to swallow the food he had in his mouth, but it was so hard to breathe as Mydei's words continued to echo in his mind. He had faintly caught the eyes of the Kremnoan attendants, who all looked a mix of either bashful or proud at their exchange.

They all finished with the rest of their meal, and Phainon thanked the maids who had rushed in to quickly clean up the table as they departed from the dining hall. Okheman soldiers met with them outside the dining hall and accompanied the rest of the Kremnoan attendants, while two Kremnoan attendants stayed behind with Mydei as Phainon led them back again to Aglaea's office.

It was nearing the end of Lucid Hour when Phainon brought a fist up to gently knock on the wooden door leading to Aglaea's office. When he faintly heard a female voice sound through the door, Phainon turned to Mydei.

“Well, I'll return once Miss Aglaea calls for me.” He nodded with a smile at Mydei, who only raised an eyebrow at his statement. “I'll see you later, Mydei.”

“Where do you think you're going?” Mydei crossed his arms, tilting his head to the side with a scowl upon his lips.

“Where?” Phainon frowned as his eyes wandered above him. “I didn't think about it yet. I was thinking maybe I'd accompany the rest of the Kremnoan attendants?”

Mydei scoffed. “I thought we were speaking with Aglaea. Together. Or did that conversation mean nothing to you?”

“Well, I…” Of course, Phainon remembered that conversation. He could never forget any conversation he had with Mydei. “I just thought you two would be discussing her proposal first–something that I shouldn't be there for.”

“And why shouldn't you be there?”

“Well, does it not concern classified information about both kingdoms?”

“Nothing about my kingdom is classified to you, Phainon.”

Phainon probably would've pinned Mydei to the wall right then and there if the other two Kremnoan attendants were not standing off to the side from them. A blush bloomed across his cheeks as he averted his gaze, ignoring the pounding of his heart that resounded loudly in his chest.

“I… see. Then, if you will have me, I will join you inside.”

Mydei nodded with a smile, gesturing to Phainon to proceed with opening the door. As Phainon did so, he was greeted with the cold air that was circulating inside the office, and two pairs of eyes met his.

“Miss Aglaea. And–” His eyes shifted to the other individual in the room. “–Professor Anaxa.”

A narrowed eye shot his way. “That is Anaxagoras to you.”

“Phainon.” Aglaea's gentle voice resounded through the room. “Thank you for bringing the King here for me.”

“It's my pleasure.” He returned the smile, gesturing for Mydei to continue into the room. As Mydei and the two Kremnoan attendants entered, Phainon felt awkward lingering in the room with such high-profile guests, and he had almost pivoted on his feet to rush out of the room if Mydei's voice did not stop him.

“I would like Phainon to stay, if that is fine with you.”

Phainon gulped. There was his one and only chance of escape, now gone with the wind. Hesitantly and anxiously, Phainon studied Aglaea's reaction, and he inwardly winced at how her polite and pleasant smile had grown into a knowing grin.

“Of course, King Mydeimos.” She waved her hand for Phainon to shut the office door, which he complied with. With the sound of the door locking shut, suddenly, the gravity of the situation fell upon his shoulders as his eyes wavered between the three other individuals in the room.

“I assume you have reviewed my proposal, King Mydeimos?”

Mydei scoffed, crossing his arms. “I'd like to hear if you have a plan first before I so readily throw my people to join your cause.”

Aglaea's golden eyes twinkled under the morning sunlight streaming through the grand window behind her. “Of course. I will do my very best.”

She abruptly stood up, the sound of her office chair sliding against the rug under her golden heels as she spread a scroll upon her desk. Phainon hadn't the least clue what could possibly be on that scroll as Mydei approached her side to peer closer.

“Every year, I and many citizens of Okhema attend an assembly with the Council of Elders,” She began to explain. “Every year, the assembly consists of reviewing government legislation in the form of debates. It may be laws that need approval or codes that need to be re-reviewed. However, this year, I plan to bring up the power of the Council of Elders themselves.”

Mydei raised an eyebrow, his gaze still glued to the opened scroll. “And, you are allowed to question the Council of Elders like so? That makes me question why no one has done it before.”

“Although participating citizens are allowed to vote, they cannot raise the laws they wish to discuss,” Aglaea answered. “Only the Council of Elders comes prepared with the discussed legislation for the day.”

“So, how will you bring up the topic of the Council of Elders if only the Council of Elders themselves bring the discussions?”

“With me,” Anaxa interjected, earning an inquisitive glance from the King.

“You see.” Aglaea stared in Anaxa's direction with a smile. “The Council of Elders is aware that the professor and I do not see eye-to-eye on… certain topics. However, that makes it easier for us to infiltrate the Council of Elders themselves.”

“The Council of Elders plans to question Aglaea's rule during this year's debate,” Anaxa added. “And to win the majority vote of banishing Aglaea from the government, they plan to win by involving the Grove and Styxia.”

“Styxia as well?” Mydei finally tore his eyes from the scroll to land on the one-eyed professor.

“Castorice is currently entertaining the Elders as they please,” Anaxa muttered. “They believe she has truly aligned goals with the Council because she was my student.”

“They plan to unite the kingdoms surrounding Okhema to remove me entirely.” Aglaea chuckled. “They believe they can override Fate with numbers. Once the discussion is brought up by the Council of Elders, we plan, in the debate, to turn it around onto them instead.”

“So, you plan to use the debate to strip them of their power?” Mydei narrowed his eyes. “Is there a guarantee you can win the participating citizens’ votes?”

“There is.” With that knowing smile plastered across Aglaea's face, a hand was waved in Phainon's direction, and he was suddenly taken aback that he was being dragged into the conversation. “The Deliverer may be convincing enough for the common people to vote.”

“Hah! And that is why you need Kremnos.” Mydei's smirk landed upon Phainon. “A specific regiment built behind the Deliverer and backed by the Kremnoans. Is that the real reason Phainon is my guard? Not to see his stagnated potential, but because he is the Deliverer with the power of the common people beside him?”

Phainon's mind was swirling over the back and forth that was occurring in this office. What were they even talking about? A specific regiment? And Phainon was going to be in charge of it? What did he mean by it being “backed by the Kremnoans”? Was this the proposal Aglaea had discussed with him previously? And, did everyone actually refer to him as the Deliverer? He swore he never heard that title as often as he did until this week.

Aglaea continued to smile. “I do believe you have been enjoying my choice of guard for you. I am sure you have no right to complain about him.”

Mydei scoffed again, refusing to answer to her implications. “With the power of the Grove and Styxia to fool the Council of Elders and turn the tides of the debate, the Deliverer and Kremnos will win the common people's vote. That is your plan?”

“With the Deliverer being backed by the kingdom with the strongest military might in all of Amphoreus, I am sure no further convincing would be needed for the common people to vote in Phainon's favor.” Aglaea rolled up the scroll on her desk with a satisfactory smile. “Previously, Phainon could not rally any support against the Council as someone born without noble blood, but with the King of Kremnos at his side, that is an entirely different story. So, how about it, King Mydeimos? Military might in exchange for the safety of your people.”

With a sigh, an unreadable gaze landed upon Phainon. “I see no reason to refuse, assuming you keep your end of the deal. I see no reason not to work with the Deliverer. Although I wonder–” Mydei's gaze shifted to Anaxa. “– what you would get out of this scheme, as someone who is not in favor of Aglaea either.”

“If given the choice of the Council of Elders rule or Aglaea's rule, there is but a simple answer.” Anaxa sighed heavily. “I do not associate with stupidity, nor do I associate with blind devotion. Their unnecessary praise for noble blood is something that I have never agreed with since the start.”

“I am glad we are on the same page about something,” Aglaea chuckled.

“Do not joke with me.” Anaxa clicked his tongue.

With a breath, Aglaea seated herself back into her office chair. “If that is settled, then I will begin preparing the necessary documents to solidify our alliance, King Mydeimos. I will have them sent to you in Kremnos in time for the debate. In the meantime, if you have any further questions, please deliver them to my guard. And, professor, thank you for joining us today.”

Anaxa nodded and immediately fled the room as if he could not stand being in there any longer. Phainon, however, was still in a daze over the previous conversation. He felt he was missing certain pieces that made the entire plan make no sense. All he could truly understand was that Aglaea planned to overthrow the Council of Elders in the upcoming debate a few months from now, and the Grove, Styxia, and Kremnos Kingdom were all uniting under that front. And somehow, Phainon was being dragged into this as well.

“Did you come here with plans to already join the alliance, King Mydeimos?” Aglaea twirled the quill pen that balanced between her lithe fingers. “I hope our previous conversation helped you come to a decision today.”

“I cannot agree to a plan that I do not know what you want with my people.”

“Is that so?” She tilted her head to the side. “Pardon me, but I believe you agreed quite readily.”

“Hmph, I just don't see any reason not to cooperate if no harm falls upon my people.” Mydei crossed his arms across his chest. “Some of my attendants have already taken a liking to the Deliverer. It doesn't seem like I will have to force them to support him or stand by his side.”

“Do they now?” Aglaea raised an eyebrow, her polite smile never leaving her lips. “It seems the Deliverer is really completing all of his duties.”

Phainon could only widen his eyes and smile nervously under Aglaea's piercing gaze. He still wasn't completely sure what exactly they were discussing.

Mydei stepped up to Aglaea's desk, where Aglaea looked less than surprised upon him overstaying his visit.

“And to what do I owe your presence, King Mydeimos?” That knowing smirk of hers returned as she gazed upward at Mydei.

“Phainon will be returning with me to Kremnos.”

Phainon almost had to throw a hand up to his chin to stop his jaw from dropping to the floor. He was just going to bring it up just like that?! No segue?!

Aglaea chuckled. “Of course, King Mydeimos. How else will Phainon return in time for the assembly with the military might of Kremnos backing him?”

“Pardon?” Phainon blurted before he could shut his mouth. Why wasn't she the least bit surprised by this development?

She grinned in his direction. “I am just approving your indefinite leave for Kremnos.” Aglaea waved the quill in her hand. “Your leave will be on the grounds of improving battle strategies, war tactics, and formations, and combat skills in the city of Castrum Kremnos, capital of Kremnos Kingdom.”

Phainon's eyes widened in shock. “You… knew I would want to leave?”

“If you didn't want to leave yourself by the end of this week, I would have to convince you myself,” Aglaea stated. “I cannot have you be present at the assembly without having set foot in Kremnos Kingdom. No one would be convinced otherwise that you have the support of the Kremnoans. Was that all, Phainon?”

With the gears turning in his head, Phainon replayed the last few quints, no, the entire last few days in his head, recalling every interaction he had during this week ever since the Kremnoans arrived. “Did you plan for this?”

Aglaea's smile only stayed consistent. “I can only plan, but I cannot force any entity to join arms with me. That all fell upon you, Phainon.” As she spoke these words, her eyes grazed over Phainon's body, and she added, “I am very glad you like your new uniform. It is much more befitting of your status than the usual dreary attire.”

With those last words, Phainon, Mydei, and the two Kremnoan attendants exited the office. Phainon was still in quite a daze from the entire exchange that had just occurred right before him, and he shut the office door behind him, only instinctively letting go of the door handle when he heard the click of the locking door.

“I am sure you have questions.”

Phainon shook himself out of his daze to return Mydei's stare. Although he was correct in that he had many questions swirling in his mind, he thought to start with this first mystery. “What was the proposal Miss Aglaea had for you?”

“Walk with me,” was all Mydei answered. He strolled down the corridor, and Phainon had to quickly hurry to catch up with him.

“Where would you like me to take you?”

“Where else?” The smirk that Mydei sent his way made Phainon's blood pump in anticipation. “The training grounds.”

With a laugh, Phainon led the way to the training grounds with the two Kremnoan attendants in tow while Mydei explained the entirety of Aglaea's plan, answering all of Phainon's questions in the process. Her plan would ultimately conclude with the end of the Council of Elders, and with the Council of Elders falsely believing that Styxia and the Grove were on their side, Aglaea would turn the debate around on them and use the support of Styxia and the Grove to support her once the Council of Elders questions Aglaea's position in Okhema.

Winning the majority vote of the citizens fell upon Phainon, who was being supported by Kremnos, which was a way for the citizens to feel self-assured in placing their vote for someone with no noble backing. Mydei also explained the Black Tide monsters that were multiplying rapidly outside Kremnos's borders, and he was looking for different places to move his people to in the case that their borders fell to the monsters. Although they were fending them off just fine for now, he couldn't say the same in a few years, and he was planning for the worst. That was what Mydei was getting in exchange for his support in overthrowing the Council of Elders.

Phainon couldn't believe such an elaborate plan had been developed in the background the entire week Phainon was accompanying the Kremnoans around Okhema. But for Aglaea, such a feat was but an everyday task. It was one thing out of many that Phainon admired her for as a leader.

Pushing open the heavy doors of the training grounds, Phainon was shocked to see that there were people already in there. He was so used to seeing the grounds always entirely vacant, so this was the most activity he had ever seen in this place.

“Phainon!” Empousa waved from the middle of the training grounds once the doors abruptly shut behind them. She and the other Kremnoans were sparring in the training grounds, and the whole area was bustling with activity as Phainon could catch them swinging their wooden weapons and dodging here and there.

Phainon could only glance at Mydei in absolute shock, and Mydei was clearly fighting the urge to stifle a laugh at his dumbfounded expression.

“You said you wanted to spar with my attendants, correct?” Mydei cleared his throat in another attempt to hold in his laughter. “I thought to give you the chance while you have the home advantage.

With a large grin all over his face, Phainon laughed loudly, grabbing Mydei's arm and dragging him down to the training grounds. The Kremnoan attendants were quite shocked that the King would let someone drag him around like so, but they also noticed how pleased their King looked at the action as Phainon began digging through the leftover wooden swords.

Phainon pushed Mydei onto the training grounds, and the two split into teams. With Mydei leading one team and Phainon leading the other, the two teams had an all-out brawl in the training grounds, betting on who would best the other first. It was absolute chaos with a multitude of weapons swinging in the air, dirt being kicked up and clouding their vision, and constantly dodging the limbs of all the people on the training grounds, but Phainon couldn't argue against the fact that it was the most fun he had had in quite a long time. He was always practicing his swings by himself every day, and it was refreshing being able to go all out against other people who were just as eager as he was.

The quints passed by just like that. Action Hour soon turned to Parting Hour, and Phainon and the Kremnoans were still outside, drenched in a mixture of dirt and sweat, as they neared the end of another brawl. Phainon had learned a lot about the ways the Kremnoans would study their opponents and how they would approach different types of fighters, yet the score was still tied by the time most of the attendants had collapsed onto the floor in complete and utter exhaustion.

Shadows were stretched all along the training grounds as the sun lowered underneath the horizon, signalling that they were now more than halfway through Parting Hour. With an orange glow cast among everything in the sun's path, a draw was ultimately announced. Phainon was gasping for breath, struggling to even stay on both of his feet as the wooden sword threatened to slip from his loose grip. He had never had to fight with such gusto for so long before, besides the arduous missions he took on outside Okhema’s borders, and he felt just as exhausted as the Kremnoans strewn all over the floor. He watched each one of them also gasping for breath, their chests desperately rising and falling for air.

With one last deep breath, Phainon swept the bangs out of his eyes and looked over at Mydei, who was also just as exhausted. He was wearing the same attire that he had arrived in on the first day, minus the royal sash, so Phainon had a clear view of his half-exposed torso that dripped with rivulets of sweat, lining each and every curve of muscle on Mydei's body. With the sunset behind them that only emphasized the shapes of his strongly built body, Phainon couldn't help but watch each and every droplet of sweat that ran down his body, lining his pectorals down to his abdomen and disappearing into the waistline that left Phainon desperately wanting more.

He swallowed dryly, averting his gaze. He could not be having such thoughts in the training grounds, and in front of everyone else, no less.

“Woo!” Empousa broke the silence with a loud, breathy cheer. She was sprawled out on the floor by Phainon's feet; she was quite adamant about joining Phainon's team when they were splitting into two groups. “You're good, Phainon! Really… really good.” She began catching her breath again in between short laughs, wiping the sweat and dirt off her forehead that only served to smear it all along her face. “I see why King Mydeimos likes you so much.”

“Truly… your stamina is quite a wonder.” Herklas was kneeling on Phainon's other side and was also a member of Phainon's team. The statement briefly reminded Phainon that Herklas shared a room with Empousa, which was right next door to Mydei’s, and he had to quickly wipe away the thought before the shame enveloped him at the double meaning of Herklas's words.

Phainon could only let out a breathy laugh. “You guys aren't too bad yourself! I learned a lot about the Kremnoan art of war.”

“I'm glad you were able to enjoy yourself,” Empousa huffed. “But please help me off the floor because I cannot do it myself.”

With another laugh, Herklas and Phainon each took a hand to pull her up from the floor. As she was dusting herself off from the remaining dirt that clung to her clothes, Phainon turned to Mydei and the rest of his team with a smile.

“Did you guys want to enjoy some of Okhema's famous public baths?”

Excited gasps resounded between the two teams, with Phainon taking that as a sign of agreement. They spent the rest of the quint cleaning up the training grounds, righting all the dummies that were thrown out of the way for their group sparring sessions, and organizing the wooden weapons that they took. With the rest of Parting Hour at their disposal, Phainon led their disheveled group over to the public baths to begin washing up.

It was a vast indoor space filled with small waterfalls and pools of glistening, heated water. In the center of all the connected baths was a grand fountain that many children enjoyed playing in, and many speakers would deliver speeches on top of the fountain. The floors leading up to the baths were made of pristine marble that shone under all the excess water that splashed upon its surface, and the warm lighting from the various lamps set up around the indoor space gave the bath a soft, angelic glow that mixed in with the steam emitting from the water.

Phainon was glad he was able to take the attendants here at least once before they departed, because none of the Kremnoans could get over the grand sight before them. It was what Okhema was famous for, after all, and it would be a shame if they missed out on what many travelers visited Okhema for.

The Kremnoan attendants excitedly tore off their marred clothing, grabbing the robes and towels that were provided by the bath attendants and exploring the vast baths in front of them. Phainon chuckled at their excitement and anticipation as they wandered around like curious children and admired the various sights set before them. They were particularly excited about the fountain in the middle and the waterfalls that they could stand under, and as it was now Parting Hour and nearing the day's end, there weren't many people around to get in the way of their antics.

“You're not going to join them?” Phainon shot Mydei a smile, gesturing to his attendants who were floundering about.

“They deserve this moment of rest before we depart tomorrow.” Mydei watched the Kremnoans scattered throughout the bath with a small smile. “They don't need their King to be breathing down on them during this time of respite.”

“I don't think any of them think of you in that manner.” Phainon had to stifle a laugh when he caught Herklas and Georgious dumping a pile of water onto Empousa’s head. “They all love and respect you, both as their King and also as their greatest fighter. I don't believe they think of you so much as a stern figure whom they cannot enjoy life with.”

Mydei's eyes caught the marble tiling underneath their feet as he digested those words. “Let us get ready for the baths.”

They each grabbed their own provided towel and robe, stripping themselves of their own dirty clothing and handing it to the bath attendants to take for a cleaning. Phainon was getting quite accustomed to the excess accessories on this new uniform, and he was able to remove all the armor and belts with much more ease than he was used to. Thanking them, they proceeded to one of the more secluded baths within a corner of the area. It was much quieter, and they could peacefully watch over the other Kremnoans splashing about in the other pools of water.

Phainon lowered himself into the bath with a contented sigh as the warm water enveloped his body. Mydei followed suit beside him, and Phainon couldn't help but watch the water blanket his built body. Grazing his body with his eyes, Phainon noticed the marks that Phainon had left all over him had healed already, and his body had returned to being completely unscathed, both from their activities from yesterday and that night, and also from their spar from earlier. He was more amazed that such a feat could occur, but magic was always something Phainon was amazed by.

“HKS.”

The deep voice interrupted his thoughts, and Phainon was immediately met with glaring golden eyes and a light blush across Mydei's cheeks.

“Sorry?”

“You're staring.” Mydei's glare only grew when Phainon widened his eyes. “Quite obviously, in fact.”

“Sorry!” Phainon raised his hands out of the water, but it only resulted in splashing water everywhere. “I wasn't exactly looking at you or anything; I was just simply thinking about your… magic.”

With a hmph, Mydei averted his gaze and relaxed his body against the wall of the bath behind him. “I wouldn't mind if you were staring, Deliverer. You are just making it too obvious.”

A loud cough erupted from Phainon's throat at the comment, his cheeks equally blooming a deep red as he attempted to settle against the wall beside Mydei. Nonetheless, it was to no avail, because he was way too nervous with how their shoulders faintly brushed against each other, and they were completely bare aside from a single towel underneath the water that draped across each of their laps. Every breath sent their shoulders ghosting against the other's, and it only served to remind Phainon of their close proximity and their lack of clothing.

He chanced a brief glance at Mydei, and he had his head thrown back, resting against the marble tile of the floor with his back lounging against the walls of the bath. Golden hair was spread on the marble tile and messily stuck to his neck and shoulders. His eyes were shut as he reveled in the warm water surrounding his body, and especially after the workout that they had in the training grounds, Phainon could see why he was in such bliss. Phainon would be feeling the same way if he weren't feeling so antsy over their proximity.

Once Phainon had caught his eyes trailing down the rivulets of bath water that ran down his exposed neck and pooled down to his collar bones, tracing his red tattoos, Phainon had to rip his gaze away or else he would get too excited. Maybe he shouldn't have invited the Kremnoans to attend the public baths; he felt as if he were fighting for his life here and struggling to stay sane. Or maybe he should've invited just Mydei during Curtain-Fall Hour, where no one would interrupt them.

Phainon violently shook his head at the incredulous thought. Was he crazy?! Did his mind just insinuate such activities in a public setting?! Well, he did masturbate in here, so it wouldn't be the first time. Wait, no, Phainon needed to get all these vulgar thoughts out of his mind. There was no way he could entertain such ideas, especially with the person of all his affection sitting right beside him.

“HKS.”

The deep voice came again, cutting through his running thoughts. Phainon whirled around and saw Mydei pushing golden hair out of his face and swiping his hand across his eyes. Oops–Phainon must've splashed water on him when he shook his head earlier.

“Sorry!” Phainon immediately moved to swipe Mydei's hand away from his face as Phainon took the liberty of clearing the extra water droplets that had splashed onto him.

Mydei scowled, his cheeks resting in the palms of Phainon's hands. “What could you possibly be thinking about to be shaking your head like so?”

“Uh…” Phainon drawled, his gaze wavering under Mydei's narrowed eyes. He offered a small, clearly unconvincing smile. “Nothing a king such as yourself should worry yourself with.”

“And if I weren't a king?”

“Then it would be nothing a beautiful, handsome man such as yourself should be worrying himself with.”

Mydei scoffed at the idiotic response, letting his chin rest in Phainon's palms. “You speak as if you don't have a brain.”

“My brain only concerns thoughts of you, King Mydeimos.”

“Spare me the pleasantries.”

“It is nothing but the truth.” Phainon smiled as Mydei's eyes fluttered closed. He gently rubbed his thumbs into Mydei's cheeks, cradling Mydei's face in his hands.

“Then tell me,” Mydei continued with his eyes still shut, “what you were thinking about that made you shake like a wet dog.”

Phainon hummed, debating whether he should actually tell Mydei the truth or not. Though, he was curious to see what kind of reaction he would evoke from the other man. Phainon leaned down, bringing Mydei's face closer to his and brushing the tips of their noses together. At the sudden movement, Mydei opened his eyes and stared into Phainon.

In a hushed voice, so quiet that only the two of them could hear, Phainon revealed his innermost thoughts: “I was thinking about how I wanted to take you for myself right here and now, Mydei.”

He didn't even realize what had happened after that; he could barely register almost being drowned and being enveloped by a copious amount of water. He barely registered flailing for breath, and he also barely registered two large hands either smacking his head or shoving his shoulders. Phainon, gasping for breath in an attempt to resurface, was left as just a pair of thrashing arms above the surface as he fought with all his might against Mydei. Although, Phainon was failing quite miserably since Mydei had the advantage of moving first and catching Phainon completely off guard.

Suddenly, their altercation turned into wrestling, as Phainon's attempts to resurface did not work. Since that wasn't working, he, instead, opted to drag Mydei underneath the water with him, and soon the two began throwing their arms and hands against each other, pulling and tugging at anything their hands could manage to grab in an attempt to pull the other under the water. Their towels were discarded from the mess of moving limbs as Mydei and Phainon kicked and pulled in the bath, splashing water all over the marble tiles to become the victor in this brawl.

Phainon could faintly make out hoots and hollers in the background every time he managed to resurface and breathe in the open air, but it was short-lived as he was quickly shoved back into the water every time, immersing himself back into silence under the water. He wasn't sure how long they had been wrestling under the water to keep one of them submerged for longer than a few beats, but the nearby bath attendants all scrambled to separate the two.

He was gasping desperately for air now that he could sit upright in the bath again; Mydei was mirroring his exact movements right across from him, his bare shoulders shaking with every breath. His hair was drenched and flat against his head, tangled this way and that from the altercation. Phainon was sure he didn't look any better.

Waving the concerned bath attendants away with a reassuring smile, Phainon pushed the hair out of his eyes with a hearty laugh. “I told you not to concern yourself with my thoughts, King Mydeimos.”

“How was I supposed to know you would have such obscene thoughts?” Mydei hissed back, running an impatient hand through his hair and slicking his golden bangs back. “We are in a public area, HKS.”

“That didn't stop me before,” Phainon mumbled, but he didn't realize that he had let it slip until he felt a hard kick to his shin under the water.

“Ow!”

“You what?”

“Mydei, that hurt!”

“Didn’t stop you from what?”

Mydei was seething as he approached him from the other side of the bath. He looked absolutely ready to shove Phainon back into the water and resume what the bath attendants had previously broken up.

“Wait, wait, Mydei, I'll explain!” Phainon had thrown his hands up into the air once more, splashing water onto Mydei's torso in an attempt to separate them. “I… I…”

“You have exactly 3 seconds to explain, HKS.”

“It was just–”

“Three.”

“It was just the heat of the moment–”

“Two.”

“I couldn't–"

“One.”

“I was by myself!”

That made Mydei pause in front of him, and Phainon's shoulders relaxed once he realized it had worked.

The golden-haired man sighed exasperatedly, lowering his hands that were ready to shove Phainon underneath the surface once again. “You… I thought you had lied to me about your lack of experience.”

“I would never!” Phainon immediately straightened up at the accusation. “I was… truly by myself.”

“So? What did you happen to do here, in such a public area, by yourself?”

Phainon gulped at the revealing question, averting his gaze as his cheeks flushed red. “Well… Did you… really need to know the specifics right now?”

“Hmph.” Mydei crossed his arms. It seemed that he also remembered they were having this sort of conversation in front of others.

As he was settling back down into the bath, a voice called to them from farther down the baths. With both of the men turning in their direction, Phainon noticed Empousa waving at them in the distance. He also noticed that the baths were much emptier now that it was getting late into Parting Hour.

“My King! Phainon!” She started this elaborate gesture of scooping her arms in the air towards her direction, jutting her head to the area beside her and the other attendants.

Phainon laughed, cocking his head at Mydei. “I told you they would want you over there.”

With another hmph, Mydei grabbed his towel and robe and began making his way over, with Phainon following shortly behind. They spent the rest of Parting Hour lounging around in the baths and enjoying the water. Mydei and Phainon actually took the time to clean themselves off of the day’s debris while Empousa and the other attendants excitedly pestered the two of them over who had won the wrestle in the bath. They also asked what they had been discussing in their secluded little corner, to which Mydei seamlessly steered the conversation away into another direction. Phainon, however, couldn't hide the embarrassment that washed over his face, and Empousa spent much of her time teasing Phainon by making up theories of what they could have been talking about.

Their time in the baths was brought to an end when a maid had scrambled inside to inform them that the kitchen would be closing at Curtain-Fall Hour, and if they wanted supper, they should start heading over to the dining hall. Because they had skipped their midday meal, again, due to spending most of their afternoon in the training grounds, the unanimous decision was made to have at least another proper meal before the day ended. Drying themselves off and dressing in their newly washed clothing, Phainon bid the remaining bath attendants goodbye before leading the Kremnoans to their usual dining room.

As they all seated themselves in their usual spots, the servants brought out the night's dinner on silver platters, as usual. Setting the table and presenting the dishes in an orderly fashion, their meal for the day was an entire roasted chicken marinated in a rich gravy sauce and placed upon glistening greens. As it shone in the center of the table under the chandelier lighting, the surrounding platters consisted of various salads and a sweet and creamy pumpkin bean casserole. The steam rose from the chicken and casserole, wafting their delicious scents across the entire table, and everyone heartily dug into the food. Especially after a day's worth of sparring and skipping their midday meal, everyone was looking forward to such a filling dish.

The chicken was extravagantly crispy as Phainon took a large mouthful, yet the meat on the inside was deliciously juicy. The flavor spread wonderfully along his tongue as Phainon indulged himself in more of the rich meat. The spices that the chicken was cooked in mixed well with the tanginess of the lemon that was squeezed on its crispy surface, and the steaming pumpkin bean casserole served on the side was a nice offset to the sourness of the chicken. The salad was a nice touch as well; though, Phainon may be biased simply because he enjoyed salad and thought it should be a staple in every meal.

The entire table was completely silent save for the clatter of their utensils. Everyone ravaged the lavish meal served in front of them as their last full day had finally come to an end. Phainon was sure they would enjoy being able to return to their home kingdom, but he at least hoped they had enjoyed their week's stay in Okhema. This all reminded Phainon that he, too, would be joining them in Kremnos Kingdom. He certainly needed to gather all his belongings together so he was ready to depart with Mydei and the others in the morning, but he definitely wanted to bid some farewells first before he left. The great debate where Aglaea's plans would come to fruition wasn't for another couple of months, which meant Phainon most likely would not return to Okhema until then.

The attending maids quickly removed the cleaned plates, courtesy of everyone who had completely destroyed all the presented food. They had even brought out another serving, to which many of the attendants continued to savor. Phainon smiled as he watched everyone in front of him revel in the food; he was grateful they were enjoying themselves like so.

As they were finishing the last few bites of the food, Mydei had pushed himself up to his feet, and Phainon quickly followed suit. He watched as Mydei gestured to his attendants to continue eating, and all the Kremnoans visibly relaxed in their seats.

“Let us go, Phainon.”

Without waiting for Phainon's response, Mydei had already begun approaching the door to exit the dining hall. As Phainon had already satisfied himself with the food, he scrambled after Mydei, not forgetting to thank all the servants and inform them to take the Kremnoans up to their rooms once they were finished eating.

“You’re not going to wait for your attendants?” Phainon had finally caught up to Mydei's side as he followed him in whichever direction Mydei was taking them to.

“I'm sure they can make it to their rooms themselves.” Mydei continued to walk onward with Phainon in tow.

“What are you in such a rush for that you couldn't wait for them to finish?” Phainon asked this in a curious tone. “And speaking of, where are we going?”

“I recall that we depart this kingdom tomorrow, yet you do not have the least of your belongings with you.”

Phainon's eyes slightly widened. It was as if Mydei could now read his mind. “So, you're taking me–”

“To the soldier's barracks.” Mydei raised an eyebrow in Phainon’s direction. “Unless I am not allowed in there.”

“No!” Phainon blurted out. “You are allowed wherever you wish.”

“Because I am a king, or because I am Mydei?”

“Because you are Mydei,” Phainon confidently and immediately answered with a smile. “If you were only a king to me still, I would be insisting on leading you there myself.”

Mydei scoffed as he continued onward toward the exit of Marmoreal Palace. “You would have.”

Feeling the cool night air against their skin as they stepped into the outside, Phainon took the lead in showing Mydei to the soldier's barracks once they had exited Marmoreal Palace, as Mydei had never been there before and didn't know where it would be. It was nearby since it was directly adjacent to the palace in case an emergency arose, so the soldiers could quickly attend to and defend the palace.

As it was late into Curtain-Fall Hour, most of the soldiers were sleeping, with the exception of the few that were up on guard duty for that quint. Nodding in acknowledgement at the soldiers he happened to cross, Phainon pushed open the shoddy door leading to the shared living space of all the soldiers. Although there were spacious rooms that separated the soldiers within the barracks, there were usually about twenty to thirty soldiers who each crowded into one room. He wasn't sure why exactly Mydei had wanted to join him in packing his belongings, but Phainon couldn't complain about the company.

He led Mydei to the room where he currently resided; for some reason, some of the soldiers were still up and conversing with each other late into the night. They immediately perked up when they saw Phainon, most likely due to the fact that Phainon had not been sleeping here for the past few days. He could tell they were about to greet him, but they quickly cowered when they saw who was behind him.

Phainon just gave them an awkward smile in greeting before returning his attention back to his bed. It was just a single bed with a simple wooden frame on the floor, and all his belongings were either underneath the bed, in a wooden trunk that sat on the floor at the end of his bed, or in the single nightstand that each bed came with.

“Are you helping me bring everything to your room?” Phainon joked as he began emptying his nightstand’s belongings onto his bed. There really wasn’t much in there; all it housed were various appraisal tools, scrolls, books, and stone tablets. Phainon didn’t have the time during this week of being a guard for the Kremnoans, but one of his hobbies was actually antique appraisals and collecting antiques. He was sure the trunk near the foot of his bed contained only a bunch of real and fake antiques he had collected over the years he stayed in Okhema, and he was, unfortunately, prepared to part with some of his beloved antiques so he could move most of his belongings to Kremnos.

“What do you think I’m here for?” Mydei began sorting through all the reading material that Phainon had haphazardly dumped onto his bed, organizing the different materials into separate piles. “Did you think I came here just to watch?”

Phainon froze as he watched Mydei meticulously sorting through his belongings. “I… I was only kidding, Mydei, you don’t have to do that.”

“Do you expect me to just sit here and watch?” Mydei impatiently repeated.

“Well… yeah.”

He scoffed in response, never taking his eyes off the piles of reading materials. “I thought I came here as Mydei.”

“I just thought you wanted to see where I stayed,” Phainon laughed lightly as he resumed digging through his nightstand to ensure he didn’t miss anything. “You don’t have to if you don’t want to.”

“Do you really expect me to sit here and wait if we can complete this faster with the two of us working?” Mydei huffed as he examined one of the appraisal tools in his hand. It was just a balance beam, consisting of two pans that hung from a central beam, and it was used to measure the weight of materials. “Why do you have this?”

“It’s a balance beam!” Phainon pressed a finger down on one of the pans, and they watched as it sank while the other pan was raised into the air. “I use it when appraising antiques.”

“Appraising antiques?”

Phainon grinned in excitement at the thought of being able to talk about antiques and relics. “My entire trunk over there is full of antiques.” He waved toward the trunk sitting on the floor. “I don’t think I can bring them all, though.”

“Why not?”

“Why?” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows at the other man. “Because they wouldn’t fit?”

Mydei equally appeared just as puzzled at Phainon. “Just bring the whole trunk.”

“They wouldn’t fit?”

“Yes, they can.”

“But–” Phainon squinted at Mydei with extreme uncertainty. “–with everyone else’s belongings–”

“They will fit, so stop talking and throw everything into the trunk.” Before Phainon could argue further, Mydei had already taken the liberty of cracking open the trunk and stacking the tablets, books, and scrolls inside. Phainon could faintly hear the rattling of the antiques inside as metal knocked against metal.

Phainon wasn’t exactly sure if he could just take the trunk, as it had come with the bed when he was assigned to this spot in the barracks, but he continued as Mydei had ordered and began rummaging under the bed for the rest of his belongings. All there were under the bed were more appraisal tools that were too big to fit in the nightstand; clothes, which consisted mostly of the soldier’s basic uniform; and tools used to sharpen and polish his sword. Of course, he had to pay special attention to his beloved Dawnmaker, but he was sure Kremnos had even better tools to keep their weapons pristine. He didn’t bother with the whetstones and cloths that he always used for his weapon and only handed Mydei the other belongings he could scavenge from under the bed. He didn’t really need his soldier’s uniforms anymore, but he also didn’t have anything else to wear, so he tossed those as well in Mydei’s direction.

Which immediately earned Phainon a scowl from the other man. “Why are you bringing these?”

“I don’t have anything else to wear.” Phainon sheepishly chuckled.

Mydei clicked his tongue and threw the clothes at Phainon. “Don’t bother. We will prepare new clothes in Kremnos.”

Phainon’s vision immediately turned black when the clothing landed straight on his face, and he could hear the murmurs from the other soldiers that were still awake in the barracks. Phainon was sure that, by tomorrow, the news of his departure to Kremnos would spread throughout Marmoreal Palace. He peeled off the clothing with a laugh, leaving them on the bed for when he could return them to Aglaea before he departed.

They soon finished packing all of his things into the wooden trunk, and Phainon swiped his hands across each other to rid them of the layer of dust that had built up on his palms from digging through everything under his bed. With the brass hinges creaking, Mydei closed the trunk shut, with the lid landing with a satisfied thump. After Phainon threw the extra uniforms on top of the closed trunk, Mydei glanced in Phainon’s direction, and with a silent agreement, each of them took one of the iron handles on either end of the trunk and hauled it out of the barracks. Even though Phainon struggled with the weight of the wooden trunk, he managed to give a quick wave to the soldiers who were still awake and were watching them the entire time, to which the soldiers quickly returned.

Most of the weight was due to all the antiques that Phainon had refused to part with, and they eventually hobbled their way back to Mydei’s temporary bedroom with the trunk swinging between them. The most difficult part of the trip was definitely the stairs, where they were forced to set the trunk down onto the floor while one of them pushed up the trunk on one end and the other pulled and steered at the other end. They were both exhausted by the time they had finally made it to their destination and dropped the trunk down into a corner, and Phainon would have collapsed onto the bed if he had not been adorned in so much armor. Mydei shut the door with a deep breath as Phainon began making quick work of ripping his clothing off and leaving him in only the black undershirt and dark trousers.

“So–” Mydei’s deep voice cut through their silence. Behind Phainon, he could hear the gold of Mydei’s gauntlets hitting against what he could only assume to be one of the tables in the room as he also prepared to ready himself for bed. “–I think it is time for you to explain what you were doing in the public baths.”

Phainon quickly recalled their previous conversation and immediately bloomed a deep red. “Do you really have to know?”

“What did you do in there, Phainon?”

Mydei was definitely not going to let him sleep until he found out the truth, so Phainon could only give him the answer that he sought. “I… may have… touched myself to you… in there.” Phainon’s voice was barely above a whisper, but he knew Mydei heard him when a long silence followed his confession.

Phainon didn’t even want to turn around to look at Mydei, but he also felt it was wrong to proceed to the bed as if he had not said a word about what he did. Phainon could only continue to stand, completely motionless, under Mydei’s glaring gaze on his back.

“You…” A deep, exasperated sigh sounded from behind him. “When you said you touched yourself to me on the second night…”

“It… was in there.” Phainon awkwardly laughed, chancing a glance over his shoulder to gauge Mydei’s reaction. His expression was a mix of utter bewilderment and exasperation, but he also looked way too tired to deal with this new information.

“You… would rather masturbate in a public space than just sleep with me?”

“No!” Phainon laughed and immediately whirled around to grasp Mydei's hands. Staring straight into golden eyes, Phainon murmured, “You were just so alluring that I couldn't wait until I got to my bed.”

Mydei's face flushed a gorgeous red color as he cleared his throat and averted his gaze. “You… HKS.”

Mydei was absolutely stunning and breathtaking in Phainon's eyes. He couldn't even believe for a moment that this man was voluntarily his partner.

“Shall we?” Phainon tilted his head toward the bed. “We have a busy morning tomorrow.”

With a nod from the other man, they both returned to the bed after turning out the lights and crawled under the silk sheets. This would be Phainon's last night in Okhema for a long time, and he couldn't even fathom that fact. He spent much time before falling asleep deep in his thoughts about his many years in Okhema and all the things that he did while serving as a soldier for this kingdom.

As he stared up at the ceiling, which he couldn't see since they had already drowned the bedroom into the darkness of the night, he reminisced about all the people he had met, all the food that he had eaten, and all the quests and missions that he had done as a soldier here. Even if he did not have any particularly strong connections in the capital, Okhema was still a dear place in his heart, and he couldn't help but miss it at the thought of moving to Kremnos Kingdom. Of course, he knew that Kremnos would treat him well, but that didn't stop his heart from feeling for his days in Okhema.

Once Phainon closed his eyes and fell asleep, that would be it for his time in Okhema. He couldn't believe it would happen just like that. What awaited him in Kremnos? And, how will the palace handle the news of his departure?

“Not tired?” A deep, husky voice cut through the darkness. From the tone of his voice, Phainon could tell Mydei was exhausted, and he was surprised he was even still awake.

“Not sleeping yet?” Phainon turned his head away from the ceiling to face the direction of Mydei's voice.

The bed shifted next to him; he could only assume that Mydei had turned his body to face him, but Phainon's eyes were still adjusting to the darkness.

“What are you thinking about?” A hand reached out to cradle Phainon's cheek, and he was more amazed over the fact that Mydei had such good accuracy in the darkness.

“Just reminiscing about my time in Okhema,” Phainon responded in a low voice as Mydei's thumb began rubbing small, gentle circles into his cheek. “It's my last night in Okhema now, so it just got me thinking.”

Mydei hummed. “Will you miss it here?”

“Of course I'll miss it here.” Phainon smiled longingly at the thought of leaving his home kingdom. “But, I think I would miss you more if I stayed.”

A scoff resounded in the darkness. “What is with you and these lines today?”

Phainon chuckled, turning his body to face Mydei. “I don't know what you mean. I'm always like this.”

“Says the guy who couldn't even speak with me casually only a few days ago.”

“I don't know what you're referring to.” Phainon feigned ignorance with another laugh.

“You went from not being able to drop formalities to blatant flirting in a matter of a few days.”

“Are you blushing, Mydei?” Phainon teased with a grin and stretched out his arm to feel for his face, but a hand quickly swatted his arm away.

“Just go to sleep, HKS.”

Phainon laughed once more as the bed shifted again under Mydei's weight when he turned his back toward Phainon and effectively ended the conversation. As if it were now second nature, Phainon wrapped his arm around Mydei's waist, pulling their bodies together until his chest was pressed comfortably against Mydei's back. With a soft smile, he buried his nose into golden hair, shutting his eyes so that sleep could overtake his consciousness.

That was, until a deep voice cut through the darkness once again.

“You're not going to say it tonight?”

Wearily opening his eyes at his words, Phainon furrowed his eyebrows. “Say what tonight?”
