Castrum Kremnos wasn't particularly far, but they would still arrive during Curtain-Fall Hour if they kept to the schedule. As it was Entry Hour now, with only a few quints until Action Hour, Mydei and Phainon decided to split up to accomplish everything they wanted before departing. Mydei would deal with the logistics for their journey back: Food and beverages; ensuring everything was packed; the carriages were in good condition; the drivers of each carriage were ready for the journey; and the Kremnoans themselves were ready to return. On the other hand, Phainon focused on bidding farewell to his fellow companions in Okhema and any other last-minute paperwork he must complete to solidify his move to Kremnos.

Once Phainon and Mydei had gotten ready for the day and indulged in a light breakfast, Phainon's first stop was the laundry room to get his shirt cleaned. It was a quick stop in which he passed his black undershirt over to one of the maids, who gave him a quizzical look as to why he was only giving a single shirt. She tried to inspect the shirt out of sheer curiosity, but Phainon immediately waved the question away and asked her to have it cleaned by Action Hour, which she said would be more than enough time to clean a single shirt.

As he was thanking her and preparing to make a mad dash out of the room, the maid asked him, “Are the rumors true?”

What Phainon had learned throughout the last few days was that there were a lot of rumors about him–some that he didn't know of even before. Raising an eyebrow, Phainon settled back down into place as he was about to run out of he laundry room. “Which rumors?”

“They say you are to depart today for Kremnos,” The maid explained, and Phainon could see that her question sparked interest among the other maids who were in the laundry room. “Will you ever return?”

“Of course I will.” Phainon flashed her a reassuring smile, and he could see the maids in the back relaxing their shoulders. “I will be training in Kremnos to become stronger and will be back within a few months.” He neglected to tell her he would return exactly in time for the assembly with the Council of Elders, as he didn't want the news of that spreading and for the noble ranks to get suspicious of his planned return.

“Training?” The maid appeared taken aback. “You desire even more strength?”

Phainon laughed. “There is no such thing as being too strong. What if another disaster fell upon us? It doesn't hurt to be prepared.”

The maid smiled softly. “You are quite diligent, Phainon. Have a safe trip to Kremnos.”

With a nod, Phainon departed from the laundry room, waving goodbye to the other maids who were in there as well. Even though he was still carrying the extra soldier's uniforms that he had to return to Aglaea, he was also wearing one of the tunics, so he didn't want to return it so soon and walk around the palace half naked until his other shirt was cleaned. So, instead, he decided to make his way to the other individual he wanted to see before departing.

He had previously asked the guards on duty where the envoys of Styxia were staying, and although they had already departed Okhema late during the day yesterday, he figured that Castorice was still there, ensuring that the guest rooms had been cleaned and restored to their original state. Phainon was sure that Castorice may have already known that he was leaving for Kremnos, as she was also being involved in the plan to overthrow the Council of Elders, but he still wanted to say his goodbyes since he would not be seeing her for the next few months.

Making his way over to the part of the palace where the Styxia envoys previously stayed, he began to hear excited voices laughing and squealing up ahead. As he was still quite a ways away, he couldn’t tell whose voices they belonged to, but the closer he approached his destination, the clearer the voices became. He was surprised he could hear them from so far away, but they were also pretty loud, much to Phainon's amusement. He thought maybe they would be the maids conversing with one another while on cleaning duty, but he couldn't have imagined who they would be upon turning the corner.

“Empousa?” Phainon's eyes widened as his gaze landed on the woman next to her. “Castorice?”

The two women quickly cleared their throats, separating from each other as they had been standing quite close to each other before.

“Phainon!” Empousa acted as if she were not caught in some suspicious act. “Looking for Miss Castorice?”

Phainon's eyes shifted between Castorice and Empousa, who were now standing a reasonable distance apart. “You two know each other?”

“It's a long story,” Empousa chuckled, rubbing a hand on the back of her neck. “I bumped into her in the palace a few days ago.”

Castorice nodded. “Good morning, Lord Phainon.”

He had to blink momentarily at her as if he didn't hear her correctly. “Lord? Where is this new title coming from, Castorice?”

“I… heard you will be joining hands with the King of Kremnos in their kingdom today.” Her face was tinted ever-so-slightly pink. “Did I hear the news wrong? I thought to give my congratulations.”

Phainon already choked halfway through her statement and couldn't even catch what she said in the later half. Catching his breath, he ran an anxious hand through his hair. “I really don't know what you're referring to, Castorice.”

Her eyebrows shot up into her bangs. “So, is the news of your union false?”

“I…” Phainon's face bloomed a deep red, and he brought a hand up to cover as much of his blushing face as he could.

He could hear Empousa snickering from beside her. “Phainon is quite a shy man.”

“Indeed,” Castorice agreed.

“And even after everything they did together, too,” Empousa said with a lengthy sigh.

“You must finish telling me the rest,” Castorice seemed to urge Empousa, and Phainon glanced up at the two of them now that his face had cooled down.

“That does remind me, what were you two talking about? I could hear you from down the hall.”

The two women grew rigid at his question, and as he raised an eyebrow at their unusual behavior, they both quickly returned to normalcy as if they had rehearsed earlier.

“We were just…” Empousa seemed to be looking anywhere but Phainon, and his curiosity only grew at her lack of answer.

“Talking about books,” Castorice finished, but Phainon could still make out a light tinge of pink across her cheeks. “I was asking her for stories about Kremnos to garner inspiration for my writing.”

“Right!” Empousa loudly exclaimed. “Not very many people know about Kremnos Kingdom, so she was asking me to tell her about our customs… for her writing, of course. She isn't writing about anyone in particular or anything.”

Phainon clearly wasn't convinced; when had he ever asked if Castorice was writing about a specific person? He let it slide, nonetheless, as he didn't have all day to spend wondering what they were discussing so loudly and with such excitement. “Right… I suppose that does make sense.” He almost laughed when he saw Empousa let out a breath of relief so obviously.

“Yes, yes, exactly.” Empousa nodded enthusiastically, eager to steer the conversation elsewhere. “So, you were looking for Miss Castorice?”

Castorice perked up when her name was mentioned, and Phainon was reminded of why he had even come to this part of the palace in the first place. Seeing the unusual pair of Empousa and Castorice together had made him forget.

“Yes, that's right. Since you already know the news, I have just come to bid you farewell.” Phainon smiled in her direction. “I'll be in Kremnos for the time being, and then I will return in a few months.”

The noble woman returned the smile, giving Phainon a quick bow in his direction. “You will do great things in Kremnos, Lord Phainon. I look forward to seeing you again in a few months. If there is anything you need, Styxia will always welcome you.”

Phainon's smile grew at her words. “Thank you, Castorice. Do you know if Miss Aglaea is in her office?”

“She should be,” Castorice replied assuredly. “I was just there right before this.

With a nod, Phainon thanked her before bidding the two women farewell and departing from the scene.

The shoulders of the two women immediately dropped once the Deliverer had disappeared from the hall, and a dramatic sigh of relief came from the Kremnoan woman.

“That was close!” Empousa laughed as Castorice's face bloomed red. “I didn't hear him approaching at all!”

Castorice cleared her throat in an attempt to suppress her blush. “Yes, that was… truly quite close.” She took in a deep breath now that Phainon was out of sight.

“I wasn't sure what else to say if he had kept questioning us.” Empousa laughed once more, turning to Castorice. “Where did we leave off?”

“You were describing their position in bed during the fourth quint of Entry Hour,” Castorice reminded her, heart pounding with anticipation as she resumed with the image she held in her head of two very specific men.

“Right!” Empousa exclaimed. “And again, these are all just my guesses as I couldn't actually see them, but their sounds were just so loud that I could make an educated guess.”

Castorice hummed with an enthusiastic nod. “Of course, Miss Empousa. Please continue with your description.”

“Now, I actually think during this particular quint, they were standing against the dresser…”

She spent the rest of Lucid Hour excitedly describing the night of the royal ball while Castorice did her best to retain every single detail that spilled from the attendant’s lips. It wasn't until Lucid Hour was nearing its end did another Kremnoan attendant angrily approached Empousa and dragged her back, yelling at her for ditching all the attendants while they were busy cleaning and packing all of their belongings. Empousa was left being dragged down the corridor, yelling a mix of apologies to Castorice and pleas to the attendant who currently held her by the collar. All Castorice could understand was that the attendant’s name was Herklas, from the amount of pleas that came from Empousa.

Phainon dropped by the laundry room just to check if his shirt was cleaned before meeting Aglaea, which the maid had passed to him. Changing back into his black undershirt and with all of his uniforms in tow, he made his way towards Aglaea's office while still reflecting on his conversation he had with Empousa and Castorice. He would have to ask Empousa later what they had been discussing, because for some reason, the peculiar conversation he had with them could not leave his mind.

Bringing a hand up to knock on the door, her familiar voice called him in, and Phainon stepped inside. It suddenly hit him that this would be the last time he would step inside Aglaea's office for a long time.

“Do you have time for me, Miss Aglaea?”

“I always have time for you, Phainon.” With a gentle wave of her fingers, Phainon understood and shut the office door behind him. “To what do I owe the pleasure of your presence?”

“I'm sure you know of the Kremnoan's departure today,” Phainon began as Aglaea set down whatever work she had been focused on. “I just came to bid my goodbyes and return these as well.”

Aglaea's head turned toward the pile of uniforms that Phainon held out in his hands. “If you wish, you may keep them. But, I am sure King Mydeimos is preparing more extravagant clothing for you in Kremnos.”

Phainon struggled to contain his blush at her words. “I… Yes, that is what he said.”

A light laugh resounded from Aglaea. “Of course, it seems that King Mydeimos truly cares for you. I have no qualms with leaving my best soldier in his care.”

“Can you please stop with the teasing?” Phainon was finding it difficult now to continue holding Aglaea's gaze with the way his face was burning from her remarks. “I really came here to say a sincere farewell, you know.”

“I am well aware.” Aglaea threw him a knowing smile. “These are also all simple facts that I am stating. The King of Kremnos quite obviously has a favorite, and I am sure news of this has already reached the ears of the Kremnoans who still reside in Kremnos.”

Embarrassment washed over Phainon at the thought that so many people knew the King of Kremnos was now in a relationship. He wasn't exactly sure what to expect when he reached Kremnos Kingdom. How would his people react to Phainon? He could only hope that there weren't too many nonsensical rumors about him already, even before he stepped into their borders.

“Your worry is unnecessary, Phainon,” her gentle voice interrupted Phainon's thoughts. “You have already won the respect of the Kremnoan attendants in Okhema; I am sure you will have no problems in Kremnos as well.”

“Thank you, Miss Aglaea.” He nodded at her reassurance. Phainon was still worried, but he knew Aglaea wouldn't speak empty words. If she truly believed it, then she would say it.

“Besides that, I am sure you will learn a lot as well in Kremnos.” Aglaea continued with her reassuring smile. “And when you return to Okhema in time for the assembly, I look forward to seeing what kind of man Kremnos has shaped you to be.”

Phainon returned the smile. “Really, I appreciate all you have done for me, Miss Aglaea, and I'm not just saying that.”

She chuckled lightly at her words. “I appreciate the compliments, Phainon, but you have done much more for me than I did for you. Learn well in Kremnos, Phainon, and return a stronger man.”

As Phainon was making his way out of her office, with the uniforms still in his hand, he suddenly paused, remembering where he had stored all of their belongings. Pivoting on his feet, Phainon opened his mouth. “So I… accidentally packed all of my belongings into the trunk that belonged in the barracks…”

Aglaea laughed. “Yes, you can keep it. It will be no problem to procure another one for that space. Enjoy your honeymoon, Phainon, and Okhema will be waiting for you in a few months.”

It wasn't until Phainon had shut the door behind him that he fully registered what she had said, and he almost busted her office door down just to retort. Instead, he swallowed dryly and rushed off, eager to wipe the red that covered his cheeks. He wasn't sure if it was his imagination, but he could hear laughter coming from her closed office door.

It didn't seem as if Aglaea had anything for him to complete before he departed, or maybe she had already taken care of it for him. So, Phainon had much more time in his schedule than he originally thought. It was getting late into Lucid Hour, but it still wouldn't be for another one or two quints before it was Action Hour, the time of their departure. He didn't have much else to do before their departure, so he decided to take in the sights of Okhema for one last time before he could no longer.

His feet carried him through Marmoreal Palace, and he made small talk with the maids and soldiers who bid him their farewells. He wandered through the halls, reminiscing about all the time he spent in the palace, whether it was on guard duty or when he would be accompanying Aglaea. He still remembered when she had singled him out during the soldier's entrance exam and had personally taken him through the palace on the day of the exam, and he was frightened out of his mind that Aglaea was punishing him for something he had done. Apparently, she had been so impressed with Phainon's performance that she took it upon herself to personally escort Phainon around, but she singled him out also because she despised his outfit and quickly gave him a soldier’s uniform. According to her, she absolutely hated the yellow and purple that he wore to the entrance exam, but Phainon still didn't think anything was wrong with the outfit. He couldn't even put away the outfit as Aglaea had quickly gotten rid of it. This was one of his earliest memories in the capital of Okhema, and it was the first time he ever met Aglaea.

Upon exiting the palace, he made his way toward Marmoreal Market. Phainon distinctly recalled how overwhelmed he had felt when he had first experienced the downtown market, as it was so much different from the markets he was used to in his hometown. The number of vendors itself vastly outnumbered the number of citizens in Aedes Elysiae alone, and the sheer number of people in the market was enough to make young Phainon's head spin. Phainon remembered with a chuckle how easily he would get swept up in the crowds and how he had to fight for his footing; he was also much shorter than he was now, and young Phainon could barely see over the heads of the other market goers. He had never conversed with so many different kinds of people before, and he had never seen so many people crowding one place all at once before. It truly put into perspective just how many different kinds of people lived in Okhema, and it also emphasized all the different lives that Phainon would be protecting as a soldier.

He recalled the first time he had ever bought clothes for the bathhouse and was taken aback by how breezy it was. He remembered the first time he met Theorodos, the antique shop owner, and had quickly befriended the man over their shared hobby. He also recalled the first time he ever set foot into the blacksmith shop, and it was on his first day in Okhema that he vowed to have a grand sword crafted by the legendary blacksmith Chartonus. It wasn't until his dragon quest in Styxia many years later did he have this dream fulfilled, and Dawnmaker never left his side after that moment.

With a nostalgic sigh and the bright sun beating down on the market, Phainon perused around for one last time. It wasn't as if Phainon could fit any more things into his trunk that Aglaea let him keep, but it didn't hurt to shop around in Marmoreal Market, as he wouldn't be back in Okhema for many months.

He visited many vendors whom he was already quite familiar with, including Aphrea, the owner of the tailor shop he had brought the Kremnoans to a few days ago, and the news of Phainon's departure had already spread even to the market. He spoke with them all as many of them bid their farewells and wished him well. Phainon stopped by the antique shop as well, where Theodoros insisted he take some more antiques and appraisal tools with him to Kremnos in case there was no antique shop there. With a laugh, Phainon caved and took all of his gifts, which Theorodos graciously packed into a bag for him to easily carry. Stuffing the soldier's uniforms that he was still carrying around with him into the bag, Phainon carried on with exploring the rest of the market.

Phainon dropped by the blacksmith shop as well. It wasn't that he particularly needed anything, but he did want to bid a quick goodbye to Chartonus before departing for Kremnos Kingdom. Upon entering the shop, he waved for Chartonus’s attention, but he seemed to gesture somewhere outside the shop. It was almost as if Chartonus was waiting for Phainon's arrival.

He frowned, raising an eyebrow and following the direction where Chartonus was gesturing, but he couldn't find what he was pointing to. All he could see in that direction was more vendors and a small number of dromas caravans–now that the royal ball was over, the number of caravans had severely decreased.

“Important product for you, caravan from afar,” Chartonus explained, but it only further confused Phainon.

“They have something for me?” Phainon turned his head back around to stare at one of the caravans that was closest to the blacksmith shop.

Chartonus nodded. “Kremnoan item, you would be interested.”

Phainon's eyes widened at his words. Now he was more than intrigued by this caravan. “Kremnos’s borders have been closed until now. How would this caravan have Kremnoan products?”

“Royal family crest, not sure. Found from discarded scraps.” Chartonus retreated into the shop and re-emerged, holding out his hand in front of Phainon.

A ring was held for Phainon in the palm of Chartonus's hand, and he was bewildered at the sight before him. Indeed, it was a golden ring with a thick band, and upon the head of the ring, he could faintly see the Kremnos royal family crest. It was quite battered and beaten, but it wasn't anything Phainon couldn't clean. Inspecting the ring even more closely and picking it up with his own hand, Phainon could tell the crest wasn't a fake, and it was truly the real thing. Since not very many people knew much about Kremnos Kingdom, let alone their royal family, Phainon was sure that the caravan owner didn't realize what this crest signified. Chartonus may have thought it looked familiar and picked it up for Phainon to verify.

“Do you know where this was originally found?”

“Styxia shores.”

Phainon knew there was a lot of water in Styxia Kingdom, so it wouldn't be far-fetched to say that someone had scavenged this ring along their shores. He wondered whether Mydei knew of this ring, where it had come from, and what it was doing near Styxia.

“Can I keep this?”

Chartonus nodded, and Phainon pocketed the new item. He would show it to Mydei later and hoped that it was something he could at least identify, but the surface was quite ruined. Unfortunately, Phainon didn't think he would have the time to clean it. Maybe he could clean it in the carriage ride to Kremnos? But, he didn't want to show Mydei until it was in a better condition, and there was a chance Mydei would see him while he was in the midst of polishing the ring.

He hadn't realized the time, but it was now Action Hour. Thanking Chartonus and bidding his farewell to him as he wouldn't be back for a long time, he quickly made his way back to the palace so that he wouldn't have to make Mydei wait for him again. Digging through the sack that Theorodos had given him while briskly walking back to the palace, he dug up some tools that would be somewhat useful in restoring the ring to its original state. Phainon could tell the ring was pure gold, so the dirt and debris stuck to its surface wasn't rust, which made Phainon's job much easier. He just needed some tools that could scratch off the dirt that clung to its surface and a burnisher that could polish the ring and make it shine again.

It was quite a shoddy job that Phainon was doing, and it definitely wasn't his best work, but he was able to scrape off most of the debris by the time he reached the doors of Marmoreal Palace. Thanking the guards that held the door open for him, he shoved the tool he was using back inside the bag and dug through the different tools that were given to him. Phainon was unsure what Theodoros had exactly given him, but a sigh of relief escaped his body when he felt his hand hit a hard material that felt quite cool to his touch. Pulling it out from the sack, he instantly recognized it as an ivory burnisher, which was exactly what he needed to polish this ring.

He spent the rest of the journey back to Mydei's bedroom alternating between using the ivory burnisher along the surface of the ring and wiping its surface with a soft cloth that he had also found in the bag. By the time he reached the corridor where the Kremnoans resided, it was almost looking brand new, and Phainon could see the Kremnos crest much more clearly now that all the dirt had been scraped away. Upon seeing that most of the attendants were outside their rooms and hanging out in the hallway, he quickly shoved the ring into his pocket once more and headed towards Mydei's direction.

Mydei was conversing with one of the attendants–most likely regarding the final preparations needed for their journey to Kremnos. With the sound of Phainon’s footsteps, Mydei turned in his direction and excused the attendant.

“You're here,” Mydei said as Phainon stopped next to him.

“Did you think I wouldn't be?” Phainon smiled at him. They had been glued to each other's sides the past few days, so it was actually a little odd being by himself for the majority of the day.

Mydei neglected to respond and, instead, gestured toward the room that Mydei had been staying in for the past few days. “Put on the rest of your armor. I left it in the room for you.”

“Would you like to help me put it on?” Tilting his head toward the side and pulling off the best pleading face Phainon could manage, Mydei sighed exasperatedly.

“Just get inside.”

Excitedly pumping a fist into the air, Phainon quickly passed his sack of appraisal tools, antiques, and extra uniforms to one of the attendants and scurried inside the room with Mydei following shortly behind. The two of them made quick work of the armor; it was a record-breaking feat with how fast they managed to adorn Phainon in all the armor and belts now. But before Mydei could exit the room, Phainon cleared his throat, stilling Mydei’s steps.

He wasn't actually sure why he was so nervous to show Mydei this ring; he had even gone through the trouble of rushing to clean and polish its surface before Mydei's eyes could see it. Phainon couldn't explain his anxiousness, but he dug his hands into his pockets while Mydei raised an eyebrow at him.

Crossing his arms over his chest, Mydei huffed, “Whatever it is, you best hurry it up or–”

His voice died in his throat when he caught what Phainon had pulled out of his pocket, and Phainon almost took a step back at how fast Mydei had approached him to inspect the ring that currently sat within the palm of Phainon's hand.

“Where did you get this?” Mydei's eyes snapped up to Phainon.

It must be important with the way Mydei was acting. Staring with bewilderment into Mydei's eager golden eyes, Phainon did his best to answer: “A caravan was selling this in Marmoreal Market. He said he scavenged it from the shores of Styxia. The blacksmith owner saw the crest and gave it to me, as he was unsure if it was truly the Kremnos royal family crest.”

“This is…” Mydei reached out a hand, and Phainon passed the ring to him. Holding the ring out in front of him, it was as if Mydei couldn't believe what he was holding.

“Is it… important?” Phainon watched as Mydei continually twirled the ring in his hand, inspecting every corner and surface of the golden ring.

Mydei was completely stupefied as he cradled the ring in his hand. “This belonged to my mother.”

“The late Queen?!” Phainon exclaimed, his eyes darting back to the ring in Mydei's hand.

“We all had thought it was lost when my mother passed.” Shutting his eyes for a brief moment, Mydei reopened them to stare at Phainon. “When she was killed, it was said her body was dumped into the River Styx, the one that flows through Styxia. The ring must have been on her when that happened, and it must have slipped off her person and washed ashore. I can't believe…” His voice trailed off as he stared at the ring once more.

Phainon's mind was swirling with this new information. The late King just dumped his wife, whom he had killed, into a river?

“I'm glad you were able to find it again.” Phainon gently held Mydei’s hands, closing his fingers around the ring. “May it not be lost in the River Styx again.”

Mydei didn't even react to Phainon's joke as he continued to stare at his hand that had been closed by Phainon's. “I owe you one, Phainon.”

“There's no need.” Phainon moved his hand away as Mydei had one last look at the ring. “I am already satisfied enough seeing that this ring has been returned to you.”

“I truly…” Mydei brought his eyes up to Phainon, his golden eyes swirling with memories that Phainon couldn't possibly imagine. “Thank you, Phainon.”

With a gentle smile, it was Phainon's turn to approach him as he pressed his lips softly against Mydei's. Mydei's eyes fluttered shut as Phainon reached his hand upward to tenderly cradle his cheek, and Mydei’s fingers closed around the ring once again.

Once they parted, Phainon muttered against his lips, “All I needed from you was just that one kiss. Don't tell me you owe anything else to me.”

He exited the room, and Mydei was left in a daze, standing in the room alone with his face burning red and a visceral need running through his veins. If Phainon still stood in this room, Mydei was unsure what vulgar things he would be doing to that man’s body at this moment. Swallowing dryly, he carefully stored the ring on his person before following Phainon out of the room, ensuring that his face had calmed down before facing all of his attendants again.

The carriages that were already packed with their belongings were all waiting in front of Marmoreal Palace by the time they had exited the palace doors. With guards and maids lining up for their farewell, the Kremnoan attendants all filed into their respective carriages. Phainon was unsure which carriage his belongings were stored in, and he turned to Mydei.

“Which carriage will I be in?” He stared with wide eyes at Mydei, and the other man shot him a glare.

“Where else would he be if not with his lover?” Mydei climbed into the carriage at the front of the line, leaving Phainon in a complete stupor.

He called me his lover. He called me his lover.

Those words echoed over and over in his mind as he rigidly managed to push his feet toward the carriage in the front, climbing into the elaborate cabin and having one of the Okheman guards shut the door for them. Phainon had never ridden in such a fancy carriage, let alone any carriage at all, for that matter, and he stared with wide eyes around the entirely elaborate interior of the cabin as the carriage began moving under his feet.

Thus, starting Phainon's new journey in Castrum Kremnos, he stared outside the windows of the carriage, taking in his last sights of Okhema Kingdom with a full heart.

chapters.title: Epilogue 1: Castrum Kremnos
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I met Mydei's English voice actor when I was in the middle of writing this chapter, and he was telling me that the first thing he signed that day was a very graphic Phaidei comic.

I laughed with him as if I did not have a 100k+ graphic Phaidei fanfic sitting in my back pocket.

It was Curtain-Fall Hour by the time they had arrived in Castrum Kremnos. Although it was quite the long journey of sitting around in the carriage, Phainon tried his best to peer through the windows to take in the sights of Kremnos, but it was much too dark to fully appreciate the view. Mydei promised him that when he had time later this week, he would take Phainon sightseeing through Castrum Kremnos. Phainon eagerly looked forward to that promise.

Barely anyone was outside save for the few guards on duty, and only a few attendants were waiting for Mydei's arrival. Upon the door opening for Mydei, the attendants gave a quizzical look at Phainon.

“He is with me.” Mydei glanced at the attendant who quickly nodded at his words, stepping back and allowed Mydei and Phainon space to exit the carriage.

Phainon scanned the area in front of him that was a grandiose mix of royal blue, white, and gold that decorated the palace in front of them. The Kremnoan attendants all moved to unpack the carriages that housed their belongings, and Phainon was so distracted with the sight that he had to catch up with Mydei who was already halfway up the steps leading up to the palace entrance.

He released a short breath once he had caught up to Mydei, who was conversing with one of the guards at the entrance of the palace.

Mydei abruptly turned to Phainon. “I apologize if the trip was quite long, but Krateros would like to meet you.”

Phainon stared at him for one beat, two beats, and three beats in complete and utter silence. It was so quiet between them that even the attendant Mydei had been previously speaking with thought that maybe the silver-haired man hadn't heard the King's words at all. The attendant still was not sure who this man was; obviously, he was not from Kremnos Kingdom, but the armor that adorned his body showed that this man had quite the status. He could only assume that the man was from Okhema, where the King had previously visited, but why was he here? Perhaps, was Kremnos and Okhema forging an alliance? All Krateros had told him was that if the King had brought back someone with him that Krateros wanted to meet with them immediately.

“Right now?!” Phainon practically yelled aloud, and much to the guard's surprise, Mydei smirked.

“He must've already heard about you, and I am sure he would like to meet you before you settle within our borders.”
