Mydei scoffed, his own face growing red once more. “Look at the stained sheets I'm laying in and ask me that again.”

Phainon chuckled, the tension leaving his body. “I guess you're right.”

“You guess?” Mydei raised an eyebrow. “You just pummeled my insides, and you guess I liked it?”

“Okay, okay, yes, you liked it.” Phainon raised his hands up with a laugh. “We will have to take another bath though.”

Heaving a deep breath, Mydei pushed himself from the soiled sheets, and Phainon helped him over to the tub once more that still circulated in warm water. Mydei had so many sheets on his bed that Phainon tore the stained ones off, and there were still unsoiled sheets underneath. Tossing the dirty sheets onto the floor, he joined Mydei in the tub, and they both cleaned up to retire for the night.

"What?!” Phainon coughed up whatever food he was in the middle of swallowing, and Empousa stood up and reached over to pat his back.

“Sorry! So sorry; I thought you heard!”

“No one told me Krateros wanted to fight me?!”

It was the following day, and it was officially Phainon's first day in Kremnos Kingdom. Mydei had a lot of work to do since he was returning from a foreign kingdom, so while Mydei was working, Empousa happily volunteered to keep Phainon company. Phainon had told Mydei that he was fine with Empousa showing him around Castrum Kremnos instead, but Mydei stubbornly refused and told him to wait for him to finish his work.

It was Lucid Hour, and he had just parted from Mydei while Empousa took him out into the city to dine at a local restaurant. It was here that Empousa had so casually mentioned Krateros and how the man wanted to fight Phainon.

“But, the fight is happening today! No one told–”

“Today?!” Phainon felt like he was going to faint from how much he was basically screaming. “When?! Where?! Why?! What kind of fighter is Krateros?!”

He began pestering the woman in front of her with incessant questions, and she had to wave her arms to stop the man before he went on a tangent.

“At the Colosseum during the third quint of Action Hour.” Empousa watched as Phainon slumped into his seat. “No one came to your room last night?”

“No?” Phainon's mind flashed back to last night, and his face grew hot. “Oh.”

“Oh,” Empousa mimicked him with a roll of her eyes. “I'm surprised the King can even get work done with how you guys keep pouncing on each other every night.”

“That's not true!”

“I had the room right next to the King's in Okhema! Do not play with me right now, Phainon!”

“It wasn't every night!”

“Yes, it was!”

The two bickered back and forth across the table at the outdoor restaurant, attracting the attention of the innocent passerbys. Even the store owner had to come over and tell them to quiet down; but the owner didn't seem the least bit surprised at all when laying eyes on Empousa.

Phainon slumped in his seat again once the owner had left. “Please tell me Krateros isn't strong.”

“That's like wishing dromas could fly.” Empousa snorted.

“Do I even stand a chance?”

Eyeing Phainon up and down, Empousa took a sip of her drink before responding. “Definitely. If you can match up to King Mydeimos, then no one can best you. Just… keep your guard up around Krateros, and you should be fine.”

Phainon heaved a sigh, burying his face into his hands. “On a scale of one to ten, how strong is Krateros?”

“He proved his strength to the King's parents and was granted a special title for his strength.”

Phainon cursed under his breath, running his hands through his silver hair. “That is not promising at all.”

“You'll be fine, Phainon!” She roughly patted his slumped shoulders. “If you lose, it's not like Krateros can kick you out without the King's approval.”

“If I lose, I might as well just return to Okhema.” He buried his face into the wooden table as Empousa spewed reassuring statements at him. However, they all went through one ear and out the other, as Phainon continued to worry about this upcoming battle.

“Phainon.” Empousa stared sorrowfully down at the head of silver hair. “Just… at least finish your food. The King will throw a fit if his lover doesn't eat properly.”

“Am I even truly his lover if I haven't beaten Krateros yet?” He mumbled against the wooden table, and he jumped when Empousa slapped his back.

“The answer is a yes, so get up from the table and eat!” She pushed against his shoulders. “You won't beat Krateros on an empty stomach.”

Agreeing with a sigh, Phainon begrudgingly lifted his head and finished the rest of his food, with Empousa scolding him until he cleaned every last crumb on his plate. They agreed to check out the Colosseum following their meal so that Phainon could get a view of the battlefield before the scheduled fight. He didn’t want to give Krateros any advantage, after all. However, because there were Kremnoan guards clearing the Colosseum for their battle, Phainon couldn’t try a fight for himself on the Colosseum grounds, so all he could do was scan the area from afar. He was only able to even step into the Colosseum thanks for Empousa–most of the guards were extremely wary of a mysterious visitor who was clearly not from Kremnos Kingdom, and because Krateros had already stopped all rumors of King Mydeimos’s lover from spreading, no one knew who Phainon was.

The Colosseum was huge, bigger than any training grounds Phainon would ever lay eyes on in Okhema. It was basically a giant circular amphitheater made of concrete that spanned into the sky. Arches made up the many entrances that circled the entire diameter, and the top floors consisted of many, many rows of seats that had a clear view of the completely empty bottom floor. Phainon heaved a worried sigh as he scanned the area up and down. There was basically nothing to hide behind and nothing that could get in their way. It was just a vast empty space where two people could fight in an all-out brawl, depending on nothing except for their own strengths. No hills could give them an advantage, no dips or holes could give them an advantage; just a completely flat ground with the sun beating down on them.

“Thanks for bringing me here, Empousa.” Phainon glanced over at her and was surprised she was already staring at him.

“You’re going to be okay, Phainon.” She offered him a small, reassuring smile. “I really think you are over-worrying right now. Krateros may be strong, but you are also just as strong as our strongest leader.”

Phainon laughed lightly. “Do I really look that worried?”

“It’s all over your face,” Empousa deadpanned, earning another light chuckle from the other man.

“Thank you again.” He sighed once more, his eyes turning back to the circular bottom floor. “I guess there’s nothing I can do except warm up and wait for the time to arrive.”

“I’ll join you!” Empousa jumped in place when Phainon turned around. “I’ll bring you to an unused training ground, and we’ll be unbothered there.”

“You really want to join me?” Phainon raised a skeptical eyebrow as the woman hurried to his side.

“Where do you think you are?” Empousa scoffed proudly. “You’re standing in Kremnos, you know–the land of battle-hungry fighters. Even regular maids know how to fight here.”

She led him down the path toward the palace once more as Phainon took in as much of the city as he could. Empousa refused to explain any of the interesting sights that he saw, and he figured it was because Mydei wanted to take the reins in showing him around. Empousa only made an exception for the Colosseum due to the battle he had scheduled against Krateros, but she only made small talk with Phainon on the way back to the palace.

Pushing open the doors to what Phainon assumed to be the training grounds, she immediately made a face. Phainon, who was standing behind her, couldn’t really see what she was seeing.

“What are you doing here?” Empousa frowned.

“What else would anyone be doing in the training grounds?”

Phainon instantly recognized that the other voice belonged to Herklas, one of the other Kremnoan attendants that had joined Mydei to his trip to Okhema. He was even the one that shared a room with Empousa during their stay in the palace.

With a sigh, Empousa stomped through the door, with Phainon following right behind her. He nodded in Herklas's direction, whose eyebrows shot up at the sight of him.

“Phainon.” Herklas returned the nod. “I see you heard about Krateros’s battle.”

“That I did.” Phainon sighed heavily. He was going to be heaving a lot more sighs until the scheduled fight was over.

“And he's going to do great!” Empousa interjected, shooting a look at Herklas, who immediately understood her silent message.

He stared back at Phainon with a small smile. “I don't think there's a chance you will lose.”

“Seriously?” Phainon's eyes grazed over Herklas's expression, but, from what Phainon had learned over his few days in Okhema, the man was never one to jest.

“Just don't underestimate him.” Herklas pushed himself off the floor, standing where he was previously sitting. “I assume you're here to warm up before the fight. Let me join.”

“And why would we do that?!” Empousa gawked.

“It wouldn't hurt to let him join,” Phainon agreed. “The more people who know about Krateros, the more helpful it'll be for me, anyway.”

Mumbling under her breath, Empousa begrudgingly agreed, and Phainon spent the rest of Lucid Hour and the beginning of Action Hour fitting in a last-minute training session with Empousa and Herklas. They went over who Krateros was as a person, his fighting style, his weapon, everything that they possibly knew about the man both on and off the battlefield. As Phainon’s only encounter with Krateros was last night, when Mydei had an argument with him, Phainon did his hardest to retain everything that they were telling and showing him. He wasn’t sure how much Phainon could have possibly accomplished without these two helping him, and the time finally arrived faster than they had all realized.

Rolling his shoulders, Phainon stowed away the wooden sword that he was using as Empousa informed them of the time. His heart pounded against his chest at the realization that the time had arrived, and he was sure he would not be facing a happy Krateros, especially after the conversation he witnessed last night. Herklas wished him good luck and said he would clean up in the training grounds for them before heading to the Colosseum, so Empousa and Phainon went ahead without him.

He patted Dawnmaker at his side as they strolled over to the Colosseum. His palms felt clammy under the bright sun, and he had to wipe his hands along his clothes, which didn’t really help because he was wearing leather gauntlets. He balled his hands into fists over and over, feeling the blood pumping through his veins from when he was training with Empousa and Herklas.

After these few days of escorting the Kremnoans in Okhema, he had no need to swing Dawnmaker around within Okhema’s peaceful borders. He had previously done some test swings with Dawnmaker in the training grounds, and the weight of the greatsword still fit so naturally in his hand. Phainon didn’t think the next time Dawnmaker would be seeing action would be against a great Kremnoan general within their borders, yet here he was, approaching the Colosseum with a battle scheduled. One thing he was slightly worried about was that he had never fought with this armor that Aglaea gifted him. He was used to the soldier’s uniform, and he spent a good quint with Empousa and Herklas trying to become accustomed to the newfound weight on his shoulders.

He had originally thought it would be a spar with wooden weapons, which Empousa and Herklas quickly shot down and explained that it was a real battle. The battle would only stop once the opponent could physically not move or if they voluntarily surrendered, and Phainon swore he felt his heart dropping into his stomach at the news. They were proud Kremnoans, after all, and there was not a chance Krateros was going to voluntarily surrender. They explained the rules of the battle that severing limbs, permanently injuring the opponent such as blinding them, and actually killing their opponent was off the table, but everything else was fair game. Phainon’s mind swirled at the simple yet drastic rules; he knew Krateros was going to do anything and everything in his power to win against Phainon, and he had to get in the same mindset as well if he wanted to win against Krateros.

Once they were face-to-face with the grand amphitheater once more, Phainon inhaled sharply as Empousa patted his back and led him to a guard standing in front of the entrance. Citizens of all ages were crowding into the stands. How did everyone know of this battle even before Phainon himself knew of this battle? He felt his hands become sweaty again at how many people filled the audience; he couldn’t believe they were all hear just to witness this fight. Well, it was against a great Kremnoan general. Phainon was sure he would be watching in the stands too if he was not actually the opposing side.

“This him?” The guard posted out front scanned Phainon up and down.

Empousa nodded as she slapped Phainon’s back. Turning to Phainon, she muttered, “Good luck. I’ll be in the stands.”

He was sad to see her go as he was left with the guard, and it felt like the pressure really was on now that Empousa was gone. The weight of the upcoming battle weighed heavily on his shoulders as the guard gestured roughly in a direction off to the side, telling him to wait in that room. Nodding, Phainon obliged, and he waited off to the side as he continued to watch more Kremnoans filing into the amphitheater. The Colosseum was filled with bustling activity and the sounds of numerous conversations all happening at once, but all Phainon could hear was his heart pounding in his chest. He stared down at his hands, wondering what Mydei was doing.

A horn sounded from the bottom floor of the Colosseum, and Phainon jumped to his feet at the sound. There was some sort of announcer who was explaining the fight, but Phainon swore he could not register a single thing they were saying. He was way too nervous to understand a single word, and he flinched when the announcer’s hand beckoned him forward.

With wide eyes, Phainon hesitantly stepped under the sunlight with hollers and cheers resounding through the stands. He wasn’t sure what kind of introduction the announcer had given him, as he was even surprised the audience was cheering for some mysterious guest from afar. His blue eyes quickly scanned the crowd, but it was much too bright to see higher than the third floor.

His eyes shot back down when he spotted movement in the corner of his eyes, and he saw that older man from last night approaching the other end of the grounds. Adorned in that same armor Phainon had met him in, Krateros actually appeared much calmer than Phainon had originally expected. He would have thought the man would be seething with rage at seeing the boy he had raised announcing his love for some random man from some random kingdom, declaring that the royal bloodline would end with him.

Phainon withdrew Dawnmaker as he narrowed his eyes across the grounds at his opponent, while Krateros spun the spear within his hand. He was at a slight disadvantage in terms of reach, as the spear could reach much farther than Dawnmaker, but his greatsword was heavy enough to overpower the weight of Krateros’s weapon. Breathing deeply through his nose to calm his nerves, the announcer departed from the bottom floor, leaving Krateros and Phainon to their battle.

He grasped tightly at the hilt of Dawnmaker, assuming a defensive stance as Krateros darted over from across the field. Phainon was shocked at how fast the man was, and sparks flew as their blades collided. Slashing his sword to the right, he threw Krateros off balance and attempted another swing, but Krateros quickly regained his footing and dodged to Phainon’s left.

Blue eyes shifted to the left as he sidestepped backwards, swinging his greatsword to the left as his foot swiped in an arc along the dirt underneath his feet. Krateros parried it with ease with his armored gauntlets, sliding his forearm down the blade that was too heavy to fully stop and ducking when he had the chance. Phainon barely managed to stumble backwards, pulling Dawnmaker back to his side when a spear jabbed forward at his abdomen.

With a deep breath, Phainon created distance between them and barely dodged the attack. Krateros was a lot faster than Phainon was expecting, and he would have to catch up to his speed if he wanted to even land a hit. Empousa and Herklas had already informed him that his fighting style was very abrupt but calculating, and Phainon was experiencing it firsthand. His movements were swift, confident, and quick, and he always managed to aim for Phainon’s weak points even though they had never fought before. Krateros knew Dawnmaker was heavy, and he knew that Phainon was uncomfortable in the armor he wore. It truly proved just how much battle experience Krateros held that he could read his opponents so well, and he admired him for that. But right now, there was no time for admiration. It was Phainon’s turn to take advantage of Krateros’s weaknesses.

Krateros dashed up to him once again, closing the distance between them. Even though his spear had more reach, Phainon realized Krateros already knew he would lose going against Dawnmaker if their weapons truly went against each other. He was trying to fit himself into the space between Phainon and Dawnmaker’s swing, and because Dawnmaker was so heavy, Krateros was trying to take advantage of the time Phainon needed to pull the greatsword back to his side. He was trying to injure him in the time before Dawnmaker could be pulled back. Phainon was well aware of this, but he needed some way to combat this. It wasn’t as if he could just pull in Dawnmaker faster, but he needed to shorten the arcs of his swings, giving Krateros less space and less time to fit in.

Keeping his elbow close to his side to shorten his swings, Phainon swung downwards to push the man back, and Krateros jumped back just in time for the blade to barely brush against his body. Phainon swore he saw a smirk across Krateros’s face, but he didn’t have time to think about it as Krateros was on the move once again.

Phainon couldn’t take advantage of knocking the spear out of his hand, as Krateros wasn’t going to swing his weapon until he was in that sweet spot between Phainon and Dawnmaker, so he opted for his second weakness: His left eye. Phainon noticed Krateros was blind in one eye, and he would have to position himself perfectly in his blind spot to gain an advantage. He knew an experienced fighter such as Krateros most likely already had defense strategies in place to accomodate his lack of sight, but it was the only chance Phainon had. The only problem was that Phainon couldn’t make it too obvious he was trying to hit Krateros from his left, and he would have to distract him until he could put himself into his blind spot.

With his new strategy in place, Phainon would have to pretend he was fighting against Krateros while discreetly moving to Krateros's left. He brought Dawnmaker up to his chest as another jab was sent his way, and Phainon swiped the blade away. Krateros spun the spear in his hand before Phainon could knock it from his grasp, and Krateros tried again, thrusting his blade toward Phainon’s right arm. Phainon could already tell Krateros was trying to block him from ever approaching his left side, and the obvious move would be to sidestep to the left to avoid the slash against his right. However, that would move Phainon farther from Krateros’s weak side, so, instead, Phainon would have to solidify his position on Krateros’s left.

Phainon pivoted his right foot behind him, turning his body and throwing his left arm forward. Raising his right arm above his head, he grasped at the shaft right behind the spear itself. It was an awkward angle, now that Phainon had turned his body to be perpendicular to Krateros’s straight thrust, but he pulled the spear to his right. Krateros, who still had his hands wrapped around his weapon, was pulled forward. Before Krateros could jump back in time, Phainon used the weight of Dawnmaker to slam the hilt against the back of Krateros’s head, knocking him face-first into the floor.

Dust flew up into Phainon’s eyes, and he coughed, squinting through the haze to make sure Krateros had not escaped. He still kept his left hand tightly grasping the spear so that Krateros could not withdraw, unless he wanted to leave without a weapon in hand. He had planned for Krateros to pull him into the ground using the spear in Phainon’s hand, and he had already bent his knees and rooted his feet into the floor so it would be harder for him to budge. But, nothing happened, and when the dust cleared, Krateros was lying on the floor, facing the vast blue sky above them with a huge grin on his face.

Phainon was too taken aback to do anything and just stared silently down at him. The older man glanced over at him once the dust had settled, and he breathlessly laughed.

“I surrender.”

The crowd erupted in the amphitheater–Phainon had forgotten he had an audience the entire time. It was so loud that he couldn’t tell if the crowd was excited or angry that the fight had ended early. He even had a momentary thought that Krateros was just pretending to surrender to get the jump on him, but Krateros released the spear from his grip and pushed himself off the floor. Phainon was left holding two weapons in his hand, gawking at the older man who was dusting himself off.

“You look surprised.” Krateros smirked in his direction, and Phainon quickly straightened himself.

“I just thought it wasn’t the Kremnoan way to surrender.”

“I already lost.” Krateros belted out a heart laugh, but Phainon was still confused.

“I don’t understand.” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows with a frown. He still felt like he wasn’t a true victor. “I didn’t hit you hard enough to render you immobile.”

“The deal was that whoever landed a hit first would win,” Krateros explained. “You’re good, kid. I didn’t believe Mydeimos when he said I wouldn’t land a single hit on you.”

“Huh?” Phainon froze when he heard the familiar name, and he blinked blankly at the older Kremnoan general.

“Mydeimos bet that I wouldn’t be able to land a hit on you, and I thought the idea was preposterous,” Krateros grunted, crossing his arms. “How could he think that I, Krateros, the man who practically raised him and taught him how to fight, wouldn’t be able to land a single hit before you? I took on his bet that I would accept you into Kremnos if you managed to land a hit before I could, thinking that it would be an easy victory. I only needed to hit you once before you could hit me, and I didn’t take the fight lightly at all. But who knew you would fight with such gusto.”

Phainon’s mind was swirling as his shoulder slumped. It was way too hot under the sun to think about this, and there was no shade he could hide under in the entirety of the bottom floor. The announcer returned to announce Phainon’s victory, and he wasn’t pulled from his stupor until the crowd began to disperse. Krateros roughly patted his shoulder, shaking Phainon from his thoughts.

“Welcome to Kremnos Kingdom. I apologize you had to see me in that emotional state last night.” Krateros patted him on the shoulder once more before taking the spear from Phainon’s hand and departing from the Colosseum.

Slowly turning on his feet, Phainon watched Krateros disappear in the distance outside the Colosseum. He still felt like he was missing something even though his opponent had already disappeared, and he stayed rooted to his spot in the Colosseum until more familiar faces approached him.

“Phainon!” Empousa practically leaped onto Phainon, and he barely had time to catch her, making sure he didn’t hit her with Dawnmaker still in his hand.

“Did everyone know the battle would just be a one-hit wonder except for me?” Phainon noticed that neither her or Herklas behind her were the least surprised at Krateros’s surrender.

“Huh?” Empousa held Phainon back at an arm’s length, staring him up and down. “They announced it at the beginning. Weren’t you listening to the announcer?”

Phainon didn’t know whether to laugh or cry. Of course it would be the one time he neglected to listen to instructions.

“No wonder you looked so lost,” Herklas commented with an amused smile.

Phainon didn’t know what to say; he was actually rendered speechless, and it even came to a point that Empousa had to basically drag him out of the Colosseum. It was getting late into Action Hour now, and Empousa wanted to celebrate his victory out at a restaurant before most of the city closed during Parting Hour.

Herklas had to recount everything the announcer said while they made their way into the city, and now everything suddenly made sense to Phainon. The announcer had introduced Phainon as King Mydeimos’s lover brought back from Okhema Kingdom, and it was why he had received so much applause when he stepped into the stadium. The announcer even explained the whole premise of the battle, that Phainon would be accepted into the kingdom as the King’s lover if he won. And because everyone except for Phainon was listening to the announcer, everyone cheered at Krateros’s surrender because they already knew it was the end of the battle with that one hit from Phainon.

Herklas had also explained that, because Krateros was such a famous figure in Kremnos, all the citizens were eager to watch a battle with him involved. Thus, because everyone went to the Colosseum during the battle, now everyone in Castrum Kremnos knew of him. Phainon slumped into his chair once they were finally seated at a table at a diner. He couldn’t believe he missed so much important information from the announcer. Suddenly, Phainon went from some mysterious visitor from afar to the King’s lover, and everyone recognized him wherever he went.

He was exhausted after so much information was poured into his brain, and he trusted Empousa to order his food for him while he reflected on his battle with Krateros. It wasn’t until the restaurant they were seated in erupted into chaos that Phainon glanced up and was met with very familiar golden eyes.

“Nice work, Deliverer.” Mydei stood over their table with a smirk across his lips.

“Mydei!” Phainon’s eyes sparkled with excitement, and he had to stop himself from jumping from his seat. Empousa and Herklas, who were seated across from Phainon, nodded at their King as he took the empty seat next to Phainon.

“Phainon truly is amazing.” Empousa grinned once Mydei had settled into his seat.

“Indeed,” Mydei agreed. “He perfectly met my expectations.”

“Were you watching, Mydei?” Phainon eagerly hounded Mydei. He hadn’t seen the man all day, and he was starving for his attention.

“Of course I was,” Mydei huffed, crossing his arms and narrowing his eyes at the silver-haired man. “I’m offended you didn’t see me.”

“Where… were you?” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows as he thought back to the Colosseum, and then it hit him. It was so bright that he physically could not see above the third floor. Because the first floor was where Phainon and Krateros fought, Phainon could only see two rows of the audience before being blinded by the sunlight.

“The King’s seat is at the very top floor of the Colosseum,” Herklas explained. “It’s quite the grand throne.”

Phainon’s eyes widened as he was scrutinized under Mydei’s sharp gaze. Herklas was obviously implying that Mydei would be extremely hard to miss in the crowd.

“It was too bright to see!” He pleaded his case at Mydei, who raised an eyebrow. “I swear! I tried to look past the third floor, but the sun was in my eyes!”

Sighing, Mydei let him off the hook, much to Phainon’s relief. “As long as you didn’t make me lose my bet with Krateros.”

“Was the battle entirely your idea?” Phainon stared at Mydei, who nodded.

“I told you that Krateros would accept you if he saw you battle. So, I set one up.”

“Without telling me?!”

“Did Empousa not tell you?”

“Well, yeah, but it was kind of sudden!” Phainon whirled his attention over to Empousa, who straightened at suddenly being dragged into this lover’s quarrel. “Didn’t you say Krateros declared the battle last night?”

“He did.” Mydei’s deep voice answered beside him before Empousa opened her mouth, and Phainon’s attention snapped back to Mydei.

“But, how did you set up a battle last night if–” Phainon interrupted himself with a heavy sigh as the realization hit him. “You didn’t fall asleep like I thought you did.”

“That’s the third time you thought I had fallen asleep.” Mydei smirked in amusement. “You’re right. After you fell asleep, I went to speak with Krateros again.”

Phainon heaved another sigh, propping his chin in the palm of his hand. “I feel set up.”

Mydei scoffed and leaned back in his chair. “You should, because you were.”

Scowling at his words, Phainon spent the rest of their meal bickering back and forth with Mydei, with Empousa and Herklas observing the couple with sheer amusement.

His body landed with a soft thump into the bedsheets that were now clean, and Phainon breathed a deep sigh of relief now that the day was finally over. After their meal, Phainon and Mydei parted from the two guards, and they spent the rest of Parting Hour together. Mydei had shown him around Castrum Kremnos and the palace as he promised, giving him a tour of his new home. He introduced Phainon to the throne room that they previously passed, Mydei’s office, the vast kitchen, the dining halls, the numerous training grounds, and even a giant library that scaled from floor to ceiling and consisted of multiple floors. It was a grand library unlike anything Phainon had ever seen, even in Okhema and Janusopolis, where he occasionally visited under Aglaea’s orders. Once they returned to their bedroom during Curtain-Fall Hour, Phainon washed up before collapsing into the bed out of absolute exhaustion, burying his face into the sheets.

He heard Mydei's deep voice chuckling beside him, and he felt the bed dip next to him as Mydei settled into the bed. Phainon's eyes fluttered shut when he felt a warm hand running through the back of his hair and massaging his scalp.

“You did good today, Phainon.” Mydei murmured, playing with the silver strands upon his head.

Phainon hummed, his face still buried in the sheets. “Praise me more.”

“If I praised you anymore, I'd have to prepare myself for another long night.”

Phainon reached out and swatted in Mydei’s direction, and the golden-haired man laughed as he caught his hand with ease. Pulling his face from the bed, he stared up at Mydei who was sitting right beside him.

“Did Krateros ever come around with you wanting to end the bloodline?”

Mydei scoffed, resuming to stroke Phainon's hair. “Of course not. But, my first priority was you.”

“I'm sure you have better things to worry about than my livelihood in Kremnos,” Phainon mumbled, his eyes half-closed from Mydei's ministrations.

“How could I have you move to Kremnos without anyone knowing who you were?” Mydei remarked. “I want you to be comfortable in my kingdom, and you wouldn't be able to learn anything from anyone without first being accepted into the kingdom.”

Humming, Phainon lost himself to Mydei's touches and fully closed his eyes. He had to admit that Mydei was right; the Okhema assembly against the Council of Elders was only a few months away, and Phainon had to use that time to gain the trust of the Kremnoans to garner their support.

“How was Castrum Kremnos?” Mydei broke their brief, but comfortable, silence. “It was your first day here.”

“Tiring.” Phainon let out a breathless laugh. “But beautiful. I want to be able to explore Castrum Kremnos more while I have more energy tomorrow.”

“You deserve it.” A pair of lips pressed against Phainon's forehead, and he sighed with content as he felt the sheets shifting beside him. Wearily opening his eyes, Phainon saw that Mydei had tucked himself into bed and was in the process of covering Phainon with the sheets.

“Good night, Mydei,” Phainon mumbled with a smile as he was wrapped in the blankets, shutting his eyes and immediately letting the sleep overtake him.

With a small smile, Mydei brushed the bangs from Phainon's face, admiring his peaceful expression as the silver-haired man quickly fell into a deep slumber.

“I love you, Phainon.”

chapters.title: Epilogue 2: The Debate
chapters.html:
The carriage door opened, and Mydei and Phainon stepped out into the cool night air. It was Curtain-Fall Hour, and they had just arrived in Okhema Kingdom after a long journey. The carriage dropped them off in front of the palace in the depths of the night, and only a few guards were alerted that they would be arriving. On the other hand, Mydei had only brought two guards with him: Empousa and Herklas.

For this to succeed, it was imperative they moved in secrecy. They were trying to catch the Council of Elders off guard, so it was essential that as few people knew they were arriving as possible. It was also crucial for Mydei to bring as few people as possible to avoid detection. As far as the entire kingdom was aware, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae was still in Kremnos Kingdom.

It had been nine months since Phainon departed from Okhema Kingdom, and it was now the second month of the new year: the Month of Balance. This was when the review of legislation took place annually, after the celebrations marking the end of the previous year had concluded. The time seemed to pass by both slowly and quickly, as Phainon stared up at the familiar, yet unfamiliar, palace in front of him.

During his nine months in Kremnos Kingdom, Phainon did exactly as he was asked: to gain the trust of the Kremnoans. It wasn't very difficult, in Phainon's opinion, mostly because so many Kremnoans had built respect for him just from his battle with Krateros on his first day in Castrum Kremnos. Because of that day, everyone recognized Phainon's strength, and he further solidified his role and position in Kremnos, the more missions and quests he took upon himself to complete.

Mydei didn't grant him a special title, promotion, or any sort of high position within the Kremnos government. He didn't want it to seem as if he were playing favorites, which Phainon agreed with as well. Instead, Mydei let Phainon do whatever he pleased in the kingdom, and Phainon decided to join the ranks of the Kremnoans vanguard alongside Empousa, Herklas, and Georgious, assuming the same role of a soldier that he had held in Okhema. It was during his nine months with the Kremnoan vanguard that they all built trust with Phainon, fought on the battlefield with Phainon, and completed missions with Phainon. It didn't take long for the Kremnoans to forget that there was even a time he did not reside in Kremnos at all. It seemed almost natural for Phainon to be with them, and they welcomed him with open arms.

There was some debate over his position, though, as many Kremnoans favored Phainon so much that they cried for him to have a position in government, similar to Krateros who earned his through strength. They believed that if anyone in this day and age was worthy of earning a title for their strength, it would be Phainon. However, Phainon had other ideas for what he would do in the government, and he had already discussed it with Mydei many months prior to their journey back to Okhema:

“You want to what?!”

Phainon's shoulders wilted at Mydei's exclamation. “Is that not possible?”

Mydei sighed exasperately, running his hands through golden hair. It had been about four months of Phainon living in Castrum Kremnos, and he had adjusted quite well to his new life. Considering that he was a vanguard, his daily life wasn't too different from when he was a soldier in Okhema. The only real difficulties he had was trying to remember where everything was located, and trying to remember that he didn't have to treat everyone so formally. In fact, people were treating Phainon with formalities, and it was something that he could never get used to.

“That's…” Mydei narrowed his eyes as he mulled over the idea.

“I know I'm an outsider, but–”

“That's not the problem. Do you know how hard it is to run a kingdom?”

“I'm with you every day, Mydei, of course I know.” Phainon steeled himself with determination. He was prepared for Mydei to lash out at him over his proposal, but he was determined to help Mydei wherever he could. “You said you would rely on me.”

“I didn't mean run my kingdom for me,” Mydei snapped.

“But–”

“I already told you that I have come to terms with my disposition. You do not have to worry about me, and it is not something that I am worrying about.” Mydei pushed himself up from his office desk, and Phainon scrambled to continue the conversation before Mydei could end it.

“Think about it, Mydei. You'll be living in a world where everyone you ever loved will be gone. You will have to watch them breathe their last breath every single time. You will have to watch them age without you, while your body remains unchanging. Every person that you will ever meet will eventually leave you behind, and it may even come to a point where you forget about all those you have ever loved. Is that really a life you want to live?”

Mydei wavered at his desk, standing in place. Unbeknownst to Phainon, Mydei was only thinking about Phainon as he spoke those words. He would have to watch Phainon age without him. He would have to watch Phainon breathe his last breath and leave without him. He would have to live a life without Phainon. And then, after all of that, Mydei would forget about Phainon and all the time they spent together.

“Let me help you, Mydei. Learn how to control your magic so that you do not live forever with your disposition any longer. And while you are away, I will run the kingdom in your place until your return.” Phainon stared at Mydei, who was still turning the idea in his head. He knew with Mydei's hesitancy that he had a chance to turn the conversation around in his favor before Mydei had a chance to end it.

Mydei had previously explained that he could not spare the time to control his magic like Castorice because he had to run a kingdom, while Castorice did not have to do that. Phainon asked him at a later time why he didn't rely on Krateros to run the kingdom in his place, but Mydei said that they had very different views on the monarchy and leading the kingdom. Unless Mydei had to physically leave the kingdom for whatever reason, he would trust the kingdom into Krateros's hands. But Mydei's leaving for magic reasons was not a necessity, according to him. In addition, Krateros still had his own duties to handle within the kingdom as a general of the Kremnoan vanguard, and he wouldn't be able to play King at the same time. Which was why Phainon had a somewhat different idea.

“Teach me about the monarchy, and I will run the kingdom exactly as you wish. Then, we can set up a new Kremnos Kingdom together once you return, so that you do not have to live as its ruler for hundreds of years.” Phainon urged. “If we get married, then I'll–”

“Married?!” Mydei's face flushed red.

“W–Well…” Phainon couldn't help his own face from flushing in embarrassment after Mydei's reaction. “I would become your… Queen, basically, right? Then, I would be able to run the kingdom in your place while the King is gone.”

Mydei's throat bobbed at the idea, and he cleared his throat in an attempt to suppress his blush. “You wish to become Queen of Kremnos?”

Embarrassment continued to wash over Phainon, and his blush crept down to his neck. “It's…Well, I just–I'm trying to help you!” He cried, covering the lower half of his face with his hand and averting his gaze. “Look, if you don't want to get married–”

“I didn't say that at all.” Despite Mydei's crimson face, his words were completely serious.

“So you… want to get married?”

“Was it not your idea?”

“I was just thinking from a government perspective!” It was getting hot in Mydei's office, and Phainon began fanning his neck using the collar of his black undershirt.

“So, you only wish to get married to me so you can run the kingdom in my place?”

Phainon stayed silent, continuing to avert his eyes with an obvious blush. “Of course… not…” He finally mumbled, frowning at his heart that pounded in his chest.

Mydei scoffed in amusement, a smirk creeping onto his face, and his blush continued to grow. “So, you want to get married?”

“Do you want to get married?” Phainon hesitantly met Mydei's golden eyes that were smiling at him. “I mean… I know it's only been four months, but we can have the ceremony before you leave for the Grove and after I learn about this kingdom.”

Mydei hummed. “That's quite a way away. I don't think I can wait that long.”

“You want to get married right now?!” Embarrassment washed over Phainon once more.

Chuckling, Mydei swung his strong arms around Phainon's shoulders, pulling him close. Phainon didn't even realize when Mydei had approached him.

“I was only joking.” Mydei laughed lightly. “Fine. Let us get married later. And in the meantime, I will teach you all there is to know about our kingdom.”

“Our…” Phainon's face grew hot at his words.

“If you are to be my Queen, that would make this our kingdom, no?” Mydei smirked and pecked a kiss upon his lips, but Phainon was in too much of a daze to even react.

Thus, starting from that day, Phainon accompanied Mydei as his personal vanguard, learning all there was to learn about the kingdom and the monarchy. He alternated between accompanying Mydei while also taking on missions to sever the black tide monsters brewing outside their borders. In this way, Phainon learned about the monarchy while also gaining the trust of the Kremnoan citizens. And he did that for the next nine months in Kremnos up until his return to Okhema.

The carriages departed behind Phainon and Mydei, and to his right, Phainon could see Empousa and Herklas approaching them. They rode in a separate carriage that followed closely behind Phainon and Mydei.

An Okheman maid led them to their accommodations for their stay, and it was the same rooms that they had stayed in many months ago for the ball. They will be staying in Okhema for a week. The debate would occur tomorrow, and it would occur for the entirety of the day. Mydei, Phainon, Empousa, and Herklas would only appear when needed, which would be when Aglaea's plan was enacted. The rest of the week would be spent solidifying the alliance with Aglaea and ironing out the details for what was to become of this new age of Okheman government. That is, if their plan tomorrow was to succeed.

Phainon collapsed into the bed, exhausted from the long journey from Kremnos. Mydei proceeded to undress for the night, while Empousa and Herklas resided in the room adjacent to theirs. Heaving a sigh, Phainon stared up at the chandelier that he was familiar with all those months ago from when he would share this room with Mydei during the week of the royal ball.

“Nervous?” Mydei's deep voice rang clearly in the guest room.

Phainon turned to him wearily, blinking the sleep out of his eyes. “I'm more exhausted than anything. Although I am a little nervous, as I don't know what to expect tomorrow.” He only had a general gist of the plans and the role he would have to play, but he wasn't exactly sure if he had to specifically do anything other than show up as the Deliverer.

The other man slipped into his familiar silk robe, strolling over to Phainon and kneeling on the floor between his legs, which currently hung off the edge of the bed. “I am sure Aglaea already accounted for you in her plans. If she wanted you to do anything specific, she would have communicated that to us.”

Sighing, Phainon couldn't help but agree. Aglaea was like that, after all. He forced himself to sit up in the bed, observing Mydei as he stripped Phainon of his outside clothes. He pulled off his leather boots, undid the belt around his thigh, but before he could move on to his pants, Phainon held out his hand. “I can handle it from here.”

His blush didn't go unnoticed by Mydei, who smirked, lowering his hands, but he didn't move from his spot on the ground between Phainon’s legs. Phainon could only helplessly strip under Mydei's darkening gaze while ignoring the fluttering in his stomach.

“We have a big day tomorrow, Mydei,” Phainon mumbled, cheeks burning hot when the sound of his pants unzipping echoed in the room.

Mydei's eyes were glued to Phainon's hands that fiddled with his zipper. “I know.”

“Then…”

“It doesn't hurt just to look.” Mydei lifted his eyes at Phainon, his hands balling into fists at how delectable Phainon looked above him. The silver-haired man sat with his legs spread before him, a bulge already evident in his pants, with the most adorable blush across his cheeks as his blue eyes trembled under Mydei's gaze. Mydei still found it amazing how Phainon would get hard even without Mydei touching him.

“How are you not tired?” Phainon continued fiddling with the zipper even though he had already pulled it down. He just didn't want to do the next step of removing his pants right under Mydei's gaze, especially because he felt the heat between his legs stirring.

At those words, Mydei pushed himself off the floor, grabbing Phainon's waistband himself and dropping his pants to the floor. “I don't have all night to wait for you, Phainon. Didn't you say we had a big day tomorrow?”

Phainon gulped, eyes flitting between Mydei’s tempting lips that were nearing his and his golden eyes that were almost black from how much they had dilated. His breath hitched in his throat when a weight settled into his lap, and his hands automatically flew to grasp a handful of Mydei's behind as he settled on top of him. He continued shifting in his seat, teasing Phainon over the edge as he continued purposefully grinding into Phainon's already hard erection.

This was going to be a long night.

It was Action Hour when they all departed from their rooms and headed to the Demigod Council. It was a part of Okhema where the Council of Elders resided, and the debate was currently occurring there. As they were not needed until the question of Aglaea's power came into the discussion, they didn't depart until much later in the day. And because no one knew Phainon and the others were here, they couldn't leave their rooms until the time was right to ensure no one else saw them.

It was Phainon's job to lead the rest of his party over to the Demigod Council, and the Okheman citizens were quite shocked to suddenly see Phainon again after a couple of months of his departure with no prior warning at all, especially with the Kremnoan King in tow. Many of them would run up to Phainon in utter excitement but would immediately back away upon seeing the high-profile noble right next to him. Phainon would only wave to them from afar, explaining to all he passed that he and Mydei were going to the Demigod Council.

Because of that, more Okheman citizens decided to join the assembly with Phainon, and it soon felt like a crowd was gathering behind them as they all made their way to the Demigod Council. Citizens who wanted to participate and vote in the debate could only join at the very start, which was in Lucid Hour, so Phainon was not exactly sure why everyone was following them.

It was quite a far trek through Okhema, but they eventually made it to the outdoor amphitheater where the debate was taking place. From afar, Phainon could spot Caenis, the leader of the Council of Elders, in the center of the amphitheater, grandly discussing something, but he was too far to see what she was harping about. Off to the side was the rest of the Council of Elders, Castorice, and Anaxa. On the other side of Caenis was Aglaea, and in the stands were the participating citizens of Okhema. Phainon whirled his head toward Mydei with wide eyes, silently wondering how they were supposed to catch the Council of Elders off guard if there was a crowd of Okhemans following behind him.

He wasn't exactly sure if Mydei understood what he was trying to wordlessly convey because the man only nodded and proceeded to the amphitheater. Phainon, panicking, could only run after Mydei while he strolled straight up to Aglaea. There was nothing barring them from entering the amphitheater, and Mydei soon joined Aglaea's side with ease. Though, the look on Caenis's face was priceless.

“You–!” Her burning eyes whipped toward Aglaea, who appeared as nonchalant as ever with Mydei at her side. “What is he doing here?!”

“I would prefer it if you spoke to me directly.” Mydei's voice boomed in the amphitheater, and murmurs resounded throughout the stands at this new appearance. “It's nice to make your acquaintance. My name is Mydeimos, from Castrum Kremnos.”

Caenis's face boiled with rage, and she pointed a finger at Aglaea. “Why did you bring this outsider?!”

“Going by that logic, I believe we should remove the Grove and Styxia Kingdom, no?” Aglaea cocked her head to the side, her smile never dissipating. “I do believe a welcome is in order for the King. It's nice to finally have you join us, King Mydeimos.”

“The pleasure is all mine,” Mydei responded.

“That's because Okhema has an alliance with the Grove and Styxia,” Caenis retorted, continuing to ignore the King's presence. “There is no reason why an outside kingdom should be present during discussions of Okheman legislation.”

“I believe there is a reason.”

As if on cue, Phainon finally met Mydei's side. He took a deep breath after finally settling next to the King, and the citizens in the stands erupted into an uproar.

“How did you get so far ahead of me?” Phainon muttered quietly enough that only Mydei could hear over the roaring crowd. The Council of Elders was taking this time to try to silence the Okheman citizens.

“Right on time, Deliverer.” Mydei smirked while crossing his arms.

“Huh?” Phainon furrowed his eyebrows, but before he could say anything more, Caenis's voice overpowered the crowd.

“Silence!” Caenis's voice boomed, and the citizens all settled down. With a deep exhale, she turned to Phainon with narrowed eyes. “Welcome back, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.”

“It's a pleasure seeing you again, Miss Caenis.” Phainon never knew such an outright lie could ever leave his mouth.

“How kind of you to make it to this assembly, but I believe we no need for any more guards on duty for today.” Caenis shot him a wry smile.

“Phainon is here to join me today,” Mydei cut in, and Caenis's eyes finally fell upon the Kremnoan King.

“To join you?” Caenis raised an eyebrow, mirroring Mydei in crossing her arms across her chest. “Pardon me, but I still don't see why the Kremnoan King has decided to join us today.”

“King Mydeimos has agreed to work with Okhema.” Aglaea gracefully stepped forward after flashing a smile in Phainon's direction. “I sent Phainon over to Kremnos to work out arrangements for an alliance.”

Caenis didn't seem the least bit impressed. “So, Okhema will be joining hands with Kremnos Kingdom. That doesn't explain why that man was in Kremnos for more than a month.”

“Phainon and I are getting married.”

The entire amphitheater froze in time; even Phainon felt the air grow cold under the afternoon sun, and even Aglaea faltered in her footsteps just slightly. Across the amphitheater, Castorice's eyes widened, and Anaxa had buried his face in his hand. Phainon couldn't tell if Anaxa was flabbergasted or exhausted from hearing the news.

“Ex–Excuse me?” Caenis was also flabbergasted, and Phainon couldn't blame her at all. Even he was flabbergasted.

“Phainon is to become the new Queen of Kremnos,” Mydei leisurely continued. “Kremnos will not be joining hands with Okhema; they will be joining hands with the Deliverer.”

The crowd erupted into a frenzy of murmurs and whispers, with Phainon faintly hearing recounts of him being Mydei's guard a couple of months ago. Caenis’s eyes widened at the King's words. “You can't just pick and choose who you want to work with–”

“The Deliverer will be joining hands with Kremnos Kingdom. I don't see what is confusing about this.” Mydei tilted his head to the side.

“If you're working with that man, that means you are joining arms with the Okhema–”

“I don't recall the Deliverer having an official position within the Okheman government,” Mydei interjected Caenis's words. “Even the title ‘Deliverer’ is an unofficial title granted by the common people. Kremnos will be working with the Deliverer, who is currently under Aglaea's command.”

Caenis fell silent at his words, her eyes trembling with fury. The other Elders continued their silence, their gazes glued to Caenis in the middle of the amphitheater.

“Well, I believe we should have a vote now.” Aglaea nonchalantly waved her hand in the air, attracting the attention of the crowd. It was then that Caenis noticed that the crowd had somehow grown in size compared to this morning, but, in a fit of rage, she could not differentiate who had been there since the beginning and who had not. However, she wasn't very concerned since the newcomers could not vote.

“You–”

“Shall we start with the citizens' vote?” Aglaea gestured toward the stands. “Or shall we start with the government vote?” She stepped forward as her golden heels resounded against the concrete under her feet, meeting Caenis in the middle. “The legislation in question is: Aglaea's role in the Okheman government. To abolish their leader and become an oligarchy–a government in which only the Council of Elders will rule. Or, shall I propose a new form of government–a government without the Council of Elders at all.”

The citizens erupted once more at Aglaea's proposal, with Caenis's attention whipping back over to Aglaea.

“And where are your grounds for proposing such legislation?” Caenis barked.

“My grounds being that my own rule is being questioned by the Council,” Aglaea promptly answered. “How are the citizens supposed to believe in a government where its Council questioned the motives of their leader?”

“It is only a mere proposal,” Caenis scoffed back. “A proposal that does not yet have a ruling.”

“To question is to lose trust.” Anaxa's voice suddenly resounded through the amphitheater. “The moment you question is the moment trust falters.”

“Would you say, when a student questions you during a lecture, that they are losing trust in you?” Caenis turned toward Anaxa, who was still standing among the Council of Elders.

Much to everyone’s surprise, Anaxa readily agreed. “I would say so.”

“So, you would agree that you have lost the trust of every single student that has ever asked you a question?”

“You misunderstand.” Anaxa shook his head in annoyance. “Asking a question does not equate to questioning. You may ask a question out of sheer curiosity or a need for clarification. But questioning would mean doubt–doubt in what an individual says, does, or believes in. Conversely, I would regain their trust after answering or explaining correctly.”

Caenis scoffed. “A professor and Grand Sage who so readily admits to having his authority questioned by his own students. Were you not of the same mind to unite under an oligarchy? Similar to how the Grove is run, Okhema can venture toward that same path.”

“An individual can never learn if they can never doubt,” Anaxa said. “And an oligarchy would only be the correct path if run by the correct people.”

With the professor’s final words, the crowd murmured amongst each other once more. His answer was vague enough that it could be taken both ways: Either he believed the Council of Elders to be the correct people, or he did not believe they were the correct people.

“Let us start with the government vote.” Caenis, who had regained her composure, glared at Aglaea. “As we always do.”

Aglaea only smiled and returned to Phainon and Mydei's side of the amphitheater. In the center of the amphitheater was placed a large jar, and each member of the assembly was given a metal disk with a different color on each side. By dropping the metal disk either up or down that corresponded with their vote into the jar, it would record the number of responses for each side and emit a color of smoke for the winning vote.

As per usual, the government officials and allies would vote first, then the citizens would vote after. After finalizing the winning side for each group of voters is when the color of smoke is released from the opening of the jar. It was why the citizens who just joined the crowd could not vote; the metal disk was only distributed at the very beginning of the debate.

However, a metal disk was each given to Phainon and Mydei now that they had joined the assembly. Caenis couldn't kick Mydei out now that he had announced his allegiance to Phainon and Aglaea. Kremnos was now seen as an ally who could partake in the assembly, and Phainon was given a metal disk now that he was connected to the monarch of Kremnos and no longer an average citizen.

Each representative went up, one by one, to drop their metal disk into the jar. With their back turned to the assembly, it would be impossible to see who voted for which side. The Council of Elders voted, Castorice voted, and Anaxa voted. Aglaea voted, Mydei voted, and finally, Phainon voted. Following them, the citizens began to cast their vote. One by one, each citizen in the stands who possessed a metal disk would rise, dropping their disk in the jar.

Phainon watched the crowd whispering amongst each other in the stands, and it was then that he realized. All of the citizens who followed Phainon up to the amphitheater were in support of him, and now that they were sitting amongst the crowd, they could influence the decision-making of those citizens in possession of a metal disk. Phainon, Mydei, Empousa, and Herklas approaching the Demigod Council was all a show. It was a wordless show of Kremnos's alliance with Phainon, and now that the citizens knew they were even getting married, Phainon was being seen in a new light of holding his own government power in a different kingdom. They were not voting for a titleless man anymore; they were voting for a queen. Everything somehow followed the exact plan that Aglaea had articulated, even without any specific instruction from Aglaea herself.

With the last citizen returning to their seat in the stand, every single metal disk was now accounted for. With Phainon, Mydei, Aglaea, Castorice, and Anaxa all voting for the same side, they should outnumber the votes of the Council of Elders. And, if all went according to plan, they would have to win two-thirds of the citizen votes to win the citizen assembly vote.

Everyone watched silently with anticipation as the jar sat in the middle of the amphitheater. Whispers and murmurs echoed amongst the stands as they urged the jar to reveal the outcome of the votes. Gold smoke would mean more metal disks with the gold side facing up were cast into the jar, which was in favor of Aglaea keeping her position. Whereas, white smoke would mean more metal disks with the white side facing up were cast into the jar, which was the side for the oligarchy.

And everyone saw the jar puff up a smoke glittering with gold.

“I believe a congratulations is in order.”

Phainon, who was watching the assembly disperse, glanced over to the voice speaking to him. With smiling eyes, he nodded in her direction. “Congratulations, Miss Aglaea. Everything proceeded according to your plan.”

Her eyebrows shot up as she stopped in front of Phainon. “I didn't mean for me. I meant for you.”

“For me?”

“I heard you were getting married. Thus, a congratulations would be in order.”

Phainon choked. “Thank you… Miss Aglaea.”

“Oh, don't be so formal with me.” She tilted her head with a smile. “I am only but a leader; nothing in comparison to a queen.”

At her jest, Phainon burned brightly. “I am not married yet.”

“Still, I didn't realize your relationship had blossomed like so.” She laughed lightly at how dark Phainon’s cheeks became. “Had I known, I would have sent you to Kremnos much earlier. I didn't realize you had talks of marriage during those couple of months on leave.”

“Miss Aglaea…”

“I'll be awaiting my invitation to the ceremony.” With another chuckle, Aglaea departed from the Demigod Council. Most likely, she had a lot of work to return to as the new sole leader of Okhema.

With Phainon left in the amphitheater, he proceeded to make his way to Mydei, who was speaking to Empousa and Herklas off to the side. They were watching the debate on the sidelines, since they could not participate in the vote. As he was making his way over, however, he noticed someone else staring in his direction.

Laughing, Phainon turned toward their peering eyes. “Castorice, I don't bite.”

Castorice's cheeks grew red as she scurried over. “I didn't mean to stare.”

“I don't mind, Castorice.” He was already quite used to Castorice’s somewhat odd behavior. “How have you been? It has surely been quite a while.”

She nodded, her eyes darting between Phainon and something behind him. “Business has been the same in Okhema. I am glad to see you in such good health, Lord Phainon.”

“The same goes to you.”

“Has… Kremnos been treating you well?” For some reason, Castorice's cheeks grew red once more. Phainon wasn't sure why; it was quite a typical question.

It was Phainon's turn to nod. “Kremnos has been very good to me. Although it took some time to become accustomed to the new environment, life has treated me well over there.”

“I'm glad.” The blush across her face did not fade. “I… would like to express my congratulations to you as well… again. Should I refer to you as Queen Phainon?”

Phainon frowned as his own face mirrored the color of Castorice's. “Thank you, Castorice. And…” He cleared his throat. “Just ‘Phainon’ is fine.”

Castorice nodded once more. “Has King Mydeimos been treating you well? I heard a little from writing to Miss Empousa.”

“You exchange letters with Empousa?” This was the first Phainon had ever heard of it. Empousa never mentioned such a thing. Since when had the two become close enough to even exchange letters?

“Err, yes.” It seemed the color of Castorice's face darkened.

“What do you write to her about?”

“...Stories.”

“Stories?”

“And… writings.”

Phainon vaguely remembered when he had first seen Empousa and Castorice together, and they had said they were talking about inspiration for Castorice's writings. “That's right. How have your stories been coming along?”

Smiling softly, it was almost as if Castorice's eyes sparkled. “Very, very well.”

“You get a lot of inspiration from Empousa?”

Her eyes seemed to sparkle even more brightly. “Very much so.”

Castorice and Phainon talked with each other for quite some time, catching up with each other and what each person had been doing. Castorice talked about what had happened in Okhema while Phainon was gone, and Phainon would explain what he had been up to while in Kremnos. It was refreshing being able to speak with Castorice again after not having seen her for a number of months. It wasn't until a strong arm wrapped around his neck did he realize just how long he had been standing in the now-empty amphitheater conversing with her.

“Phainon.” Mydei narrowed his eyes at him with his arm wrapped around his neck. “Will you be staying here for the remainder of the day?”

Phainon chuckled, turning his head toward him. “Sorry, I didn't realize how long it's been.”

“I don't mind you staying here,” Mydei clarified. “I can go ahead if you'd like more time.”

“No!”

Phainon and Mydei paused momentarily before turning toward the third person present who had shouted.

Castorice's face was bright red as she stammered, “Don't worry about me! We… We have spoken long enough. Please go ahead.” She cleared her throat in an attempt to regain her composure.

“Are you sure, Castorice?” Phainon tilted his head to the side as she nodded enthusiastically.

“Please, I insist,” she squeaked. Nodding toward Mydei, she quickly added, “It is a pleasure to see you again, King Mydeimos. Congratulations on your union.”

Mydei, with wide eyes, quickly cleared his throat to contain his blush. “Thank you.”

She scurried off, leaving Phainon and Mydei in quite a daze. They both stared at each other, exchanging a laugh before reuniting with Empousa and Herklas. They spent the rest of their day at the pub, thanks to Empousa, celebrating their victory and the news of their soon-to-be marriage. They now had the rest of the week to enjoy their time in Okhema, which Phainon was looking forward to. Mydei and Phainon would have to meet with Aglaea quite frequently during this week to solidify their alliance, Phainon's new regiment consisting of both Okheman and Kremnoan soldiers, and other plans for this new Okhema that Aglaea had in mind, but Phainon was more than happy to resume his role of assisting Aglaea once more.

It was now the depths of Curtain-Fall Hour when they returned to their temporary quarters and parted from Empousa and Herklas. Empousa, who was thoroughly knocked out from all the drinking, was slumped in Herklas’s arms, and Phainon and Mydei bid him good night as he stumbled into their shared room.

Phainon and Mydei returned to their own room, with the bedsheets freshly washed after their previous night’s activities. A tub of warm water sat in the corner, awaiting their arrival, and Phainon wanted nothing more than to relax in a bath at this moment. He began to unravel each belt, but before he could get very far, Mydei cleared his throat from behind him.

Still fiddling with the belt that held his pauldrons upon his shoulders, Phainon pivoted on his feet, assuming that Mydei needed him for something. “Did you need me, Myd–”

When Phainon had glanced up from the belt, his voice faltered when he saw how red Mydei's face was. It was so red that it was the same color as the cape that hung off his shoulder and his red tattoos. Mydei was nervously shifting on his feet, holding a small box in his hand.

“Give me your hand,” Mydei murmured. It was so quiet that Phainon had barely caught his voice.

Quickly releasing the belt from his grasp, Phainon held out his fighting hand for him; although Phainon was ambidextrous, he often used his right hand for fighting. He wasn't sure what exactly Mydei needed him for, but it must have been important with how nervous Mydei was. Usually, out of the two of them, Phainon was the one who was always more nervous.

“Other hand.”

Phainon immediately switched hands, holding it in front of them with his palm facing upwards.

Mydei, who had removed his gold gauntlets at some point already, gently grasped Phainon’s hand and flipped it over. The warmth from his hand spread up Phainon’s arm as Mydei tenderly rubbed his fingers. Mydei still had his eyes cast downwards at Phainon’s fingers before bringing the small box closer to his hand. Curiously, Phainon watched as Mydei slowly opened the box.

“Don't say anything,” Mydei mumbled, refusing to look up at Phainon, who could see how adorably red his ears were through his blonde hair.

With a smile, Phainon stayed quiet, but when Mydei unveiled what had been hiding in the box, it suddenly became hard for Phainon to keep his voice down.

Trembling hands slipped a golden ring on Phainon’s finger. With widened eyes, Phainon saw the crest of the Kremnos royal family engraved upon the head of the thick, gold band. It was the ring that Phainon brought back to Mydei before they returned to Kremnos all those months ago; however, the only differences were that the ring was in completely new condition now and that the ring perfectly fit his finger. Phainon's shoddy job of trying to clean the ring had been perfected, and it stood glowing upon Phainon's hand.

“This is…” Phainon was frozen in place, unable to do anything except mutter these words.

Mydei hesitantly lifted his gaze up from the ring, frowning at how much his face burned. “It is my mother's ring.”

“I… know. But, why are you giving me this?” Phainon's throat burned as he asked this question, his heart racing in his chest.

“It's a symbol of the Queen,” Mydei explained. His eyes dropped toward Phainon's hand, but he quickly caught himself and locked eyes with Phainon's once more. “This ring is supposed to belong to the current Queen of Kremnos.”

“But, I'm not–”

“But you will be.” Mydei cut him off, struggling to take a deep breath. “So this ring is yours.”

“Mine…” Phainon slipped his hand from Mydei's warm grasp, holding his hand out in the air and watching the ring twinkle under the chandelier light.

“Will you marry me, Phainon?”

Phainon's eyes, now wide again, quickly shot up from the raised ring to Mydei's shaking gaze. The blood pumped through Phainon's veins as his pounding heart filled his ears. Phainon needed to hear those words again–at least confirm that he wasn't just dreaming.

“...What… What did you say?”

“You heard me.” Tears twinkled in Mydei's glaring eyes, and Phainon immediately wrapped his arms around Mydei, almost knocking the breath out of his lungs and causing the man to stumble backwards.

“Yes! Yes! Mydei, of course I will!” Phainon, who was grinning from ear to ear and with his own tears brimming in his eyes, squeezed Mydei in his arms like his life depended on it. He was even holding back from jumping into Mydei's arms, but he was afraid of catching the man off guard and making them both crumple to the floor. Phainon opted to squeeze the life out of Mydei and nuzzle his face into golden hair instead.

Mydei smiled, half from relief and half from how adorably Phainon had reacted as the man continued to shove his face into Mydei. Although they had already talked about marriage, that conversation occurred a few months ago, and neither of the two men ever officially asked for the other man's hand in marriage. As the date of their return to Okhema quickly approached, Mydei had planned to officially ask for Phainon's hand in marriage with the ring that he had found, and took it to a shop in Kremnos to have the ring cleaned, polished, and fixed to be in pristine condition for when he presented it to Phainon again. He had been nervous ever since the debate ended, for he knew he was going to ask for Phainon's hand today. He was only thankful that Phainon did not notice his nervousness until they returned to their room.

“You're… really asking me to marry you?” Phainon had his forehead pressed against Mydei's shoulder as he clung to his red cape.

“Did you think I gave you the ring and asked you just as a joke?”

“No!” Phainon's head shot up, and his face flushed red at Mydei's narrowed eyes. “I just… I just feel like I'm… dreaming.”

Mydei scoffed, throwing his hands to Phainon's cheeks and pulling him in for a deep kiss. But before Phainon could react, Mydei had already pulled away.

“Does this still feel like a dream?” Mydei muttered against Phainon's lips, his eyes boring into his blue ones.

“Um… Yes…” Phainon's gaze darted left and right, unsure of where to look on Mydei’s beautiful face that was still close to his.

Rolling his eyes, Mydei muttered, “HKS,” before pressing yet another kiss onto Phainon once more.

Phainon groaned, his eyes fluttering shut and cheeks ablaze as he pulled Mydei's waist toward him, hungrily returning the kiss. He leaned his head toward Mydei, who equally reciprocated with the same fervor, and they parted breathlessly, their hot breaths fanning upon their lips as they panted for breath.

“Phainon.”

“Yes?”

“I love you, Phainon.”

“I love you too, Mydei.”
